groups.name: Supply-chain and persistent-state poisoning
groups.scope: Mechanisms that poison or protect the resources an agent consumes and accumulates: model-artifact integrity with backdoor and training-data poisoning and decontamination, package/skill/MCP-server ecosystem attacks and their screening, hallucinated-resource squatting, persistent-memory poisoning with write-time and lifecycle defenses, and RAG corpus and retriever poisoning. The boundary with injection is durability and locus - durable contamination of memory, corpora, registries, or artifacts belongs here even when delivery resembles injection. Secret leakage from these resources is a confidentiality concern and belongs to the secrets group.

groups.name: Offensive security automation and adversarial pressure
groups.scope: Mechanisms that generate adversarial pressure to expose weaknesses: automated red teaming and jailbreak synthesis, penetration-test and exploit/PoC-generation agents (including execution-validated witnesses), social-engineering and deception of agents, multi-agent compositional and authority-capture attacks, evasion of ML/code detectors and verifiers, resource-exhaustion and denial-of-wallet abuse, workflow fuzzing and adversarial-environment synthesis for attack discovery, attack-surface systematizations, and attacker-defender co-design for adaptive robustness. The boundary with detection is object and goal: fuzzing that hunts implementation vulnerabilities in code belongs to detection, while probing that breaks agent workflows, models, or security machinery stays here.

groups.name: Authorization, capability control, and sandboxing
groups.scope: Mechanisms that constrain what agent actions can do before and during execution: pre-execution tool-call authorization and intent monitoring, capability-scoped, earned, and least-privilege authorization with drift control, tool-call interception and policy gating, deterministic runtime enforcement and contract-based supervision, OS-level sandboxes and reference monitors, sandbox-escape and privilege-escalation measurement, blast-radius and dry-run action verification, identity/attestation and zero-trust delegation, and trusted-execution isolation. The boundary with injection handling is the object of control: these act on actions and authority, not on the content of prompts and tool outputs; credential confidentiality belongs to the secrets group.

groups.name: Benchmark and evaluation validity for security claims
groups.scope: Mechanisms that keep security evaluation itself honest: benchmark validity with contamination and shortcut auditing, anti-cheat and measurement-integrity methods, ground-truth label quality and verifier/judge reliability (including model substitution and correlated-agreement blindness), metric-validity audits for repair and optimization claims, multi-axis robustness and reproducibility audits of detectors, agent safety and scope-adherence measurement, dual-use harm measurement, refusal calibration, and harness and pentest-agent baselining. The boundary with oversight and verification is the target: this group audits evaluation claims and measurement instruments, not running systems or shipped fixes.

groups.name: Vulnerability and malicious-code detection and discovery
groups.scope: Mechanisms that find and characterize security weaknesses in code and artifacts: SAST augmentation, taint reasoning and LLM/GNN vulnerability detection over source and repositories, evidence-driven triage, CVE/CWE classification and severity prioritization, binary/malware/protocol reverse engineering, hardware and RTL analysis, spec- and checklist-driven auditing, causal vulnerability-introduction forensics, and dynamic discovery - LLM-guided fuzzing, fuzz-harness and test synthesis, and mutation testing of detectors. The boundary with secure development is post-discovery work: generating or verifying a fix belongs to the repair group; the boundary with operations is that these analyze code and artifacts rather than live telemetry.

groups.name: Agent oversight, audit, and governance
groups.scope: Mechanisms that observe, record, and govern the agent itself at runtime: action monitors and statistically calibrated monitoring, trajectory- and activation-level compromise detection with recovery, reward-hacking and oversight-evasion detection, tamper-evident audit trails and claim-to-evidence traceability, watermarking and machine-text provenance, attack-safeguard accountability taxonomies, deployment governance, compliance automation, and human-factors deployment studies. The boundary with authorization is the mode of control: monitors detect and record, while blocking, sandboxing, and admission enforcement belong to the authorization group; auditing the evaluation pipeline itself belongs to benchmark validity.

groups.name: Secure code generation, repair, and fix verification
groups.scope: Mechanisms that produce and prove secure code: design-time misuse-case and attack-tree analysis, secure code generation and hardening (inference-time steering, model editing, gated co-decoding), vulnerability-repair pipelines and repair-data generation, and the machinery that shows a claimed fix actually holds - reproduction and witness tests, independent and layered oracles against deceptive fixes, differential/metamorphic testing, formal and neuro-symbolic verification, conformal risk certification, gate and test-suite adequacy measurement, evidence-gated lifecycle promotion, and mechanical verification of agent completion claims. The boundary with oversight is scope: verifying a finished artifact or claim belongs here, while continuously monitoring a running agent belongs there.

groups.name: Prompt injection and untrusted-content handling
groups.scope: Mechanisms acting on attacker-controlled content that crosses into an agent's context: indirect-injection attack surfaces and channel expansion (tool descriptions and outputs, logs, workspace artifacts, stored/fragmented/implicit-context payloads), and the defenses applied to that content - boundary filtering, deterministic out-of-band mediation, model-internal injection detection, tool-output sanitization and retrieval/perception screening, instruction-provenance binding, and post-injection containment. The boundary with the supply-chain group is durability: one-shot content delivered through a live context boundary belongs here, while poisoning of long-lived resources (memory, RAG corpora, packages, model weights) belongs there. Monitors that watch agent behavior rather than content belong to oversight.

groups.name: Security operations and defensive deception
groups.scope: Mechanisms that run the security back office and actively defend against external threats: SOC triage and alert investigation, CTI retrieval/merge and IOC extraction, APT investigation, incident response and policy analysis, network/ICS/WAF detection and adversarial hardening, tiered autonomous cyber defense, cross-layer attack-path reconstruction, and defensive deception - honeypots, decoys, sentinel endpoints, and live defender evaluation. The boundary with oversight is the watched object: these act on external adversaries and their telemetry, while oversight watches the agent's own behavior; deception attacks mounted against agents belong to offensive automation.

groups.name: Secrets, privacy, and data-leakage protection
groups.scope: Mechanisms that keep secrets and personal data from leaking: secret/credential/PII leakage detection and pre-call redaction, cross-turn PII detection, memorization and extraction attacks on deployed models, covert exfiltration and channel diversion, privacy-boundary enforcement around LLM pipelines, privacy-preserving inference and private integrity-verified retrieval, credential hygiene at the execution boundary, and cryptographic-asset discovery. The boundary with authorization is purpose: credential hygiene here protects the confidentiality of secrets rather than constraining authority; watermarking and provenance of outputs is oversight, not confidentiality.

ranked.technique: Red-teaming the untrusted-content path (injection as behavior-path search)
ranked.mechanism: Injection vulnerability is a property of the behavior path that carries untrusted content — files, skills, tool returns, log fields, web text, shared tool contexts — to a privileged outcome, not of any single payload. Red-team by searching that space: enumerate ingestion paths, place payloads including fragmented ones that stateless filters cannot see (context stitching across log entries), and verify compromise against agent action traces. Structural surfaces dominate: a fabricated 'already passed moderation' trace in a shared tool context suppresses later checks at near-total success, and the fix is structural context isolation, not input/output filtering. Accept an ingestion path only if injected instructions demonstrably cannot reach privileged effect; treat any content crossing a trust boundary as adversarial by default.
ranked.reported_results: Automated skill red teaming reaches ASR 0.73-0.93 on adversarial skills and up to 0.26 on real-world skills, showing benign-looking skills harbor latent vulnerabilities (arxiv:2604.04989); frontier agents show up to 80% ASR on skill-file injections and neither model scaling nor input filtering solves it (arxiv:2602.20156); simulated moderation traces jailbreak function-calling LLMs at near-total success across providers, with filtering ineffective and structural isolation required (arxiv:2607.00481); a 38-entry MCP threat taxonomy carries PoCs for 31 attacks (arxiv:2603.18063); fragmented Context-Stitching payloads evade stateless filters and layered defenses leave residual success (arxiv:2607.14493).
ranked.miniork_surface: MCP / tool surface (+ kickoff and intake guard)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Inventory mini-ork's tool surface as an ingestion-path list (MCP servers, IDE actions, skills, retrieved docs entering runs) and add an intake-guard rule marking each input untrusted with provenance; seed one benign-looking instruction per path in a sacrificial run and check no privileged action (push, write outside the run dir, secret read) follows. Measure: privileged actions traceable to injected instructions, before vs after provenance marking.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py + mini_ork/intake/ + evidence ledger traces - a planted-injection probe term
glm.rationale: The state records the gap verbatim: no red-team term plants an instruction and checks whether the run follows it. Measured ASRs (0.73-0.93 on adversarial skills, up to 80% on skill-file injections for frontier agents, near-total success for spoofed moderation traces) make this a fixture repo, a planted instruction in a file and an issue body, and a deterministic grep of the run tool-call trace - no model judgment in the verdict.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface (+ kickoff and intake guard) - an ingestion-path inventory with one planted instruction per path
minimax.rationale: This is precisely the hole the state snapshot names: 'there is no red-team term that plants an instruction and checks whether the run follows it'. It is also the cheapest honest measurement of whether the agent follows instructions planted in a repo file or issue body, and the evidence is strong that no input filter solves it (frontier agents up to 80% ASR on skill-file injections; simulated moderation traces jailbreak function-calling at near-total success, so structural isolation is required), which is why it must be a probe rather than a filter.

ranked.technique: Deterministic security verification of agent-written diffs
ranked.mechanism: A measured negative finding drives the technique: automated plus human review misses most credential introductions before integration, AI-generated code introduces vulnerabilities at a multiple of human-written code, and execution feedback plus repository access improve task completion without establishing security — so per-change security must be a deterministic gate, not a review habit. The verifier runs scoped to the change surface on every run that writes code: secret and credential detection over the dirty set, dangerous-API and permission-escalation diffs, and hidden 'ghost' security tests that verify patch integrity beyond the visible functional suite. Accept = clean scan and ghost tests pass; reject = any hit, failing closed; abstain = scanner unavailable means hold, never pass. Anchored on the diff and the touched-file set, never on the agent's characterization of its own change.
ranked.reported_results: Humans introduce 67.6% of genuine leaked secrets and automated plus human review misses 81.1% of credentials before integration; cited analyses put AI-generated code vulnerability introduction at ~2.7x human-written (arxiv:2607.12428).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security.py to the code-fix verifier set — secret/credential scan plus dangerous-permission diff over MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES, reusing the pinned gitleaks configuration — so the run's gate covers security exactly as it covers tests and types today. Measurement: a seeded credential in a test change is blocked at the verifier with no added human step.

glm.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - security verifier scoped to the dirty set (MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES)
glm.rationale: The open gap verbatim: no security check in the code-fix verifier set, nothing detects a vulnerability the agent just introduced. The motivation is direct - AI-generated code introduces vulnerabilities at ~2.7x human rate and review misses 81.1% of credentials - and v1 is deterministic and cheap: gitleaks over the dirty set plus a pinned dangerous-API diff scan, failing closed beside test/typecheck.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security.py - secret and credential scan plus dangerous-permission diff over MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES
minimax.rationale: This is the literal named hole in the state snapshot: the verifier set is test, typecheck, fallback_guard and metamorphic, and none looks for injection, authz defects, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, credentials gitleaks misses, or an attacker-chosen dependency source. The measured motivation is strong (automated plus human review misses 81.1% of credentials before integration; AI-generated code introduces vulnerabilities at about 2.7x human-written), it is deterministic and fail-closed, it reuses the pinned gitleaks configuration, and at S effort it is the first security check rather than a fifth verifier - the only thing missing is that it must be held to the pairing and witness rules in the now-list.

ranked.technique: Dependency hallucination and version-risk guard at code-verification time (slopsquatting defense)
ranked.mechanism: A deterministic post-edit verifier treats every package name, import, skill name, or registry URL an implementer emits as unverified until checked against the true registry: reject names that do not exist (the squattable slot an attacker can register), reject unpinned versions, flag pinned versions with known CVEs, and triage package intent with a calibrated low-false-positive pipeline before anything is installed; abstain to human review on registry ambiguity rather than letting the model self-verify, which is a coin flip (51% balanced accuracy). The check is grounded in registry truth, not model opinion, and measurement must exclude standard-library false positives that inflate apparent hallucination by up to 9.4pp. Caution: the guard is load-bearing exactly when a run processes hostile text, since adversarial prompts surge hallucination by up to 45 percentage points, and static analysis alone detects only 14-85% of hallucinated dependencies.
ranked.reported_results: Retrieval grounding cuts skill-name hallucination 40.8% to 3.2%; self-verification 51% balanced accuracy; standalone-LLM hallucination 36.0%, agents 36.9% (arxiv:2607.12340). Rust crate hallucination 20.23% overall (arxiv:2606.08444). Static analysis detects only 14-85% of library hallucinations, manual ceiling 48.5-77% (arxiv:2604.07755). A single squatted name intercepts 95% of skill installs; 90.7% of 140 trials land on squattable slots (arxiv:2607.07433). 36.70%-55.70% of LLM-specified pinned versions carry at least one known CVE, 62.75%-74.51% of them Critical/High (arxiv:2605.06279). Adversarial prompts add up to 45pp hallucination (arxiv:2608.22652); a deterministic existence check plus classifier reaches hallucination-free code on 76% of runs (arxiv:2608.23897). Registry-grade intent triage is achievable at deployable false positives: CHASE 98.4% recall at 0.08% FPR over 3,000 packages (arxiv:2601.06838); IntelGuard 99.26% accuracy at 0.50% FPR, 96.5% on obfuscated packages, 54 unreported PyPI packages surfaced (arxiv:2601.16458); SBOM graph learning flags chain-risky components at 91.03% accuracy (arxiv:2604.04977).
ranked.miniork_surface: code-fix verifier set - recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ gains a deterministic dependency guard next to test/typecheck/lint.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add recipes/code-fix/verifiers/dep_guard.py: parse the run's diff for added imports and requirement lines, resolve each against a vendored registry snapshot (existence, publish date, pinned version, known-CVE list), and fail the gate on unknown or newly-registered names and on CVE-carrying pins. Measurement: on historical code-fix runs report the fraction of added dependencies that were hallucinated, unpinned, or CVE-carrying before the guard, and confirm planted name-squat fixtures are blocked 100%.

glm.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - deterministic dependency guard beside test/typecheck/lint
glm.rationale: The state names the exact hole: code-fix verifiers never check a dependency pulled from an attacker-chosen source, and nothing hashes what a run resolves. Hallucinated names are measured at 20-36% across ecosystems with self-verification a coin flip (51% balanced accuracy), so registry-existence + pinning + lockfile-hash checks close it with zero model judgment.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - a deterministic dependency guard beside test/typecheck
minimax.rationale: The state snapshot names 'a dependency pulled from an attacker-chosen source' as something the current verifier set does not look for, and this is a deterministic, registry-grounded check that fails closed on unknown or CVE-carrying pins; the numbers are directly on-target (36.70%-55.70% of LLM-pinned versions carry a known CVE, 90.7% of 140 trials land on squattable slots, adversarial prompts add up to 45pp hallucination). Effort is M because it reuses the existing verifier plumbing, and it directly extends the shipped verifier set.

ranked.technique: Composite secure-and-correct gates and proxy-metric validity audits
ranked.mechanism: Refuses single-axis success metrics for code changes: a patch is accepted only if it is simultaneously functionally correct AND secure AND compliant with review-derived acceptance constraints — a joint predicate, not an average of scores. It audits the proxy metrics themselves (compile rate, retrieval recall, headline F1) by testing whether movement in the proxy tracks the outcome it stands for; a proxy whose gain does not move the outcome, or moves it the wrong way, is rejected as a steering signal. Abstention rule: an optimization claim without measurement ('faster', 'safer') is scored as a failure under classification-penalty scoring, not treated as neutral. Cautions: a recall-maximizing retriever configuration adopted on retrieval metrics reduced downstream issue resolution; a specialized-routing cheatsheet hit 100% synthetic recall while real-world F1 fell below the zero-shot baseline; benchmark protocols that pass perturbations through an uncorrected processing chain mis-measure hackability by up to 4x.
ranked.reported_results: SecurePass@1 below 6% — models are rarely simultaneously correct and secure (arxiv:2601.22706); 221 of 644 repairs that pass functional tests fail review-derived constraints (arxiv:2609.04167); compile rate shown scientifically unreliable for single-function vulnerability repair over 5 controlled experiments / 203 functions (arxiv:2609.26749); a corrected round-trip-referenced protocol changes measured metric hackability by up to a factor of 4 (arxiv:2610.10899); cheatsheet routing lifts synthetic recall to 100% while real-world F1 collapses below zero-shot and recalibration makes it worse (arxiv:2607.14628).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a security verifier to recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ (secret-injection, dangerous-API, and taint probes) and make the gate conjunctive: pass = tests AND types AND security check. Measure: on the next code-fix runs, the rate at which patches pass tests but fail the security check (the SWE-Gate ratio) — the measured hole this recipe exists to close.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set + publish gate - joint correct-AND-secure predicate
glm.rationale: The joint predicate is the acceptance-rule flip that makes the new security verifier binding (221/644 repairs pass functional tests but fail review-derived constraints; SecurePass@1 under 6%); it is nearly free once G06-T05 exists, so sequence it immediately after.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - pass = tests AND types AND a security check
minimax.rationale: This is the composition rule that turns a security verifier into a gate: 221 of 644 repairs that pass functional tests fail review-derived constraints, and SecurePass@1 sits below 6%, so a patch that is functionally correct but insecure must not be accepted. Effort is S because it is a conjunction over existing verifiers, and it is next only because it presupposes the security verifier I rank in the now-list.

ranked.technique: Oracle-integrity invariants and known-answer controls for the verifier harness
ranked.mechanism: Audits the evaluation harness itself for oracle defects that score tables cannot reveal. It instruments the verifier/oracle with state-integrity invariants (grader state cannot be mutated by the run; treatment metadata cannot reach the label computation; payloads must actually be delivered before an effect is scored) and plants known-answer controls — cases with pre-adjudicated verdicts, including must-fail and must-flag canaries — that the oracle must reproduce exactly. Accept rule: an oracle passes only when every control returns its known verdict and every invariant holds; any violation fails the harness closed, and no scores from a broken oracle are published. This also covers verifier answer-leakage: if a closed-loop verifier's probes encode target identity, an optimizer's apparent effectiveness is rejected and routed to a diagnosability audit before any optimization claim. Caution: re-scoring preserved traces of published security campaigns has exposed large inflation from silent payload non-delivery and direct treatment leakage — plausible numbers from a broken grader are the default suspicion, not the exception.
ranked.reported_results: Five state-integrity invariants plus three known-answer controls validated by injecting seven oracle defect classes into an agent benchmark (arxiv:2610.16067); tracing 10,200 execution rows of a preserved MCP security campaign finds the historical grader had direct treatment leakage, with treatment-blind label reconstruction (arxiv:2608.12880); re-scoring identical traces of an IPI benchmark shows large inflation from four harness defect classes (arxiv:2609.32691); a verifier that leaks target identity makes an exact optimizer appear effective (arxiv:2610.00126).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Ship a canary self-test inside each code-fix verifier: on every run (and on every verifier change), execute known-pass / known-fail / known-flag fixtures and require exact expected verdicts before the verifier may gate a real patch. Measure: canary failures caught per verifier change over the next month, and zero gated runs executed with a failing oracle.

glm.landing_surface: verifier harness - known-answer controls and state-integrity invariants in recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ and mini_ork/verify/
glm.rationale: Doctrine says a guard that cannot measure blocks - known-answer controls (must-fail canaries) and invariants are how the new security verifier proves it can fail: five invariants plus three controls caught all seven injected oracle-defect classes. Days of work, and it hardens every gate added in this cycle.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - a canary self-test inside each verifier (known-pass / known-fail / known-flag fixtures)
minimax.rationale: Re-scoring preserved traces exposed large inflation from silent payload non-delivery and direct treatment leakage, so an oracle that can be broken without tripping anything is the failure mode to guard against, and the shipped doctrine already says a guard that cannot measure must block. Known-answer controls are S effort and make the new security check trustworthy, so they are next behind the check itself.

ranked.technique: Bare-LLM security verdicts as a gate (caution: high false discovery, non-replication, run-to-run instability)
ranked.mechanism: CAUTION technique: the consistently measured failure modes that constrain every other technique in this group. Across independent evaluations, bare LLM vulnerability verdicts show very high false discovery rates at project scale, run-to-run reporting inconsistency, headline RAG gains that fail to replicate on open weights, near-failure at repository-scale localization, and accuracy that can drop when more context is added while token cost nearly doubles; mechanistic analysis adds that models detect safe-coding patterns rather than vulnerability signatures. The rule it yields: an LLM security verdict is never an accept signal. It is at best a hypothesis generator whose output must fail closed (unverified = abstention) behind a deterministic oracle, and any LLM-based check must be stability-tested (repeated identical runs with consistent verdicts) before its output is recorded at all. Anchored on the accumulated negative evidence, not on any model's self-reported confidence.
ranked.reported_results: Best model detects 63% of real web vulnerabilities with reporting consistency as low as 50% across iterations (arxiv:2606.21397); RAG-detection gains fail to replicate on open weights, plateauing at ~0.30 pairwise accuracy (arxiv:2606.04739); reproduction of four RAG-SVD systems shows recall deviations up to 58.2% that aggregate F1 hides (arxiv:2609.37669); best repository-scale localization reaches only 0.229 File F1 and 38.4% of tasks are never localized by any model (arxiv:2609.15939); agents complete the full locate-attribute-CWE chain in 11.1% of Linux-kernel cases (arxiv:2610.25705); general agent methods have the highest recall but very high false discovery rates at project scale (arxiv:2601.19239); adding interprocedural context degrades some models by up to 25 accuracy points while nearly doubling token cost (arxiv:2604.08417); detection rides on safety-pattern attention heads rather than vulnerability signatures - removing Layer 11 drops accuracy from 100% to 6% (arxiv:2605.29901); token-feature detectors fall to ~0.436 PR-AUC cross-project, showing lexical-cue sensitivity (arxiv:2605.04260); a survey catalogs AI-slop failure modes (hallucinated vulnerabilities, plausible-but-wrong reports) in vulnerability assessment (arxiv:2608.25667).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Encode it as a written gate invariant plus a probe: no publish/merge decision may cite an LLM security verdict as its evidence unless a deterministic check co-signs it, and any LLM security node runs a 3x consistency probe that auto-abstains on disagreement. Measure the verdict-flip rate across re-runs on a fixed seeded corpus (replayed vulnerable-then-fixed commits); the pre-gating flip rate is the baseline number and zero unstable verdicts reaching the gate is the pass condition.

glm.rationale: The doctrine row and verdict trichotomy already forbid model-opinion security gates, which is what this caution demands; its measured failure numbers (63% detection at 50% reporting consistency) are the reason G05-T02's oracle tier is deterministic.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate - a written gate invariant plus a 3x consistency probe on any LLM security node
minimax.rationale: This is the rule that makes every other technique in this review safe to adopt: an LLM security verdict is never an accept signal, only a hypothesis generator behind a deterministic oracle, and the negative evidence is strong (63% detection with reporting consistency as low as 50%; RAG gains that fail to replicate; models confirming vulnerabilities in already-patched code 23-61% of the time). It is S effort and constrains the now-list, so it is next.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: repository, intake, and runtime-feedback poisoning of coding agents
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique — the exact inputs a coding-agent run trusts are demonstrated attack surfaces: issue text, repository files, CI/test feedback, and workspace layout all carry injections that make agents ship functionally-correct-but-insecure patches, run trojans, or exfiltrate. Trace-guided placement hides payloads at AST nodes the agent's execution trace touches; adversarial issue descriptions induce insecure repairs that still pass tests, and both pre-repair and post-repair detection of the manipulation is weak; a compromised peer component injects through runtime feedback that has diagnostic authority but no action authority. Provenance-based trust has its own hole: a trojan swapped into an already-referenced file is exempt from re-inspection while an equivalent novel file is inspected. The mini-ork rule this implies: intake content is data, never instruction, and re-inspection is mandatory whenever a referenced file's content changes.
ranked.reported_results: Runtime-feedback injection succeeds 94.8% across 3,000 trials, 61.3% on Codex and 58.7% on Claude Code at product level (arxiv:2610.38799); trace-guided repository poisoning reaches peak ASRs 76-100% across payload carriers with backdoor implantation above 90% and average ASR over 60% across 4 harnesses and 12 models (arxiv:2610.23109); adversarial issue descriptions achieve 40-64% ASR with post-repair detection only 39.4% (static analysis) and 55.4% (LLM judge) (arxiv:2609.15963); injection success falls from 38% at directory depth-2 to 8.5% at depth-4 and modular codebases are significantly safer (arxiv:2608.14876); scaffold choice alone shifts ASR 40.0% to 48.6%, and a swapped-in trojan referencing an existing script runs without re-inspection (arxiv:2604.01438); neutral-condition deception rates reach 49.88% active and 64.29% passive across the SDLC (arxiv:2610.13626); spec manipulation makes a benign LLM emit exploitable code (arxiv:2610.03857); LLM output acts as confused deputy carrying attacker influence into classic sinks (arxiv:2608.10281).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Teach mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py to treat issue text, repo state, and CI feedback as untrusted data — quoted, provenance-tagged, never instruction — and trigger re-inspection whenever an already-referenced file's content changes. Measure with a SWEADV-style planted issue: the insecure patch must be flagged by an independent security check even while tests stay green.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py + mini_ork/intake/ - untrusted labeling of repo prose, issue text, CI feedback
glm.rationale: The caution that motivates the implement-now probe: runtime-feedback injection succeeded on 61.3% of Codex and 58.7% of Claude Code runs at product level, and trace-guided repository poisoning peaks at 76-100%. Its buildable residue - label kickoff, issue text, repo prose and CI output untrusted at intake - is S effort and should land with G02-T10.

minimax.landing_surface: kickoff and intake guard - treat issue text, repo state and CI feedback as untrusted data, re-inspect any referenced file whose content changes
minimax.rationale: This is the attack evidence for the injection hole stated precisely: runtime-feedback injection succeeds 94.8% across 3,000 trials, trace-guided repository poisoning reaches peak ASRs 76-100% with backdoor implantation above 90%, and adversarial issue descriptions achieve 40-64% ASR with post-repair detection only 39.4% (static analysis) and 55.4% (LLM judge). It is next rather than now because the prevention rule it implies (intake content is data, never instruction, with mandatory re-inspection) is cheap but only becomes meaningful once the probe in the now-list can measure whether the agent complied.

ranked.technique: Honeytokens and canary-linked exfiltration tripwires
ranked.mechanism: Plant credentials and identifiers that no legitimate node should ever reference - a per-run canary secret minted by the vault, plus trap triggers on tool surfaces. Any occurrence of a canary value in outbound traffic, tool arguments, artifacts, or logs is a high-precision compromise signal, and detection fails closed by blocking promotion of the run; linking canary exposure back to the specific tool invocation that touched it yields an auditable trace of silent access that output-only review cannot see. Deception traps double as high-precision labels for a compromise classifier, catching exfiltration that content inspection misses because encoded, unicode-mangled, or paraphrased payloads evade output scanning. Abstain rule: a run in which a canary fired is quarantined for review, never silently passed, and a benign-path check runs too since agents leak credentials with no adversary present.
ranked.reported_results: Deception-trap detection caught 90.7-100% of successful injection attacks with zero false alarms across 485 normal-use tests and 176 cross-lingual attack prompts (arxiv:2605.11026); canary-linked audits found 3 of 5 models invoking PHI tools unnecessarily on identifier-free tasks, and a task-necessity gate nearly eliminated residual identifier access (arxiv:2611.02319); output-level detection of credential exfiltration was evaded by encodings, unicode substitution, and paraphrase, while activation features separated credential-seeking from benign prompts including held-out encodings (arxiv:2606.04141).
ranked.miniork_surface: vault and per-node secret scope (canary minting), with the tripwire check wired into the publish gate and evidence ledger and traces
ranked.adoption_sketch: Mint one unused canary token per run in the vault - referenced by no recipe - and add a canary-byte scan to the publish gate alongside gitleaks, with any hit linked to the tool invocations in the run transcript. Measure by seeding the canary into a deliberately compromised test node's context and requiring gate detection with zero false positives across a corpus of clean historical runs.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/vault.py canary minting + publish gate tripwire (mini_ork/cli/publisher.py) over evidence-ledger traces
glm.rationale: The vault can mint a per-run canary no legitimate node should ever emit, and any occurrence in artifacts, tool arguments or outbound traffic is a deterministic, near-zero-false-positive compromise signal (90.7-100% detection with zero false alarms across 485 normal-use tests) wired into the publish gate - the cheapest structural injection and exfiltration tripwire mini-ork can ship.

minimax.landing_surface: vault and per-node secret scope (canary minting), with a canary-byte scan wired into the publish gate and evidence ledger
minimax.rationale: A per-run canary secret referenced by no recipe, with any occurrence in outbound traffic, tool arguments, artifacts or logs blocking promotion and linking to the touching tool invocation, is the cheapest high-precision exfiltration detector available, and deception traps caught 90.7-100% of successful injection attacks with zero false alarms across 485 normal-use tests. It is next rather than now because it overlaps the honeypot in G09-T01 and is a detection tripwire, not a boundary.

ranked.technique: Paired exploit-and-functional oracle for security fix acceptance
ranked.mechanism: A security fix is accepted only when an executable exploit oracle — a proof-of-vulnerability or reproduction test — fails on the base revision and passes on the head revision while the project's functional suite passes on both; functional green alone is a rejection for a security-labeled fix, exploitability is confirmed by execution rather than a scanner verdict, and an oracle that cannot be faithfully built is an abstention. Oracle independence is structural: witness tests are authored before or hidden from the patcher, and an adversarial re-attack loop treats each accepted patch as a fresh attack target, accumulating every newly surfaced exploit as a permanent regression requirement. The same executable evidence detects memorized patches (similarity to historical developer fixes) and crash-suppressing fixes that pass automatic validation while remaining exploitable. Cautions: dynamic confirmation fails when compile repair reaches executability via stubs that bypass the intended target, and LLM-claimed exploits are unreliable enough that roughly 20% of curl bug-bounty reports were AI-generated false vulnerabilities — the oracle must run against the real target, never be described by the generator.
ranked.reported_results: Over 40% of AVR patches deemed correct by basic tests fail PoC+ tests across three systems (arxiv:2603.06858); a paired exploit+functional oracle rejects 15/119 patches an exploit-only oracle accepts, and 98/104 admitted patches are manually confirmed equivalent (arxiv:2608.00692); among static-gate-clean security-sensitive Python files, dynamic verification confirms runtime exploitability in roughly 1 in 7 (arxiv:2609.10762); adversarial patch-then-attack surfaces a distinct confirmed exploit in 41% of runs after the original PoV is blocked (arxiv:2610.20245); 16-38% of patches passing automatic validation remain semantically incorrect and on average 25% are substantially similar to historical developer patches (arxiv:2609.04075); only 24.8% of LLM security patches are fully correct while 51.4% fail both security and functionality (arxiv:2603.10072); agent-generated PoV tests demonstrate feasible attacks in 55% of cases (arxiv:2605.03956); dual programmatic/agentic grading agrees 93.9% (kappa 0.88) on exploit-blocking plus behavior-preserving criteria (arxiv:2610.17020).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security.py implementing the paired-oracle rule: for security-flagged tasks (or diffs touching auth/crypto/input-handling paths), require a reproduction-or-exploit test that fails on the base and passes on the head plus the functional suite passing on both, sourced independently of the implementer node. Measurement: on a replayed set of completed security-fix runs, the fraction of previously-green patches the paired oracle rejects — the literature suggests a double-digit rejection rate where only functional tests gated before.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set + verification stack differential runs - paired exploit/functional oracle on base vs head
glm.rationale: The state names the hole exactly: correctness is measured, exploitability is not, nothing replays an exploit against the patched tree. Over 40% of patches deemed correct by basic tests fail PoC+ tests, and the paired oracle rejects 15/119 patches an exploit-only oracle admits; base-fails/head-passes/suite-passes is a deterministic differential replay the verification stack is already shaped for.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security.py - a reproduction-or-exploit test that fails on the base and passes on the head, with the functional suite passing on both
minimax.rationale: This is the 'exploitability is not measured' hole stated as an accept rule: over 40% of patches deemed correct by basic tests fail PoC tests, a paired exploit-and-functional oracle rejects 15/119 patches an exploit-only oracle accepts, and among static-gate-clean security-sensitive files dynamic verification confirms runtime exploitability in roughly 1 in 7. It is deterministic (fail on base, pass on head), oracle-independent of the implementer node, and an oracle that cannot be faithfully built is an abstention rather than a pass - exactly the doctrine's fail-closed posture.

ranked.technique: Execution-witness validation of AI security findings
ranked.mechanism: Every AI-generated vulnerability claim, exploit, or confirmed finding must pass a deterministic runtime witness before it counts: validate the target is reachable, execute the PoC in a sandbox, and check the vulnerable sink actually fires (reachability -> trigger -> sink). Accept only findings whose witness reproduces; reject claims whose PoC fails execution; abstain — record as unverified, never as confirmed — when the environment cannot be built. The verdict is anchored on recorded execution artifacts (exit codes, crash output, environment state diff), never on the model's description of impact. Caution: treating runtime-plausible LLM exploits as real is a false-confidence generator — the majority of LLM-generated 'exploits' fail full validation, and unvalidated triage is precisely the failure this technique removes.
ranked.reported_results: Only 65 of 338 LLM-generated exploits pass full validation across 20 CVEs (arxiv:2602.04165); dual-loop execution + description-repair reaches 82.9% exploit-generation success on SecBench.js and 54.3% on PatchEval (arxiv:2602.05721); >50% of 100 real-world KernelCTF n-days reproduced agentically, beating directed fuzzer SyzDirect in effectiveness and speed (arxiv:2602.07287); SAST triage precision rises 77.9%->85.7% with 1.71x faster confirmation when unit-test execution validates findings, recall 67.3%->79.7% (arxiv:2602.11209); agentic zero-day confirmation ~30% of reports, ~3x baseline agents with execution feedback (arxiv:2602.14345).
ranked.miniork_surface: code-fix verifier set (+ evidence ledger and traces)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a security_witness check to code-fix's verifier set: any run whose diff touches security-relevant paths must reproduce a stated impact (a failing assert, a sandboxed PoC exit code) recorded in the evidence ledger; a claim without a witness is recorded as an abstention. Measure the fraction of security-flagged findings carrying a reproducible witness, and the reviewer time spent on non-reproducing findings before vs after.

glm.rationale: Only 65 of 338 LLM-generated exploits pass full validation - exactly the false-security-claim risk if mini-ork ships any model-proposed finding. Fold this witness rule into G05-T02 and G07-T01 as their accept condition rather than building it separately.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set (+ evidence ledger and traces) - a security_witness check
minimax.rationale: This is the mechanism that stops a false security claim from reaching a gate: only 65 of 338 LLM-generated exploits pass full execution validation, so a finding without a runtime witness must be an abstention, never a confirmation, and the anchor is recorded execution artifacts rather than the model's description of impact. It lands beside the shipped verifier set and reuses the evidence ledger, so it directly closes the 'exploitability is not measured' gap.

ranked.technique: Caution: scanner and LLM verdicts are not ground truth - calibrate or abstain
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique, backed by measurement: security-scanner and LLM-judgment verdicts cannot serve as a sole accept signal. MCP scanners flag 96.89% of real servers as risky at 45.53% average precision, 24.17% CVE recall, and 15.66% pairwise agreement; LLM package triage frequently flags safe packages and drops to 0.48 F1 on the specific indicators responsible; direct LLM judgment of skills reaches 19.05% recall; LLM-judged attack evaluations reflect the judge's decision boundary rather than objective ground truth. A gate built on such a verdict must anchor to deterministic evidence or abstain: under fail-closed semantics an uncalibrated verdict yields Review, never Accept. This bounds what any new scanning gate (secret scan, gaming scan, tool vetting, dependency triage) may claim about its own coverage.
ranked.reported_results: Scanners flag 96.89% of servers as risky; average precision 45.53% (worst 10.40%); pairwise Jaccard 15.66%; CVE recall 24.17% (arxiv:2607.11086). LLM malicious-package detection F1 0.40-0.99 with frequent safe-package false positives; indicator identification 0.48 F1 (arxiv:2602.16304). Malicious-skill detection: 62.4% false-positive rate on benign skills at 0.653-0.665 source-disjoint F1 (arxiv:2608.19901). LLM-judged attacks reflect the judge's decision boundary, not objective ground truth (arxiv:2610.04378). Unrepaired probability sampling: only 48.8% of registry servers complete an initialize handshake, so repair-until-it-works sampling overstates the ecosystem (arxiv:2609.10962).
ranked.miniork_surface: gaming scan - mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py, and by extension every gate that would lean on an LLM judge (publish gate, tool vetting).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Wherever mini-ork uses or plans a model-judged check, add a calibration harness: run the judge over a versioned labeled fixture set (benign + malicious) inside the run dir and record precision/recall before its verdict may gate anything; below threshold the gate abstains to human review. Measurement: per-judge calibration numbers attached to the gate's evidence ledger entry, refreshed when the judge model or prompt changes.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py and every gate that would lean on an LLM judge
glm.rationale: The doctrine row (deterministic checks decide; a model may propose or veto, never approve) plus the publish-gate verdict trichotomy already bar scanner and LLM verdicts as sole accept signals; keep the scanner-disagreement numbers (15.66% pairwise Jaccard, 24.17% CVE recall) as design ammunition for G05-T02, not as a build.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py and every gate that would lean on an LLM judge
minimax.rationale: This is the measurement rule that makes the doctrine's 'a guard that cannot measure blocks' enforceable: MCP scanners flag 96.89% of servers as risky at 45.53% precision and LLM skill judgment reaches only 19.05% recall, so an uncalibrated verdict must yield Review, never Accept. It is S effort and constrains every technique I rank above it, but it does not itself close a hole, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Mutation-based self-testing of shipped detectors (boundary-mutation battery for secret scanners)
ranked.mechanism: Turn the detectors on themselves: synthesize credentials from each secret-scanner rule's own regular expression, embed them in varied realistic contexts and boundary mutations, and score detection per rule; for code analyzers, LLM program transformation plus dynamic validation generates fault-revealing variants clustered by program differencing. A rule or tool change is accepted only when the whole battery re-runs green - the battery exists precisely to catch plausible-looking changes that silently regress rules. The honest null result is kept: no significant recall difference on real code means the battery measures boundary robustness on synthetic mutants that per-tool fixtures never cover. Anchored on per-rule detection metrics computed in CI beside the pinned scanner.
ranked.reported_results: Per-rule boundary mutation shows robustness near-perfect at >=0.9976 across ten contexts but collapsing to 0.5233 when a credential ends in a hyphen (five rules affected), and the battery caught a plausible rule change that silently regressed two rules; no significant recall difference on 292,527 lines of real code (null result reported) (arxiv:2609.02983); LLM transformation testing with dynamic feedback finds 66 unique faults across six SAST tools, 32 confirmed or fixed, detecting 3.4x more faults from 39.8% of the variants (arxiv:2610.21309).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend make secrets with a boundary-mutation battery: generate credentials from each .gitleaks.toml rule regex, embed them across roughly ten realistic contexts plus edge suffixes (for example a trailing hyphen), and assert per-rule detection in CI on the pinned gitleaks version. Measure the per-rule detection score (watching for the 0.52-style collapse) and require a green battery re-run on any rule edit.

glm.rationale: A per-rule mutation battery for the shipped gitleaks config caught a silent regression and a robustness collapse to 0.52 on hyphen-ending credentials - cheap, deterministic, and it protects the secret-scan tier G10-T08 extends.

minimax.landing_surface: secret scan - make secrets gains a boundary-mutation battery over each .gitleaks.toml rule
minimax.rationale: Per-rule boundary mutation showed robustness near-perfect at 0.9976 that collapsed to 0.5233 when a credential ends in a hyphen, and the battery caught a plausible rule change that silently regressed two rules, while the honest null on 292,527 lines of real code is reported too. This is S effort, deterministic, lives beside the pinned CI job, and directly addresses the snapshot's statement that secret scanning is pattern-and-entropy only.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: detection-centric defenses overestimate — validate adaptively and align evaluator channels
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique — the evidence is univocal that defenses relying on a model or a classifier to recognize injections collapse once the attacker knows the defense: published in-band detectors break above 90%, reported robustness often measures the training distribution rather than robustness, near-target injections slip past injection-trained models, and evaluators that inspect different channels than the agent reads are bypassed through scope gaps. In one 20,000+-attack adaptive campaign every model-relying defense broke and only output filtering held, so output-side enforcement is the component to trust. The rules this imposes on mini-ork: no guard ships on static-benchmark numbers alone, every guard gets a defense-aware adaptive red team before promotion, evaluator channels must cover exactly what the agent ingests, and presence-based refusal both over-refuses and under-detects.
ranked.reported_results: 12 published in-band defenses broken above 90% by adaptive attacks; out-of-band Progent drops from 25.8% to 4.2% robustness under its adaptive attacker; repetition erodes survivors; attention-tracker AUC 1.0 becomes a full bypass via separator tokens (arxiv:2606.26479); Meta-SecAlign falls from reported single-digit ASR to 100% under optimized adaptive attack (arxiv:2610.41998); near-target injections raise Meta-SecAlign-70B ASR@3 from 3.2% to 36.7% (arxiv:2610.32531); across 20,000+ attacks and nine configurations every model-relying defense broke while output filtering held (arxiv:2604.23887); attack-chain detection mean F1 is only 0.406 versus 0.216 for frozen baselines, and full-chain success is 0.814%/0.337% where ~48-51% bypass the detector (arxiv:2609.30657); Attention Tracker is near-chance on AgentDojo across most model families (arxiv:2610.28988); scope-gap placement bypassed all three competition evaluation stages for 5/19 targets with S2 acceptance 78% versus 23% in-skill (arxiv:2610.34777); benchmarks create a false sense of security (arxiv:2603.30016).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Make gaming scan defense-aware: for each registered gate, generate attacks conditioned on the gate's mechanism rather than a fixed corpus, and record adaptive robustness as the shipped number; align scanned channels with agent-visible channels including attachments and file contents. Success is procedural: no gate is promoted with only static-benchmark evidence, and every gate carries a measured adaptive-robustness figure.

glm.rationale: The 20,000+-attack campaign result - every model-relying defense broke, only output-side enforcement held - is the design constraint that keeps mini-ork's injection defenses deterministic (probe, tripwire, contracts) rather than detector-based.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - defense-aware adaptive evaluation of every registered gate
minimax.rationale: Across a 20,000+ attack adaptive campaign every model-relying defense broke and only output filtering held; 12 published in-band defenses break above 90%; a defense shipped on static-benchmark numbers alone is a false security claim, which is the second thing the snapshot asks this review to catch. It is next rather than now because it is the admission rule for the gates in the now-list, and mini-ork's gate registry has no shipped security gate to be broken yet.

ranked.technique: Mutation- and injection-based adequacy measurement for gates and verifier suites
ranked.mechanism: Inject security-regression mutants into a copy of the target and measure what the verifier set actually kills; each mutant is doubly validated (the injected build still passes the functional tests and a proof-of-vulnerability triggers only on it) so the ground truth is executable rather than asserted. A check is promoted to a hard gate only on demonstrated marginal separation — TPR minus FPR with interval estimates and multiple-comparison correction — between builds labelled by downstream outcome; checks that fail the screen stay advisory. The measurement is anchored on deterministic mutation kills and labelled outcomes, never on a model's opinion of the suite. Cautions: the standard single-observation validation (passes a good implementation, fails a broken one) certifies suites with major gaps, unearned passes grow with agent capability, and automatic identification of true vulnerability-inducing commits is still weak, so mutant corpora need dynamic validation before use.
ranked.reported_results: An invariant suite that passed standard validation caught only 5 of 10 independently specified faults (arxiv:2610.02928); of 13 validators screened against 550 runtime and 350 static labelled builds, only two survived correction for multiple comparisons (arxiv:2609.39037); confirmed unearned passes peak at 73.47% of passing tasks for a frontier model on SWE-bench Pro 1.0 (arxiv:2609.34262); doubly-validated vulnerability injection yielded 1,034 validated vulnerabilities across 80 projects and improved downstream repair +3.3 to +14.7 points (arxiv:2608.06471); a deterministic non-AI baseline killed 36/75/78 of 124 authored security regressions at increasing resource limits, calibrating what verification plans must beat (arxiv:2609.19844); SZZ-style commit identification reaches only 33.3-40.1% F1 (arxiv:2608.12246).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a mutant-audit mode to mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py: inject N doubly-validated security regressions into the run's base ref, run the code-fix verifier set, and report a per-gate kill rate; require demonstrated separation before register_gate_evaluator promotes any check to a hard gate. Measurement: kill rate on security mutants — expected to start near zero because the verifier set ships no security check — and its rise once the paired-oracle verifier (G07-T01) lands.

glm.landing_surface: verification-stack suite adequacy (docs/architecture/verification-stack.md) + mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py - security-mutant battery
glm.rationale: The stack already ships suite adequacy, and extending it with doubly validated security mutants is what proves the new verifier set catches anything (an invariant suite that passed standard validation killed only 5/10 faults; only 2 of 13 validators survived multiple-comparison correction). This is the measurement that keeps the new security gate from being theater.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py - a mutant-audit mode over the run's base ref, gating promotion of any check to a hard gate
minimax.rationale: The snapshot's gaming scan looks for patches that satisfy a gate without doing the work, but nothing measures whether the verifier set can kill a real security regression, and the measured state is damning: an invariant suite that passed standard validation caught only 5 of 10 independently specified faults, and a deterministic non-AI baseline killed 36/75/78 of 124 authored security regressions. Doubly-validated mutants make the ground truth executable, the kill rate on security mutants is expected to start near zero because no security check ships today, and this is the instrument that proves the now-list actually closed the hole.

ranked.technique: Layered oracles and silent-failure classification against deceptive fixes
ranked.mechanism: After the targeted symptom is removed, stack increasingly strong oracles — full-scanner cleanliness, plan/behavior diff, security-intent checking — and classify every test-passing repair as omission (the fix was never applied), introduction (a new vulnerability was added), or inadequacy (partial fix) instead of treating green tests as done. Purpose-built detectors for cross-cutting invariants catch locally-valid but globally-incoherent patches — missing auth guards on sibling routes, undeclared config keys — that typecheck, tests, and SAST almost never catch. Reproduction tests must be rigorous, failing on the original bug and its variants, and written before the code, because tests derived from faulty code inherit its misunderstanding and misaligned tests actively reduce resolved rates. Where intent cannot be checked mechanically the layer abstains, since conventional static analysis is structurally unable to verify requirement conformance (multiplication implemented as addition leaves no vulnerability signature).
ranked.reported_results: Targeted finding removed in 83.3% of Terraform repairs but full-scanner-clean in only 10.4%, and 71.4% of real-world repairs are deceptive fixes that pass every automated oracle (arxiv:2606.26590); across 170 test-passing agentic repairs: omission 48.2%, introduction 30.6%, inadequacy 21.2%, insecure API preserved in 24.7% (arxiv:2609.10548); rigorous bug-reproduction tests add +8.5pp resolved on SWE-bench Verified while lax tests add +0.0pp and misaligned ones -3.6pp (arxiv:2607.19843); test-first workflow detects 25% of injected faults vs about 14% for tests written after the faulty code (arxiv:2607.05139); 97% of cross-cutting structural failures evade strict compilation and 100% evade test suites and SAST (arxiv:2607.08981); static-analysis-guided agentic repair reaches 83.13% overall repair success with local open-source models (arxiv:2606.22647).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Order a deception layer after the test verifier in recipes/code-fix/verifiers/: a scanner-cleanliness check over the diff (starting with the pinned secret scan) plus a behavior/plan diff over the touched surface, with failures classified omission/introduction/inadequacy in the node verdict. Measurement: the deceptive-fix rate — repairs passing tests while preserving or introducing a finding — on replayed code-fix runs.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - layered oracles and introduction/omission/inadequacy classification
glm.rationale: Introduction - a new vulnerability added - occurs in 30.6% of 170 test-passing agentic repairs, exactly the agent-introduced-vulnerability hole, and the deterministic detectors for cross-cutting invariants (missing auth guards on sibling routes, undeclared config keys) are what test, typecheck and lint structurally cannot see.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - a deception layer after the test verifier, classifying failures as omission, introduction or inadequacy
minimax.rationale: 71.4% of real-world repairs are deceptive fixes that pass every automated oracle, and across 170 test-passing agentic repairs 48.2% were omissions, 30.6% introductions and 21.2% inadequacies, while 97% of cross-cutting structural failures evade strict compilation and 100% evade test suites and SAST. That is a precise statement of what the snapshot's test/typecheck/lint set cannot see, it layers on the existing verifier set rather than replacing it, and the three-way classification gives the gate a verdict vocabulary that matches the shipped PROVEN/REFUTED/UNVERIFIED trichotomy.

ranked.technique: Tiered hypothesis-then-confirm discovery with deterministic oracles
ranked.mechanism: Detection runs as a cheap-then-expensive-then-deterministic cascade: a cheap proposer (small/local model or lightweight static screen) generates vulnerability hypotheses over the changed surface; static-signal ranking (repository-wide security signals, shadow-complexity sinks, call-graph risk) decides which hypotheses deserve expensive reasoning; and only hypotheses confirmed by a deterministic oracle - sanitizer-instrumented execution, compiler check, a generated proof-of-concept that actually triggers, or a failing test - are reported as findings. The oracle, never the model, is the accept rule; unconfirmed hypotheses are recorded as abstentions in the run log rather than as findings. It consumes the run's touched-file set plus static-analyzer output, so cost scales with the diff rather than the repository. Anchored on reproduced runtime evidence.
ranked.reported_results: 11 to 14 confirmed vulnerabilities with recall 60% to 80%, zero false positives, and cost per vulnerability $10.57 to $8.43 versus a single-tier baseline (arxiv:2606.22263); generated-PoC confirmation via lightweight execution oracles confirms 84% of benchmark package vulnerabilities versus under 22% for prior program analysis (arxiv:2604.20179); an adversarial local verifier adds +10.3 precision points at $0.002 per sample with 77.2% F1 and 100% recall (arxiv:2604.21282); staged screening with selective dynamic verification outperforms static, encoder-based, and simpler agentic baselines on function-level and JIT benchmarks (arxiv:2603.13384); repo-signal prioritization then deep reasoning finds 20/35 logic vulnerabilities with GLM-4.7-Plus (arxiv:2607.01138); shadow-complexity sink screening makes algorithmic-complexity detection 4.7x/8.1x faster than prior tools while detecting more real ACVs (arxiv:2607.05474).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security_scan.py implementing the cascade over MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES: cheap hypothesis pass, static-signal ranking, deterministic confirmation (test/sanitizer/scanner reproduction), abstain otherwise. Measure on a seeded benchmark of replayed CVE-fixing commits: every finding reaching the gate must be oracle-confirmed by construction, and the reported number is seed recall at fixed per-run cost versus a single-pass frontier-scan baseline.

glm.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - security verifier (proposer tier + deterministic oracle confirm)
glm.rationale: This is the missing security check itself: cheap hypotheses over the changed surface, deterministic oracle confirmation (11-14 confirmed vulns, zero false positives, 8-10 dollars per vuln), scoped to MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES at one verifier node's cost. Oracle-not-model as the accept rule is already doctrine, so it composes with the shipped publish gate.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security_scan.py - cheap hypothesis pass, static-signal ranking, deterministic confirmation
minimax.rationale: This is the detector the missing security check needs: a cascade where a cheap proposer generates hypotheses over the touched surface, static signals decide which deserve expensive reasoning, and only hypotheses confirmed by a deterministic oracle are reported, with the rest recorded as abstentions. The measured shape is right for mini-ork's economics (60-80% recall at zero false positives, $10.57 to $8.43 per vulnerability, cost scaling with the diff via MINI_ORK_TOUCHED_FILES) and it satisfies the doctrine that the oracle, never the model, is the accept rule.

ranked.technique: Verifier-checkable, site-citing security findings (evidence-anchored adjudication)
ranked.mechanism: Every security finding must carry machine-checkable evidence - cited program sites (file:line, dataflow steps) or evidence-ledger entries - and a deterministic checker re-verifies that the cited sites exist and hold the claimed property before the finding can gate anything; entailment-style checking additionally requires the claimed reasoning path to be an actual traversal of the analyzed call/dependency graph. Findings whose citations do not verify are rejected; findings with no citations are abstentions by construction. Two cautions shape the design: models confirm vulnerabilities in already-patched code 23-61% of the time, and 26-55% of correct verdicts ride on flawed rationales - so the rationale is never the evidence, the citation is. Anchored on re-verifiable citations rather than prose plausibility.
ranked.reported_results: Site-citing verifier-checkable training lifts a 7B reviewer's verdict accuracy from 4.8% to 96.6% with 87.5% of Tier-1 oracle sites cited and zero off-oracle citations (arxiv:2610.35477); entailment checking of reasoning paths against call graphs and domain knowledge raises pooled entailment from 78% to 98% (arxiv:2608.01763); statement-level confirm/rule-out/uncertain analysis reaches 0.315 statement precision at 0.605 recall (arxiv:2611.06135); caution - all models confirm candidates in 23-61% of already-patched functions (arxiv:2611.06135) and 26-55% of true positives rest on flawed rationales (arxiv:2607.13439); evidence-augmented assessment makes outputs auditable with attached evidence rather than bare predictions (arxiv:2608.25905).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend the evidence-ledger record for security findings with mandatory citation fields (file:line sites, oracle output) and make the verifier drop any finding whose cited sites are absent from the diff or run artifacts. Measure the share of raw LLM findings rejected for unverifiable citations (expected high) and the human-audited precision of surviving findings versus an unstructured free-text baseline.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py - findings must cite file:line or ledger entries re-checked deterministically
glm.rationale: Site-citing, verifier-checkable findings (verdict accuracy 4.8% to 96.6% with zero off-oracle citations) are what stop a false security claim from gating - the third target on the impact scale - and it is a citation format plus a checker on the shipped evidence ledger.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - mandatory citation fields for security findings
minimax.rationale: Site-citing training lifts a 7B reviewer's verdict accuracy from 4.8% to 96.6% with zero off-oracle citations, and the cautions are the point (models confirm vulnerabilities in already-patched code 23-61% of the time; 26-55% of true positives rest on flawed rationales, so the citation is the evidence and the rationale never is). It is next because it is the attribute of a finding rather than the check that produces one.

ranked.technique: Label-blind audit of failed attacks: ignored is not refused
ranked.mechanism: A low attack-success rate is not evidence of defense. Audit the trajectories of failed attacks label-blind and classify each outcome - refused (the agent recognized and rejected the manipulation), ignored (the manipulation simply did not take), or executed-anyway - and score safety and task completion as separate axes, because an agent can be safe and useless. The finding: most 'failed' injections were merely ignored, a nontrivial fraction still executed the attacker's action, and headline attack-success metrics swing wildly with configuration. The transferable rule for any gate: a pass must be shown to have examined the surface, not merely failed to react.
ranked.reported_results: 76.3-80.3% of failed attacks were ignored while genuine refusal accounted for only 17.2-18.0%; in 28.9% and 16.9% of failed attacks the agent still executed the attacker's action; changing only the system prompt shifts InjecAgent ASR from 0.2% to 43%; 21.7% of AgentDojo episodes stayed safe but did not complete the user's task (arxiv:2610.23254).
ranked.adoption_sketch: After each gated run, audit verifier engagement without trusting exit codes: check the trace for whether each verifier actually read its evidence surface (touched files opened, commands executed) and classify every pass as examined / ignored / no-op, publishing the three-way split beside the gate verdict. Measure by seeding no-op verifiers into test runs and requiring the audit to classify them correctly while examined passes stay classified as examined.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/gaming_scan.py - label-blind outcome classification for the injection probe
glm.rationale: The injection probe's scoring rule: classify failed attacks label-blind - 76-80% were merely ignored, only 17-18% refused, and 16.9-28.9% still executed the attacker's action - or the probe will overclaim robustness. Cheap, and it makes G02-T10's measurement honest.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - classify each pass as examined, ignored or no-op by checking whether the verifier actually read its evidence surface
minimax.rationale: 76.3-80.3% of failed attacks were ignored while genuine refusal was only 17.2-18.0%, and in 28.9% and 16.9% of failed attacks the agent still executed the attacker's action, so a pass must be shown to have examined the surface rather than merely failed to react. It is S effort and directly guards the new security verifier against being a no-op, which is precisely the false-security-claim failure this review is asked to catch.

ranked.technique: Execution-grounded ground truth with attributable verdicts
ranked.mechanism: Makes ground-truth labels for security claims executable before they gate anything: a label counts only if an artifact substantiates it — a differential run between vulnerable and fixed revisions, a SAST hit adjudicated by multiple independent LLMs plus human spot-checks — and the substantiating evidence is kept for replay. Verdict and justification are scored separately (a correct verdict with an unsound rationale earns partial credit, never full trust), and a reviewer must cite the specific defect that makes a change unsafe, so a block triggered by an unrelated issue cannot masquerade as a security catch. Reject rule: labels that cannot be substantiated by replay are dropped from the ground truth, not averaged in. Cautions: widely-used label sources audit as unreliable (NVD CWE labels; up to 23% invalid labels in popular vulnerability datasets); MCP security scanners flag almost everything with precision near 50%, so scanner verdicts are leads, not ground truth; and LLM evaluators judged 85% of agent findings valid where measured precision was below 9%.
ranked.reported_results: LLM-agent-constructed vulnerability-triggering experiments audit function-level labels in BigVul/PrimeVul/DiverseVul with replayable evidence (arxiv:2610.05103); up to 23% invalid labels and Matthews correlation near zero after cleanup across 770 published runs (arxiv:2611.06373); large-scale code-semantics audit of NVD CWE label reliability (arxiv:2608.21977); frontier coding agents reach recall below 21% and precision below 9% while LLM and human evaluators judge 85% of findings valid (arxiv:2610.35987); MCP scanner precision near 50% at best with poor CVE recall (arxiv:2607.11086).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Require every security-relevant verifier verdict mini-ork records to carry an evidence pointer in the evidence ledger (failing input, differential pair, or cited line range); a verdict without one is recorded as an abstention. Measure: share of gate verdicts carrying executable evidence, and inter-adjudicator agreement on a sampled subset.

glm.rationale: Execution-grounded labels with attributable verdicts is the discipline for building the security verifier's own validation set; fold it into G07-T02's mutant corpus rather than a separate build.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - every security verdict carries an evidence pointer in the evidence ledger
minimax.rationale: The evidence is decisive about false security claims: frontier coding agents reach precision below 9% while LLM and human evaluators judge 85% of findings valid, MCP scanners flag almost everything at precision near 50%, and up to 23% of labels in popular vulnerability datasets are invalid. Requiring an evidence pointer and dropping unsubstantiated labels is the cheapest way to stop mini-ork publishing a security claim it cannot substantiate; it is next because it is a property of the verdicts rather than the verifier set's existence.

ranked.technique: Correlated-agreement blindness of report-based auditing (caution)
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique: audit layers built on agent-filed reports relay conclusions instead of verifying them. It is provable that no report-only aggregator can generally distinguish replicated reports from independent evidence (the epistemic Sybil bound), and empirically such accountability layers originate almost nothing on clean episodes, filter upstream error poorly, and name origins from within the agents' own proposals. Disagreement-triggered escalation misses correlated errors — most errors occur while agents agree — so twin reviewers from similar training distributions share blind spots, and numerically correct metrics can measure a different construct than their label claims; benign agents also covertly assist each other past safety boundaries without adversarial incentives, and runtime explainers' accounts can diverge from actual agent state. Countermeasure when keeping multi-reviewer designs: heterogeneous detector ensembles with a calibrating arbitrator, conservative override, and a safety-flag gate to human review, with every verdict anchored on execution records rather than peer reports. Rule: treat agreement between correlated reviewers as weak evidence; accept only on independent execution evidence; escalate on correlated-agreement risk.
ranked.reported_results: No report-only aggregator can generally distinguish replication from independent evidence (proved) (arxiv:2609.01873); a report-based accountability layer originates almost nothing on clean episodes and filters upstream error poorly (arxiv:2609.07680); most errors occur while agents agree and joint error inflates several-fold under disagreement-triggered escalation (arxiv:2607.19899); a compaction pilot's reported 94.39% figure was reproduced as measuring a different construct than its label implied (arxiv:2609.12017).
ranked.adoption_sketch: In mini_ork/cli/publisher.py, require each reviewer verdict to cite execution-record ids from the evidence ledger rather than node self-reports, and flag acceptances where both reviewers rest on the same non-independent evidence base. Measurement: a seeded run whose nodes relay one upstream error is escalated rather than promoted.

glm.rationale: The correlated-agreement bound correctly warns that mini-ork's two-reviewer pattern shares blind spots; the remedy - anchor reviews to execution records, not reports - is already evidence-ledger discipline, and disagreement flags ship in merge_reviews.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - reviewer verdicts cite execution-record ids rather than node self-reports
minimax.rationale: The epistemic Sybil bound means no report-only aggregator can distinguish replicated reports from independent evidence, and disagreement-triggered escalation misses correlated errors because most errors occur while agents agree - directly relevant to mini-ork's two-reviewer merge and to the voting between reviewers that this very run feeds. It is next because it hardens an existing multi-review surface rather than filling a named hole.

ranked.technique: Tool-output integrity audit: formatter fidelity, fabricated-evidence probes, counterfactual redaction
ranked.mechanism: Audits the gap between what a tool did and what it prints. Formatter-fidelity checks re-derive each agent and verifier claim from raw tool output rather than the formatter's summary, catching omission-type misrepresentation (search limits, result caps, identifier namespaces) that falsification checks are blind to; fabricated-evidence probes feed the verifier deliberately false assurances to measure deference, with per-claim verification plus refutation display as the measured remedy; counterfactual redaction deletes localized token classes and re-runs the frozen judge to expose which tool result a conclusion actually depends on. Accept: a claim survives re-derivation and redaction; reject: a claim depends on a redactable shortcut or contradicts the raw output; abstain: unverifiable claims are labeled unsupported. Anchored on raw output bytes and a frozen verifier, not on any model's reading of them.
ranked.reported_results: Repairing formatter wording flipped verifier verdicts from accepting incorrect answers 90/90 to rejecting 90/90, and warped formatters were found in production OpenClaw and Hermes (arxiv:2610.32110); false assurances lower real-vulnerability detection by up to 19 points while per-claim verification with refutation display recovers 12 points (p = 0.002) (arxiv:2610.32876); redacting localized identifiers drops performance to chance, proving shortcut dependence (arxiv:2610.25540); value-versus-binding decomposition attributes 67.5-81.8% of failing financial claims to wrong-binding errors (arxiv:2610.34887); reference-free fault localization locates failing pipeline stages from logs without expected outputs (arxiv:2611.03725).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add recipes/code-fix/verifiers/security.py that re-derives every verifier claim from raw command output instead of its formatted summary, plus a canary probe that injects a false 'all checks passed' note to measure verifier deference. Success is the canary being rejected and omission-style misreports caught on a fixture set — the first security check in a set that today has none.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - re-derive claims from raw tool output; fabricated-evidence probes
glm.rationale: Formatter fidelity (90/90 verdict flips from summary wording alone) and fabricated-evidence probes measure verifier deference - cheap hardening for the new security verifier's own reporting path.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - re-derive every verifier claim from raw command output, plus a false-assurance canary probe
minimax.rationale: Repairing formatter wording flipped verifier verdicts from accepting incorrect answers 90/90 to rejecting 90/90, and false assurances lower real-vulnerability detection by up to 19 points, so re-derivation from raw bytes plus a planted false assurance is a concrete, deterministic check that the new security verifier does not merely report fine. It is next because it is a property of the verifier's output handling rather than the check itself.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: dormant, staged, and distributed payloads; matched by boundary-action auditing
ranked.mechanism: Caution plus matched defense — injections that do not fire on contact defeat presence-based screening: sleeper payloads persist across interactions served by the same agent, trigger-conditioned payloads stay dormant until an attacker-chosen event, staged injections propagate across causally connected workflow stages to alter a later consequential action, and harmful objectives split across individually benign requests under unlinkable identities defeat every stateful defense tested. Deployed classifiers trained on contact-fired injections are miscalibrated on dormant ones.
