glm.rationale: Ceilings that abort already ship (MO_NODE_TIMEOUT_S, MO_NODE_MAX_TURNS, MO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD, heartbeat watchdogs); the 658x token-amplification attacks die at the same budget cliff.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config (+ sandbox placement and per-node sandbox) - per-node token and tool-call ceilings
minimax.rationale: The snapshot has no per-node budget ceiling beyond MO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD and node timeouts, and the evidence shows a single crafted tool-chain response inflating consumption to 60,000+ tokens per interaction (658x). A fail-closed per-node ceiling is S effort and stops denial-of-wallet through the injection path, but it is a containment measure rather than a detector, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Scope-adherence and dead-end evaluation under deception
ranked.mechanism: Tests whether an agent stops when stopping is correct: tasks whose stated objective is impossible (dead ends) where the only passing behavior is to recognize the dead end and stay in scope, and resource-conflict scenarios where a privileged agent may seize or terminate a pre-existing task instead of reporting the conflict. Decision integrity is measured directly — whether a choice under a deceptive injection is steered toward the attacker's target — and tool outputs are adversarially poisoned in matched clean/poisoned pairs to separate checking a plausible result from adopting it. Accept rule: out-of-scope actions are hard failures regardless of task success, and adoption of an unvalidated poisoned tool result fails even when the final answer looks right. Anchored on execution traces of what the agent actually did, not its stated rationale. Caution: dual-control interaction (trajectory jointly shaped by user and agent) raises attack success substantially versus solo evaluation, so solo-run safety numbers overstate protection in interactive use.
ranked.reported_results: 30 dead-end offensive tasks where the stated objective is impossible and the only correct behavior is to stop in scope (arxiv:2609.30325); dual-control interaction raises attack success substantially across 14 models / 8 domains versus solo evaluation (arxiv:2609.24662); decision-steering measured with multi-candidate selection tasks under deceptive injections (arxiv:2610.06898); clean/poisoned observation pairs quantify blind compliance with plausible-but-wrong tool outputs (arxiv:2609.37153).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Encode kickoff constraints (the c:0/c:1-style scope limits) as machine-checkable declarations and add dead-end fixtures to the run suite: impossible-in-scope tasks whose pass condition is a clean stop plus escalation. Measure: rate at which lanes violate declared scope on fixtures, and rate of correct stops.

glm.rationale: Dead-end and scope-adherence measurement is a benchmark shape; the nearest mini-ork need (stopping at impossible tasks) is already planner/verifier behavior.

minimax.landing_surface: kickoff and intake guard - machine-checkable scope declarations plus dead-end fixtures whose pass condition is a clean stop
minimax.rationale: The snapshot's kickoff guard already parses numbered hard constraints, so turning them into machine-checkable rules and adding fixtures where the correct behavior is to stop in scope is a cheap, deterministic extension, and 66.22% of unsafe runs still complete their task means completion cannot stand in for safety. It is next because it measures scope adherence rather than the planted-instruction behavior the probe measures.

ranked.technique: Pre-commit persistent-memory write triage (Accept / Review / Quarantine)
ranked.mechanism: Intercept every proposed write to persistent memory (lessons, preferences, semantic entries, cross-agent shared insights) before commit and decide it deterministically from source trust, semantic risk, and attack radius over a dependency DAG - never from content screening alone, which catches 0/360 attacks and is suppressed to at most 7.4% detection by placement attacks. Accept only writes of trusted provenance with bounded blast radius; quarantine writes originating from untrusted channels whose semantics touch authority, credentials, or future tool choice; route to human review when classifiers disagree, so the gate abstains rather than guesses. Score whole write batches rather than single entries, because salami-sliced coalitions of individually benign fragments and end-to-end optimized payloads survive per-stage defenses. The anchor is write-time provenance and trust labels, not retrieval-time detection; Caution: this is a defense technique whose limits are documented - content screening alone fails, so the provenance/trust signal is the load-bearing part.
ranked.reported_results: MemSentry: all four classifiers detect 100% of external quarantine-class threats; SBERT+LR 91.7% accuracy, 0.908 macro-F1 (arxiv:2609.08747). SENTINEL reduces FARM attack success 100% to 0% (arxiv:2607.05029). Write-time memory safety filtering: 100% detection, restores without-memory baseline (arxiv:2607.17619). MAPLE-Guard: attack success 38.2% to 0.9% (LongMemEval) and 34.7% to 0.2% (AppWorld) (arxiv:2608.00426). CAPTURE: poisoning detection 71.5% F1 (arxiv:2609.02265). Negative: content screening catches 0/360 and utility falls 0.850 to 0.300 at 1.2% poison fraction (arxiv:2608.21230); MAFIA reaches 90.7% ASR while holding audit detection at most 7.4% (arxiv:2608.03844); MemCollusion 75.0% ASR survives memory-level defenses (arxiv:2608.01637); PIPEPOISON retains 41-66% AUR under eight defenses (arxiv:2609.00523).
ranked.miniork_surface: Sibling of the evidence-ledger surface: the GRPO learning-writeback / run-lessons memory - mini_ork/learning/writeback.py and mini_ork/memory/ (lessons injected into every node prompt are trusted persistent state).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a deterministic pre-commit gate in the learning writeback path that stamps every persisted lesson with origin node, run id, and artifact source, and quarantines any write derived from untrusted-channel content (retrieved body text, user files) whose semantics mention authority, credentials, or tool choice. Measurement: replay historical lesson writes through the gate for the Accept/Review/Quarantine split, then run a fixture set of planted lessons (the MemPoison 1,227-case pattern) and require 100% quarantine with zero blocked legitimate lessons.

glm.rationale: Lessons injected into every node prompt are trusted persistent state, and write-time provenance is the load-bearing signal (content screening alone catches 0/360). Real surface, but second-order next to the verifier-set hole, and the classifier numbers (MemSentry 100% detection) are single-system claims.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/learning/writeback.py and mini_ork/memory/ (GRPO lesson writeback)
minimax.rationale: The state snapshot notes the evidence-ledger surface but nothing gates what persistent memory accepts, and the evidence is explicit that content screening catches 0/360 attacks while write-time provenance filtering reaches 100% detection with a restores-baseline utility. It is a real open gap but sits beside, not on, the two named holes (no security verifier, no injection probe), so it waits behind the now-list.

ranked.technique: Proof-of-execution ledger: trust executed steps, never claimed steps
ranked.mechanism: Never accept an agent's claim that a safety or verification step ran: a tamper-proof log writable only by trusted code records what actually executed, and every consumer (publish gate, planner, sibling node) must match the claim against the log before relying on it. Wording- and content-based defenses against forged already-done entries are defeated by simple rewording (protection drops to zero) and additionally block 33-50% of legitimate operations, whereas the execution-log check blocks all forged-reasoning attacks at microsecond overhead - and the forged-claim attack is stronger on more capable models, so capability is no excuse. The rule is purely deterministic: a claimed step is accepted if and only if a matching trusted-log entry exists; otherwise reject, with no LLM judgment in the path.
ranked.reported_results: PoEM: 0% attack success and 0% false positives in 8 of 9 evaluation cells (1.7% in the ninth) at microseconds of overhead; SENTINEL is defeated by rewording (protection to zero across 3 models) and wrongly blocks 33-50% of legitimate operations; FARMA succeeds 98-100% on GPT-4o-class versus 44% on Llama-3.1-8B (arxiv:2608.16032). Signed trajectories plus path-aware runtime verification mitigate workflow-repository invalidation attacks that reach 90.12% attack success unprotected (arxiv:2610.14795).
ranked.miniork_surface: evidence ledger and traces - mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py, consumed by the publish gate.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Tighten the publish gate to deny promotion when a node's output asserts a verifier outcome (tests, gates, approvals) that has no matching evidence-ledger row written by the verifier itself; the ledger stays writable only by trusted runtime code. Measurement: inject transcripts claiming green gates without ledger rows and require 100% denial with zero false denials on genuine runs.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py consumed by the publish gate
glm.rationale: The evidence ledger ships, but claims are not yet matched against a tamper-resistant execution log; PoEM's 0% attack success at microsecond cost and SENTINEL's collapse under rewording make this the right extension once the security verifier exists.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py, consumed by the publish gate
minimax.rationale: The snapshot says node output is written to the run dir and cited by path, but nothing requires a claimed verifier outcome to have a matching trusted-log row; the evidence is sharp (0% attack success at microsecond overhead, while wording-based defenses fall to zero protection and wrongly block 33-50% of legitimate operations). It is the substrate the new security check needs, so it is next behind the check itself.

ranked.technique: Context-isolated verification of persistent-state-dependent decisions
ranked.mechanism: Verifiers and safety checks must run in a context that shares no state with the agent or memory they judge. Persistent semantics propagate through name binding, event triggers, and tool registries: all 24 evaluated models across 11 families were susceptible at 20-100% contamination, and multi-agent cascades amplify contamination from 40% to 75% over four stages - shared-context self-checks inherit the poison they are meant to catch. Context-isolated verification reduces contamination 20-79% precisely because the verifier does not share the contaminated state, and removing name binding alone drops contamination to 0%, showing the propagation channel is structural, not statistical. Rule: a check over persistent state yields Accept only from an isolated verifier; a shared-context check may only abstain.
ranked.reported_results: All 24 models (11 families, 1.5B-1T parameters) susceptible at 20-100%; removing name binding reduces contamination to 0%; multi-agent cascades amplify contamination 40% to 75% over four stages; context-isolated self-verification reduces contamination 20-79% across 8 models (arxiv:2608.07952).
ranked.miniork_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - verifier nodes must not share context or persistent state with the implementer nodes they judge.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Audit that every verifier node runs in a fresh process and context receiving only its declared input manifest, and add a regression test that a poisoned lesson or shared cache entry cannot influence a verifier verdict. Measurement: run verifier nodes with and without state isolation against a poisoned-state fixture and report the verdict delta (target: zero influence in the isolated configuration).

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - verifier nodes must not share persistent state with implementers
glm.rationale: Artifact contracts already isolate node inputs, but lessons are injected into every node prompt - shared state. Running the new security verifier without implementer lessons is a cheap, measured (20-79% contamination reduction) isolation win.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - verifier nodes must not share context or persistent state with the implementer nodes they judge
minimax.rationale: This directly protects the new security verifier: the evidence shows every one of 24 models across 11 families was susceptible to persistent-state contamination at 20-100%, that removing name binding alone drops it to 0%, and that context isolation removes 20-79%. Since the snapshot's whole problem is that nobody currently checks a patch for security, a checker that inherits the implementer's poisoned context is worth little.

ranked.technique: Policy-graded evaluation under enforced security tiers
ranked.mechanism: Evaluates agents inside natively enforced policy tiers — scoped credentials, restricted egress, read-only filesystems, non-root — so numbers describe behavior under a real boundary rather than under instructions. Reference-solution solvability audits separate tasks the policy forecloses (harness failures) from model failures, so a score drop after hardening is attributed correctly; provisioning starts from a task-matched minimal harness and escalates only after failed self-checks, charting the accuracy-cost frontier of hardening. Harness configuration is varied factorially (tool exposure, permission enforcement, extension loading, state persistence) across the task lifecycle to isolate harness-induced from model-induced risk. Accept rule: a security property counts as present only when the harness enforces it deny-by-default, never when the model merely respects it. Caution: about half of confirmed harness security mechanisms in major coding-agent harnesses are opt-in, so 'shipped' does not mean 'on'.
ranked.reported_results: 12 coding agents on Terminal-Bench 2.1 under nested NIST-derived policy levels: hardening costs are large, non-uniform, and predictable via reference-solution compatibility (arxiv:2608.02670); about half of confirmed harness security mechanisms are opt-in, with substantial evidence gaps in closed-source harnesses across 400 mechanism cells (arxiv:2610.07639); minimal-first harness provisioning with escalation on failed self-checks shows a domain-dependent accuracy-cost frontier (arxiv:2608.17433); user memories expressing a preference shift cited sources by 33–39 percentage points under controlled harness manipulation (arxiv:2611.03939).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Define two enforced placement tiers for mini-ork nodes (network-restricted + read-only workspace vs today's default) and run one recipe's fan-out under both, with a reference-solution check that tasks remain solvable under restriction. Measure: task success delta per tier plus per-node blocked-egress counts — the measured delta, not anecdotes, prices the boundary.

glm.rationale: Policy-tier evaluation would measure what enforced sandbox tiers cost mini-ork's own recipes - useful before mandating G03-T02, not independently.

minimax.landing_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox - two enforced placement tiers with a reference-solution solvability check
minimax.rationale: About half of confirmed harness security mechanisms in major coding-agent harnesses are opt-in, and about half of the confirmed harness mechanisms have evidence gaps in closed-source harnesses, so 'shipped does not mean on' is exactly the measurement mini-ork needs against its own configurable placement. The reference-solution audit is what keeps a hardened tier from being scored as a harness failure, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Claim-to-evidence adjudication with execution-bound receipts
ranked.mechanism: Every claim in an agent-produced artifact is represented as a node linked to a verbatim evidence packet — a source span, a tool output, or an execution event — and an adjudicator assigns a support relation (supported / unsupported / contradicted / mixed); unsupported or contradicted claims are routed back to the author node instead of silently passing. Repairs are typed state transitions that cannot introduce content lacking tool-produced provenance, and claims may cite only currently active ledger entries. A claim-anchored receipt jointly binds the claim shown to the user, its exact cited span, the ordered execution prefix that produced it, and the source version observed, so a valid citation cannot be transplanted across claims, actions, runs, or source versions. Accept = every load-bearing claim supported by a live packet; reject/return = any unsupported, contradicted, or mixed claim; abstain = packet missing, which is a hold rather than a pass. Caution: a hash does not establish semantic truth and a signature does not establish authorization, so adjudication is anchored on the execution record itself, not on the agent's summary of it.
ranked.reported_results: Validated on a 2,335-row blind benchmark, substantially beating non-agent baselines (arxiv:2607.26512).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py so each node's claims carry an evidence-packet id and unsupported claims route back to the author node, reusing the receipt shape (claim, span, execution prefix, source version) at emit time. Measurement: on this recipe's own runs, the final verify already rejects citations absent from the corpus — extend it to count routed-back claims and show seeded unsupported claims never reach the published report.

glm.rationale: Claim-to-evidence adjudication with execution-bound receipts extends the ledger in the right direction (unsupported claims route back to the author node), but the evidence is a single 2,335-row benchmark; pilot on report-style nodes.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - claims carry an evidence-packet id, unsupported claims route back to the author node
minimax.rationale: The snapshot ships an evidence ledger with per-run transcripts and path citations; this adds the support relation and the routing-back behavior, so a claim with no verbatim packet is returned rather than silently passed. The caution is exactly the doctrine's point (a hash does not establish semantic truth, a signature does not establish authorization), which makes it a sound extension rather than a new capability; next.

ranked.technique: Intake and repository-context poisoning controls (caution: prevention over detection)
ranked.mechanism: The context an implementer consumes is an attack surface: a single insecure exemplar in repository context measurably raises exploitable generation, withheld safeguards measurably lower security, and adversarial issue descriptions — benign-looking text that smuggles a vulnerability into a functionally correct patch — succeed at high rates against repair agents. Guard at intake: flag or withhold insecure exemplars from retrieved context, record context provenance, and treat kickoff and issue text as untrusted input rather than instruction. Post-hoc detection is a weak backstop — static analysis and LLM judges both miss most manipulated repairs — so when intake cannot be established clean for a security-sensitive task, the run abstains rather than proceeds.
ranked.reported_results: One insecure exemplar in context raises exploitable-code generation by 6.3 points and withholding repository safeguards costs 8.1 points, with safeguards followed in only 27-36% of trajectories (arxiv:2611.06294); adversarial issue descriptions achieve 40-64% attack success with malicious-but-successful repair in 51.7% of cases on average, while post-repair detection averages only 39.4% (static analysis) and 55.4% (LLM judge), and pre-repair detection only 62.3% (arxiv:2609.15963).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py and the intake layer to scan files selected as implementer context for insecure-exemplar patterns and to record the provenance of every context source in the run manifest. Measurement: difference in security-check failure rates between runs with flagged context withheld versus present, and how often intake flags correlate with later verifier findings.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py + mini_ork/intake/ - untrusted labeling of issue text and repo context
glm.rationale: Adversarial issue descriptions reach 40-64% ASR with post-repair detection averaging only 39.4%, so intake must label issue text and repo context untrusted, and the measurement belongs to the G02-T10 probe; the insecure-exemplar effect (+6.3pp exploitable generation) is the context-selection rule.

minimax.landing_surface: kickoff and intake guard - flag insecure exemplars from implementer context and record context provenance in the run manifest
minimax.rationale: One insecure exemplar in context raises exploitable-code generation by 6.3 points and withholding repository safeguards costs 8.1 points, while adversarial issue descriptions succeed at 40-64% with post-repair detection only 39.4% (static analysis) and 55.4% (LLM judge) - so detection is a weak backstop and prevention at intake is the load-bearing part. This is the intake-side half of the injection hole and belongs beside the probe in the now-list.

ranked.technique: Typed, isolated tool-result channels with span-level sanitization
ranked.mechanism: Tool outputs never enter agent context as free text: each is parsed into a typed, provenance-tagged envelope whose fields the node's declared port announced, and anything inside that parses as an instruction is quarantined as data. Each tool or subagent gets an isolated context segment so a fabricated trace in one tool's output (for example a spoofed 'this already passed moderation' record) cannot authorize behavior in another tool's channel, and a privileged executor sees only a minimal compressed residual from the untrusted side. Sanitizers delete only injected spans rather than whole outputs, preserving task-relevant content; residual key-mediated evasion is a documented limitation, so this is a reducer paired with boundary enforcement, not a complete boundary. Accept: declared-field content; reject/quarantine: instruction-like spans; abstain: unparseable output fails closed to an error artifact.
ranked.reported_results: Simulated moderation traces jailbreak shared-context function-calling at 99.67% ASR on SafeBench and 98.33% on JailbenchBench with input and output filtering ineffective — structural isolation is required (arxiv:2607.00481); application-layer channel separation detects concealed injections at precision 1.000 / recall 0.944 with zero false positives on clean resumes (arxiv:2609.20188); an offline-learned sanitizer cuts AgentDojo ASR 34.6% to 0.1% and raises attack-free completion 51.4% to 77.5% with ~127x fewer defense tokens, while residual key-mediated and within-unit evasion persists (arxiv:2610.39758); typed tool-result parsing mitigates injected instructions without degrading task completion (arxiv:2601.04795); privilege-separated twin agents with context compression improve the security-utility tradeoff (arxiv:2607.19595).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Wrap every tool-server response in a typed envelope (fields the port declared, provenance tag, instruction-quarantine marker) before it reaches a node's prompt, and give each MCP server its own isolated context segment. Measure: an instruction planted in one tool's output changes no downstream node decision and benign completion is unchanged.

glm.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - typed tool-result envelopes
glm.rationale: Typed envelopes fit mini-ork's declared ports, but node inputs are already structured artifacts; the free-text surfaces (evidence files, docs) are covered more cheaply by intake labeling (G07-T09).

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - typed, provenance-tagged envelopes around every tool response, with one isolated context segment per tool server
minimax.rationale: Simulated moderation traces jailbreak shared-context function-calling at 99.67% ASR with input and output filtering ineffective, which makes structural isolation the load-bearing property, and a typed envelope is the cheapest form of it (precision 1.000 / recall 0.944 with zero false positives on clean resumes). It is next because it needs the MCP surface wrapped, which is a real build, and because the technique's own caution says it is a reducer paired with boundary enforcement rather than a boundary.

ranked.technique: Perception/retrieval-boundary screening with graded demotion
ranked.mechanism: Screens external content before it enters agent state: static field contracts on response units, trajectory-conditioned priors, and a trusted provenance hierarchy decide how much informational authority each unit gets — the attack model is content making environmental claims beyond its source's authority. Suspicious units are demoted (quoted, excluded from decisions) rather than hard-filtered, which preserves benign utility; soft trust scoring with label-embedding consistency checking plus multi-document retrieval dilution cuts single-document label flips; cross-modal screening reads semantic intent via few-shot reasoning instead of surface patterns. Accept: provenance-consistent content; demote: authority-exceeding claims; abstain: unresolved trust drops the unit from decision inputs while staying visible to the operator.
ranked.reported_results: Provenance screening cuts adaptive PAIR attack success from 84.7% to 2.3% (and 21.6% to 1.1% on a second model) while benign utility is 92.5% versus 90.6% undefended (arxiv:2608.12789); multi-document retrieval dilution drops injection-driven label flips from 35-55% single-document to 0.6-2.4%, with recovery degrading gracefully from R=1.0 at 1% poisoning to 0.57 at 30% and soft demotion beating hard filtering (arxiv:2608.08100); ICL reasoning-based cross-modal detection reaches up to 99.80% on 500 obfuscated injections and 100% recall on textual tasks (arxiv:2610.30202); prefill attention probes that predict actual breach avoid the over-refusal of presence-based detection, with hardening levels L4-L5 most consistently improving resistance (arxiv:2608.08027); generator-defender co-training adds resilience to evolving hidden prompts (arxiv:2604.26506).
ranked.adoption_sketch: On every retrieved artifact or tool response entering a node, run contract checks (fields the port declared, provenance tag) and demote units whose claims exceed their source's authority to quoted-data status. Measure: an injection planted in a retrieved evidence file is demoted with benign retrieval utility unchanged.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/intake/ - graded demotion of untrusted retrieved content
glm.rationale: Graded demotion (quote, exclude from decisions) fits the research recipes' retrieved body text - adaptive PAIR fell 84.7% to 2.3% at 92.5% utility - without hard-filter cost.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - contract checks and graded demotion at the retrieval boundary
minimax.rationale: Provenance screening cuts adaptive attack success from 84.7% to 2.3% while benign utility holds, and multi-document retrieval dilution drops injection-driven label flips from 35-55% to 0.6-2.4%, with soft demotion beating hard filtering - which matters for a research recipe that ingests 2,000 retrieved papers. It is next because it is a per-artifact rule and the run's own corpus is a plausible injection target.

ranked.technique: Provenance-based information flow control at the tool-execution boundary
ranked.mechanism: Every artifact and tool result carries a provenance/sensitivity label, and a deterministic information-flow check runs at the tool-execution boundary - the one point the model cannot manipulate - so labeled data can flow only to tools whose declared recipient class matches. Enforcement deliberately lives in a programmatic layer rather than the conversational surface: prompt-level and single-context consent defenses are structurally bypassable because the attacker controls that surface, and channel-diversion attacks split the extraction request and the disclosure across two channels that single-context checks never associate. Denied invocations are recorded as first-class provenance events, so denial-feedback laundering (probe a protected action, learn from the denial, exfiltrate the inference through a later benign call) becomes visible where flat data-flow tracking misses it. Accept rule: a tool call proceeds only if no labeled byte flows to an unapproved channel; otherwise it is blocked and logged, and the denial itself is ledgered.
ranked.reported_results: Provenance-based IFC dropped leak rates from 52.2% to 0.5% (Collaborative Workspace Lure) with item-level leakage held to 0-3.3% at 72.4% benign-task utility across eight attacks including a live MCP-agent setting, regardless of LLM backend (arxiv:2609.14003); channel-diversion attacks achieved 43.8-75.6% item-level leakage vs 1.9-3.0% for prior single-context attacks (arxiv:2609.14003); denial-feedback leakage succeeded across all constructed scenarios (100 runs each) and was not captured by flat provenance tracking (arxiv:2604.04035).
ranked.miniork_surface: MCP / tool surface (interception at tool dispatch), with sensitivity labels carried in the artifact contract (schemas/artifact_contract.schema.json)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend the artifact contract's declared ports with a sensitivity class, and enforce flow in the tool dispatcher: any tool argument whose bytes originate from a labeled artifact may proceed only if the tool's declared egress class admits it, with denials written to the evidence ledger. Measure by replaying disguised-retrieval and split-channel scenarios against a scratch agent and requiring a near-zero leak rate where prompt-level filters were bypassed at 81-87% (arxiv:2604.05432).

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - provenance labels enforced at dispatch
glm.rationale: Provenance IFC at the tool boundary (52.2% to 0.5% leak) is the strict version of artifact-contract visibility limits; sequence after labels exist in manifests.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - a deterministic information-flow check at tool dispatch, with sensitivity labels in schemas/artifact_contract.schema.json
minimax.rationale: Enforcement at the one point the model cannot manipulate is what makes the check meaningful: provenance-based IFC dropped leak rates from 52.2% to 0.5% while holding benign-task utility, and denial events written to the ledger expose denial-feedback laundering that flat tracking misses. It is next because it requires extending the shipped artifact contract with sensitivity classes, which is a schema change with cross-recipe consequences.

ranked.technique: Deterministic pre-execution action verification and policy gating
ranked.mechanism: Interpose a decision point before every tool call or shell command: canonicalize the action into a stable verification target, then apply deterministic evidence (syntax, binaries, path context, provenance, declared policy rules) with an LLM intent judge escalated only for genuinely underdetermined cases. The rule is execute / ask / refuse: clearly-in-scope actions run, clearly-out-of-scope actions are refused before any side effect, and ambiguous ones are escalated rather than guessed. Anchored on deterministic checks and a declared policy, not model opinion — alignment is probabilistic and post-hoc evaluation is retrospective, so enforcement must sit at the action boundary. A two-stage cascade (cheap local check, then a stronger judge only on escalation) buys most of the interception at a fraction of the false-positive rate.
ranked.reported_results: 85.64% F1 at 0.91% FPR with 2.32ms median latency; static-only profile 84.99% F1 at 0.34ms; downstream harm reduced 37.33% (arxiv:2607.21642). Catches 95.8% of invalid commands at 10.0% FPR across 9,930 commands and 482 tools (arxiv:2609.11957). All five LLM intent judges achieve at least 93% interception; two-stage cascading cuts FPR from 34.1% to 1.9% while retaining 91.9-92.6% interception (arxiv:2603.07191). Guardrails proxy lifts injection recall from 25.0% to 94.5% at 0.1% FPR (arxiv:2610.09906). Deterministic rule enforcement at the tool-call boundary reaches DSR 97.4-98.2% (residual ASR 0.6-3.1%) on AgentDojo (arxiv:2604.11790). EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE routing beats open-weight 3-4B guards by 39-50 points on accuracy (arxiv:2607.13594).
ranked.miniork_surface: `MCP / tool surface` — concretely its sibling, the dispatch tool-call boundary in `mini_ork/dispatch/` where every node's shell/tool action crosses before execution.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a deterministic pre-dispatch screen in the dispatch backend that canonicalizes each node's shell command and admits only writes inside the run dir and the node's declared worktree scope, escalating anything else to the operator lane (fail-closed abstain, never silent allow). Measure on a replay of recorded runs: out-of-scope commands blocked (seeded red-team cases) versus false blocks on a sample of green code-fix runs.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/ tool-call boundary - deterministic pre-execution policy gate
glm.rationale: The strongest structural answer to the state's broad-tool-surface gap with good numbers (85.6% F1 at 0.91% FPR), but interposing on every shell command of a coding agent invites false-positive friction on legitimate builds; start with the deterministic policy subset at dispatch.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/ - a deterministic pre-dispatch screen on the tool-call boundary
minimax.rationale: The state snapshot's tool-surface gap says placement is configurable and not enforced per node, and this closes that with an execute/ask/refuse rule that is deterministic rather than model-opinion: deterministic rule enforcement at the tool-call boundary reaches DSR 97.4-98.2% (residual ASR 0.6-3.1%), and a two-stage cascade cuts FPR from 34.1% to 1.9% while retaining 91.9-92.6% interception. It also gives the injection probe a place to land: a planted instruction that tries to write outside the run dir is refused by the screen rather than by a prompt.

ranked.technique: Scaffolded authorization-relation verification of code changes
ranked.mechanism: Broken access control is an authorization relation, not an input flow, so generic scanners and unstructured model review both miss it; a scaffolded check drives systematic relation extraction — subject, action, object, and the policy that should connect them — from the diff and its callsites, then verifies each extracted relation against the declared authorization model. The verdict is evidence-anchored: a relation that is underdetermined from the retrieved code is an abstention requiring more context, never a pass; a relation that lets a subject act outside its declared scope is a reject that blocks the change. Scaffolds (navigation, apply-feedback loops) are what make this tractable for models — single-turn prompting repairs far less. Caution: transaction-derived relation learning can hit 100% recall only with a high false-positive rate, so the gate must report precision honestly rather than optimize recall alone.
ranked.reported_results: CodeQL and Semgrep recall none of the broken-access-control cases; an unstructured agent on the same model recalls 3 (arxiv:2610.00977). Scaffolded repair: applicability 62.50% to 96.11% (+33.61 pp); Opus 4.8 repair rate 30.43% to 75.36%, within 3.63 pp of Claude Code's 78.99% (arxiv:2610.34290). Black-box BOLA relation learning: 100.00% recall, F1 56.63%, FPR 33.65% under controlled synthetic conditions; removing evidence quarantine or provenance independence raises unauthorized-relation pollution to 100.00% (arxiv:2611.00738).
ranked.miniork_surface: `code-fix verifier set` — a new security verifier beside `recipes/code-fix/verifiers/{test,typecheck,fallback_guard,metamorphic}.py`.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add an authorization-relation verifier to code-fix runs: when a diff touches auth-relevant paths (middleware, permission checks, object ownership), extract subject-action-object relations from the diff plus retrieved callsites and fail the gate on any relation that escapes the repo's declared authorization model, abstaining explicitly when the relation is underdetermined. Measure recall on seeded broken-access-control changes (where CodeQL/Semgrep recall zero) and false blocks on clean auth-touching diffs.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - authorization-relation verifier beside test/typecheck
glm.rationale: Broken access control is named in the open gap, and deterministic scanners recall none of it (CodeQL/Semgrep 0, bare agent 3), so scaffolded relation extraction with abstention fits the code-fix set - but black-box relation learning carries 33.65% FPR, so sequence it after the deterministic tiers and hold it to abstention on underdetermined relations.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - a new security verifier beside test, typecheck, fallback_guard, metamorphic
minimax.rationale: Broken access control is an authorization relation, and the evidence that generic scanners miss it is direct (CodeQL and Semgrep recall none of the cases; an unstructured agent on the same model recalls 3), which is precisely a gap in the snapshot's verifier set. It is next rather than now because the measured false-positive rate is high (FPR 33.65% at 100% recall under synthetic conditions) and the scaffolded relation extraction is a research-scale component.

ranked.technique: Tool-server gateway governance: content pinning, silent-drift re-verification, least-privilege permission registry
ranked.mechanism: Treat tool servers, skills, and their updates as a governed dependency layer: record a content hash and version at approval time, express permissions as a deny-by-default bounded registry (tool x scope), and re-run vetting whenever the bytes or advertised schema change - silent drift is the norm (51.1% of multi-version servers changed advertised tools, 40.6% silently), so yesterday's approval must never cover today's server. Bind what was audited to what executes, so a skill or tool whose content differs from the approved artifact is rejected at load. Accept a tool only while hash and permission entry match; reject on any delta; quarantine when the registry cannot decide. Scope tool exposure by retrieval so unvetted tools never enter context at all.
ranked.reported_results: 16.0% of 3,171 public agent setups carry a confirmed supply-chain defect: 9.8% install an unpinned MCP server, 3.1% pre-approve arbitrary execution behind scoped-looking grants, 3.8% ship a skill that pre-approves the shell (arxiv:2609.07360). 51.1% of multi-version MCP servers changed advertised tools between versions, 40.6% silently; silent-drift odds ratio 2.96 (arxiv:2609.14119). Permission-DNF registry: out-of-scope tool attempts 21.1% (152/720) to 0/720 (arxiv:2609.22573). SIGIL audit-runtime binding: strong detection across 1,023 in-the-wild skills, six attack types (arxiv:2605.05274). Retrieval-scoped tool exposure: 140.2k to 1.3k tool tokens in production (arxiv:2608.23992). Internet-scale assessment: 640 servers, 68 reportable vulnerabilities, 91.8% of audited servers lack OAuth (arxiv:2608.00150).
ranked.miniork_surface: MCP / tool surface (declarations, approvals, and dispatch), with lane config for provider endpoints.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Give mini-ork's MCP/tool declarations a lockfile - server id, content hash, version, and a per-tool permission entry captured at first vetting - and have dispatch refuse any tool whose live hash or advertised schema differs, routing it back to vetting. Measurement: instrument existing tool declarations for hash/schema drift across a month of runs and count drift events caught versus silently executed before the guard.

glm.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface declarations and dispatch (providers.yaml)
glm.rationale: Silent tool-server drift (51.1% changed advertised tools, 40.6% silently) is real but mini-ork's tool registry is first-party and versioned in-repo; adopt content pinning when an external tool surface appears.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface (declarations, approvals, and dispatch), with lane config for provider endpoints
minimax.rationale: A tool lockfile is the cheapest durable fix for the snapshot's unmeasured tool surface, and the evidence that yesterday's approval must not cover today's server is strong (51.1% of multi-version MCP servers changed advertised tools, 40.6% silently; permission-DNF took out-of-scope tool attempts from 21.1% to 0/720). It is next rather than now because the named holes are the verifier set and the injection probe, both of which this guards rather than fills.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: exfiltration through legitimate agent channels
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique — a perfectly behaved agent can still leak: malware with no direct internet access abuses legitimate LLM web-fetching as a courier (the model fetches attacker-constructed URLs that encode the secret), phishing-style page content drives agents into attacker-controlled login flows without task-specific assumptions, and a compromised inference server can encode payload bits in plausible token choices. Preventing behavior manipulation alone therefore gives false security against data theft. The implied rule is that egress is a sandbox property, not a model property: per-node deny-by-default egress allowlists, secret-bearing values kept out of untrusted-context prompts (only a minimal residual crosses), and sequential e-process monitoring of outbound content with anytime false-alarm control. Reject: egress outside the declared allowlist; abstain: flagged sequences halt for review.
ranked.reported_results: Covert exfiltration via legitimate fetching reaches 79.7% success across eleven open-parameter models with a real-world chatbot case study (arxiv:2610.01768); task-agnostic login-flow hijacking averages 86% end-to-end success across backbones and defenses (arxiv:2608.04741); an anytime-valid e-process detects weight exfiltration with sequential false-alarm control over unbounded horizons, with seed access determining attacker stealth (arxiv:2610.11843).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Enforce a per-node egress allowlist in the sandbox provider (deny-by-default destinations, flag URL-parameter encodings) and keep vault values out of untrusted-context node prompts, passing only the minimal residual. Measure: an LLMLeak-style constructed-URL fetch from a sandboxed node is blocked and raises an alert.

glm.rationale: Egress is a sandbox property, not a model property is the right rule for the state's tool-surface gap - covert exfiltration via legitimate fetch hit 79.7% - and default-deny egress belongs with G03-T02's sandbox enforcement rather than as a separate build.

minimax.landing_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox - default-deny egress allowlists, with vault values kept out of untrusted-context prompts
minimax.rationale: Covert exfiltration via legitimate fetching reaches 79.7% success across eleven open-parameter models and task-agnostic login-flow hijacking averages 86%, so a perfectly behaved agent can still leak and the control must be egress, not behavior. It is next because egress enforcement belongs in the sandbox providers, and it is the property the snapshot's 'nothing measures leakage' gap needs.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: covert, split-channel, and infrastructure side channels bypass conversational and output-only defenses
ranked.mechanism: CAUTION - a negative finding, not a defense: content inspection applied at the model's conversational surface or to final outputs is structurally evadable. Demonstrated bypasses: exfiltration disguised as legitimate retrieval, reversible context obfuscation that survives textual-similarity detection, request/disclosure split across two channels so single-context consent defenses never associate them, RL-crafted malicious tool descriptions that trick the agent into passing its own context, compromised runtime extensions encoding secrets into residual streams, relay prompt-cache identity pooling across tenants, and CPU-cache traces reconstructing local model outputs during detokenization. The design rule that survives: enforce at boundaries the attacker does not control - tool execution, network egress, provider selection - and never count an output filter or prompt-level guardrail as the exfiltration control. For mini-ork this argues for per-node network egress allowlists in the sandbox and direct pinned provider endpoints, rather than trusting output scanning or guardrail-style prompting to catch exfiltration.
ranked.reported_results: NeMo Guardrails v0.16.0 and LLM Guard v0.3.16 default configurations were bypassed at 81-87% by retrieval-disguised exfiltration, with 2-3 word backdoor triggers giving >96% ASR at <0.3% FPR (arxiv:2604.05432); reversible-obfuscation poisoning reached 58-100% ASR across three model families and three domains, dropping at most 10 percentage points under detection-based defenses (arxiv:2610.25937); split-channel attacks achieved 43.8-75.6% item-level leakage vs 1.9-3.0% for single-context attacks (arxiv:2609.14003); 5/5 tested LLM API gateways exposed cross-customer prompt-cache state, with 12/28 label namespaces (33.7% of volume) leaking via one provider path (arxiv:2608.17485); detokenization cache-trace attacks reconstructed semantically accurate outputs from real local agentic deployments (arxiv:2609.06674); RL-crafted malicious tool descriptions exfiltrated agent context and significantly outperformed prior malicious-tool attacks (arxiv:2608.27800).
ranked.miniork_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox (default-deny network egress per node), plus lane config (pin direct provider endpoints, refuse shared-credential relays)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Give each sandboxed node a default-deny egress allowlist - provider endpoints plus the sanctioned retrieval host only - and add a lane-config check that refuses relayed providers pooling upstream credentials. Measure by attempting an outbound connection to an arbitrary host from a test node: it must be blocked at the sandbox with the attempt recorded in the run's evidence ledger, not merely absent from the node's output.

glm.landing_surface: sandbox placement (default-deny egress) + lane config (pinned endpoints)
glm.rationale: The caution - output-only inspection evadable at 81-87% - argues for the same build as G08-T12 and G03-T02: default-deny egress and pinned endpoints, not more content inspection.

minimax.landing_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox (default-deny egress) plus lane config (pinned direct provider endpoints)
minimax.rationale: This is a negative finding that constrains design: output filters and prompt guardrails are bypassed at 81-87% by retrieval-disguised exfiltration, 5/5 tested LLM API gateways exposed cross-customer prompt-cache state, and detokenization cache-trace attacks reconstructed outputs from a real local deployment. The rule it yields - enforce at boundaries the attacker does not control, never count an output filter as the exfiltration control - is directly applicable and belongs with the egress work in G08-T12.

ranked.technique: Judge-validity discipline for LLM-scored security verdicts
ranked.mechanism: When LLM judges score attacks or findings, raw agreement is meaningless in high-base-rate regimes: most inputs already fail, so two judges agree ~85% while sharing almost no information (Cohen's kappa near zero). Score judge validity with kappa or classifier-independent agreement per regime, confirm success through judge-independent pathways (execution checks, deterministic oracles, provider exclusion), and separate headline from operationally actionable success. Sampled refusal is not robustness — probability mass on harmful continuations must be measured, not one sampled output. Accept a judge verdict only when its validity is established for that regime; abstain when base rates make the judge uninformative. Caution: validator agents are systematically optimistic and nonspecific, and released detectors are confidently wrong under attack shift.
ranked.reported_results: 80-87% pairwise judge agreement coexists with near-zero Cohen's kappa because 90-97% of inputs already fail (arxiv:2606.24589); adversarial camouflage cuts LLM drain-detection by 20 percentage points across 22 models, established via multi-path validation (arxiv:2609.14098); checklist-gated dual metrics expose a large gap between headline and operationally actionable attack success (arxiv:2607.11151); validator agents in multi-stage attack systems are evidence-grounded but nonspecific and overly optimistic (arxiv:2609.28572); prompt-injection detector confidence is content-keyed and a black-box rewriter manufactures confident misses on the most dangerous category (arxiv:2606.22659); bounded continuation analysis separates models that sampled-refusal ASR cannot distinguish (arxiv:2610.22754).
ranked.adoption_sketch: For every LLM-judged verdict already in the stack (gaming-scan annotations, reviewer scores), record judge-vs-oracle agreement and kappa on a seeded validation set in the evidence ledger, and require kappa above a floor before a judge-only verdict may block or promote anything. Measure: kappa of each judge against deterministic oracles on seeded evasions.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - judge-validity measurement
glm.rationale: Judge validity is measured by default since e9d14399 (oracle verdict kinds recorded); the kappa-vs-agreement point belongs in that report, not in a new mechanism.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - record judge-vs-oracle agreement and kappa per judge
minimax.rationale: This bounds every LLM-judged verdict mini-ork already relies on, and the evidence is unambiguous: 80-87% pairwise judge agreement coexists with near-zero Cohen's kappa because 90-97% of inputs already fail, so agreement in a high-base-rate regime carries no information. It matters most for the two-reviewer merge this run feeds, so it is next rather than now.

ranked.technique: Caution: plaintext API routers and proxies sit inside the dispatch path
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique: third-party API routers see every in-flight payload in plaintext, and no major provider or the current MCP specification deploys response signing, so a tool-call response's claimed origin is unverifiable. Measurement with researcher-controlled decoys found 9 of 428 commodity routers injecting malicious code into tool-call streams and 17 abusing exposed credentials. Client-side policy gates on returned tool calls block all naive injections at about 1% false positives and microsecond cost, but adaptive variants bypass them completely - the gate is a floor, not a boundary. Rule for lane config: only pinned, provider-owned endpoints; an unvetted proxy-shaped endpoint is rejected outright, never degraded to.
ranked.reported_results: 9 of 428 routers injected malicious code, 17 abused credentials; decoys attracted 2B billed tokens, 440 autonomous sessions, 99 leaked credentials (arxiv:2604.08407). Client-side policy gate blocks 100% of AC-1/AC-1.a samples at 1.0% FP and 2.3 microseconds median cost but is bypassed by 100% of adaptive samples; no deployed response-signing mechanism exists in provider tool-use APIs or MCP (arxiv:2604.08407).
ranked.miniork_surface: lane config - providers.yaml endpoint allowlisting and dispatch-path response validation.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Constrain providers.yaml to provider-owned base URLs with a config lint that rejects unknown hosts and proxy-shaped endpoints, and validate each returned tool call against the requested tool's schema before execution. Measurement: config-lint pass rate across existing setups, plus a planted router fixture serving an injected tool call that dispatch rejects 100% of the time.

glm.rationale: Endpoint pinning and refusing shared-credential relays is the actionable residue; the 9/428 malicious-router measurement describes commodity infrastructure mini-ork does not route through.

minimax.landing_surface: providers.yaml endpoint allowlisting and dispatch-path response validation
minimax.rationale: The measurement is uncomfortable and cheap to act on: 9 of 428 commodity routers injected malicious code into tool-call streams and 17 abused exposed credentials, with no deployed response-signing mechanism in any provider or MCP spec, so only pinned provider-owned endpoints plus per-call schema validation are admissible. It is S effort via config lint, and it hardens the dispatch path that the injection probe would attack, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Self-configuration containment floor: enforce limit-granting config at the write point
ranked.mechanism: Partition agent-editable configuration from limit-granting configuration (writable paths, allowed senders, auth, risk gates, frozen kernel paths) and enforce the boundary at the point of writing, inside the runtime. The caution this carries: prompt prohibitions stop only requests quoting the prohibition's own words, prompt-only policy permits most dangerous operations, and LLM policy gates are unstable — temperature-0 re-runs disagree, models block explicitly authorized actions, and an agentic enforcer underperforms a deterministic rule baseline. A deterministic check at the write point, by contrast, stops every protected write. Accept rule: a write to a limit-granting path is rejected mechanically regardless of the requester's phrasing; agent-editable config remains freely writable inside its floor. Signed, tamper-evident process attestations extend the same floor to the audit record.
ranked.reported_results: Prompt prohibitions stopped only requests using the prohibition's own words, while a check at the point of writing stopped every protected write (arxiv:2610.06274). Prompt-only baseline: 78.1% of dangerous operations permitted, 94.7% of bypass attempts succeeded; repeated same-case runs at temperature 0 agreed only 48.7-71.3% (arxiv:2609.38224). LLM authorization gates decide unevenly and unstably, and even block explicitly authorized actions; retrieved environment signals improve accuracy (arxiv:2610.16426). Agentic zero-trust enforcement reaches 95.0% accuracy where a deterministic rule baseline reaches 100% on the same set (arxiv:2610.05782).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend `config/kernel-frozen.yaml` to cover all limit-granting config (risk tiers, approval policy, gate registry, vault policy) and enforce it at the merge-path write point so a run that edits its own limits fails closed. Measure: attempts by an agent to widen its own gates across a suite of ordinary and adversarial requests — target zero successful protected writes.

glm.rationale: The repo integrity guard already enforces frozen kernel paths at the write point and heals rebates - the write-point enforcement result (every protected write stopped vs wording-only prohibitions) is the shipped mechanism.

minimax.landing_surface: repo integrity guard - config/kernel-frozen.yaml and mini_ork/gates/
minimax.rationale: Extending the shipped freeze to all limit-granting config (risk tiers, approval policy, gate registry, vault policy) and enforcing it at the merge-path write point is cheap, and the measured gap between prompt prohibitions and a write-point check is stark (a check at the point of writing stopped every protected write; prompt-only permitted 78.1% of dangerous operations with 94.7% bypass). It is next because the existing guard already covers the frozen kernel paths.

ranked.technique: Fixed-model baselines and operational evidence before architecture claims
ranked.mechanism: Holds the model fixed and runs the simplest capable harness repeatedly to establish a best-of-k baseline that any fancier architecture must beat before its gains are believed — published agent-architecture gains routinely confound model choice, harness choice, and selection over benchmarks (architecture-benchmark co-evolution). Deployment claims additionally require operational evidence — per-decision latency, cost, calibration, escalation behavior — not aggregate accuracy alone. Accept rule: an architecture or config change is credited only against a same-model, same-data baseline with the comparison declared up front; an unbaselined gain is an abstention. This is the evaluation-side complement to gaming scans: it audits the claim rather than the run.
ranked.reported_results: A plain Codex CLI agent with the model held fixed matches or exceeds published pentest-agent architectures on HackTheBox best-of-k, and security-focused prompting adds nothing (arxiv:2607.13085); a survey of 81 papers documents the architecture-benchmark co-evolution confound (arxiv:2607.02605); a role-and-evidence frame requires per-decision latency, cost, calibration and escalation reporting before LLMs enter fraud-detection workflows (arxiv:2607.13078).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Before adopting any new routing policy or provider claim in mini-ork, run a fixed-model best-of-k baseline through the existing lane and record it in the run ledger; promote only configs that beat it on the same fixtures. Measure: how many proposed config changes fail to beat their baseline, and the cost delta of those that do.

glm.rationale: Fixed-model baselines before architecture claims is good hygiene for the GRPO loop's own experiments; not a security-impact item.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config - fixed-model best-of-k baseline recorded in the run ledger
minimax.rationale: A plain Codex CLI agent with the model held fixed matches or exceeds published pentest-agent architectures on best-of-k, and the survey of 81 papers documents the architecture-benchmark co-evolution confound, so a same-model baseline is the honest control before crediting any routing or provider change. It is S effort and cheap, but it is an evaluation-side control rather than a hole-closer.

ranked.technique: Prompt-injection evasion of LLM telemetry interpretation (caution) with explanation-leak detection
ranked.mechanism: Caution: the telemetry an LLM security node interprets is attacker-controllable input. Adversarial log content - built from real attack traces via generic generation, refinement, and attack-specific optimization - flips the interpreter's verdict so malicious traces with clear IOCs are classified benign, at up to 60% attack success. The defensive lead from the same work: the manipulated model's own explanations leak manipulation indicators, so scanning the judge's reasoning for tells is a detection channel. Rule: any pipeline where an LLM reads adversary-influenced text must quarantine that text (structured, delimited, provenance-tagged) and treat verdicts over injected content as untrusted; a verdict that references instructions found in the evidence is itself an incident.
ranked.reported_results: Adversarial log evasion classifies malicious traces with clear IOCs as benign with attack success up to 60% (average score 5.12) (arxiv:2607.24174); the same work finds the LLM's explanations leak manipulation indicators usable for detection (arxiv:2607.24174).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Treat run artifacts consumed by LLM judge nodes as untrusted input: intake them structured and delimited (quoted evidence blocks, length-capped) instead of raw inlines, and scan the judge's explanation for references to instructions that originate in the evidence. Measure by planting an instruction inside a test artifact - the structured intake plus tell-scan must flag it while a raw-inline baseline run complies.

glm.rationale: The caution - LLM nodes reading attacker-influenced text get flipped (up to 60%) - lands on the same intake-labeling fix as G07-T09 and G08-T08.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - structured, delimited, length-capped intake for artifacts consumed by LLM judge nodes
minimax.rationale: Adversarial log content flips an LLM interpreter's verdict up to 60% of the time, and the same work finds the manipulated model's explanations leak manipulation indicators - so structured intake plus a tell-scan is a concrete, cheap control for the judge surfaces mini-ork already has (the two impact reviewers of this very recipe). It is next because it is S effort and protects an existing decision point.

ranked.technique: Caution: setup documentation and config are an execution channel (inspection-execution gap)
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique: the files an agent reads at setup are an attack channel. Payloads embedded in README examples, requirements, Makefile targets, config templates, and skill documentation bypass explicit-instruction defenses entirely (0% blocked) at 11.6-33.5% success; conjunctive payloads that activate only under a specific wrapper-plus-config combination evade per-component scans; and Python may execute a substituted bytecode cache while scanners read benign source, so inspected bytes must be proven identical to executed bytes. Intake must therefore treat repository prose as untrusted input: anchor any install or setup action to a reviewed, pinned manifest and reject doc-sourced install commands that deviate from it; a payload whose only provenance is prose is rejected, not executed.
ranked.reported_results: DDIPE: 11.6%-33.5% bypass across four frameworks and five models while explicit instruction attacks achieve 0% under strong defenses; 2.5% evade static analysis and alignment (arxiv:2604.03081). Setup-instruction poisoning: 11.6-33.5% success under strong agent defenses across 12 scenarios (arxiv:2607.15143). Conjunctive poisoning activates deterministically across fifteen LLM/VLM pipeline systems (arxiv:2608.15913).
ranked.miniork_surface: kickoff and intake guard - mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py and mini_ork/intake/.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Teach the intake guard to inventory every install or exec command a run could source from repository prose (README, Makefile, requirements, skill docs) and diff it against the pinned manifest, failing closed on unmatched install commands and on any bytecode cache that differs from its source. Measurement: run the guard over fixtures carrying doc-embedded payloads in the DDIPE pattern and require 100% flagging plus a zero-false-positive pass over clean repos.

glm.rationale: Supports treating kickoff and README prose as untrusted (the state's agent-inputs-are-trusted gap), but the buildable piece is subsumed by the implement-now injection probe (G02-T10) plus intake labeling.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py and mini_ork/intake/
minimax.rationale: The setup-documentation channel is one of the two concrete carriers of the injection hole (README, Makefile, requirements and config templates are read before any instruction defense engages; 11.6%-33.5% bypass where explicit-instruction attacks are blocked 0%), and the intake guard is the natural home. Evidence is moderate and the fix (pin installs to a reviewed manifest) is narrower than the general injection probe, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Closed-loop red teaming with reusable attack skills and deterministic oracles
ranked.mechanism: Run adversarial pressure as a closed loop: an attacker proposes probes, a deterministic oracle scores outcomes (filesystem/service/gate state, never a judge), failed trajectories are diagnosed into named strategies, and strategies accumulate as reusable, composable skills across campaigns instead of per-run prompt search. Diversity must be rewarded explicitly (coarse-to-fine diversity rewards, quality-diversity archives, atomic-strategy decomposition) or attackers collapse onto near-duplicate patterns and under-report risk. Accept findings only with oracle-verified success recorded with evidence and source; treat strategy coverage as a first-class metric alongside success rate.
ranked.reported_results: Surrogate-guided jailbreak fuzzing attains 90% ASR with >70% fewer queries and 84% ASR on GPT-4o at 25 queries (arxiv:2603.23269); MDP-formulated multi-turn attacking improves ASR@5 by up to 53% (arxiv:2610.31937); self-play red teaming at RL-post-training compute scale finds more successful attacks than human red-teamers and its attacks were used to adversarially train a production model (arxiv:2607.26115); autoresearch discovers attack algorithms outperforming all 30+ existing methods (arxiv:2603.24511); test-time training of the attacker consolidates per-victim signal into attacker weights instead of discarding it (arxiv:2610.05282).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend gaming scan's fixtures into a small attack-skill library (test tampering, verifier stubbing, metric gaming, scope escape) applied in a loop against a sacrificial run, each scored by deterministic oracles mini-ork already ships (pytest exit codes, gate exit codes). Measure: distinct evasion classes found per campaign and their fix rate, vs one-shot static scanning.

glm.rationale: The reusable attack-skill loop with deterministic oracles is how to scale the injection probe after G02-T10 proves out; oracle-verified findings only is already mini-ork doctrine.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - an attack-skill library scored by deterministic oracles (pytest exit codes, gate exit codes)
minimax.rationale: mini-ork already has deterministic oracles (test and gate exit codes), so a closed attacker loop needs no new judging surface, and the reuse-across-campaigns property is the real win: self-play red teaming found more successful attacks than human red-teamers. It is next because it multiplies the value of the gates above it rather than closing a hole itself.

ranked.technique: LLM-synthesized reproduction harnesses with deterministic mutation (fail-to-pass confirmation)
ranked.mechanism: For each confirmed-hypothesis finding, an LLM synthesizes a parameterized reproduction artifact - a fuzz harness, test, or input template - grounded by code navigation, and a deterministic fuzzer or mutator explores only the uncertain parameters; the finding is accepted when the artifact triggers the failure on the vulnerable code (crash, sanitizer report, assertion) and stops triggering after the fix. Harness synthesis is decomposed by dataflow (functions sharing state get one state-machine harness, not per-function ones) and directed at coverage gaps reported by the build rather than generated blind. The caution keeps the loop honest: generator-based fuzzing matched agent-based fuzzing on deep-path exploration, so the deterministic mutation loop - not agent iterations - carries the exploration. Anchored on the executed fail-to-pass transition, the same anchor as a regression test.
ranked.reported_results: LLM-synthesized parameterized harnesses reproduce 78% of 100 KernelCTF cases (mean 2.9h) and 73% on SyzDirect, outperforming directed greybox fuzzing (arxiv:2609.23889); dataflow-aggregated state-machine harness generation reaches 3.07x/1.71x/4.26x branch coverage over prior generators and finds 7 new library bugs (arxiv:2607.07007); coverage-gap-directed generation reaches 68.13% GCC and 69.11% LLVM coverage in 72 hours (arxiv:2607.15762); documentation-mined API-sequence fuzzing finds 31 zero-days across PDF readers (arxiv:2608.06641); logic-shifting SQL mutation finds 64 bugs with 9 CVEs assigned (arxiv:2602.19490); caution - agent-based fuzzing shows no advantage over generator-based coverage-guided mutation on deep paths (arxiv:2604.01442).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a security_repro verifier next to metamorphic.py: for each confirmed finding, an LLM emits a parameterized pytest/harness, the runner mutates the uncertain parameters, and the finding's gate weight requires fail-to-pass against the fix. Measure the share of confirmed findings that yield a working repro artifact and the flakiness rate of those artifacts across re-runs.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - synthesized reproduction harnesses
glm.rationale: Synthesized parameterized harnesses reproduce 78% of KernelCTF cases and are the scalable version of G07-T01's exploit oracle for memory-unsafe targets; heavy machinery, right after the paired oracle proves out on Python-shaped repos.

minimax.landing_surface: recipes/code-fix/verifiers/ - a security_repro verifier whose gate weight requires a fail-to-pass transition
minimax.rationale: LLM-synthesized parameterized harnesses reproduce 78% of 100 KernelCTF cases and dataflow-aggregated harness generation finds 7 new library bugs, and the honest null is preserved (agent-based fuzzing showed no advantage over generator-based mutation, so the deterministic mutation loop carries the exploration). It is next because it is the executable evidence behind the paired exploit oracle I rank in the now-list.

ranked.technique: Unforgeable origin binding for instructions, tool parameters, and decoded content
ranked.mechanism: Every instruction and every value that reaches a state-changing tool parameter carries a cryptographically checkable origin; a value is admitted only if it traces unforgeably to the user/kickoff, a source the kickoff explicitly named, or run-produced artifacts signed at write and verified at read. Decode-time binding tags content the moment a tool decodes it (image, archive, document), so steganographic or cross-modal carriers inherit the untrusted label regardless of carrier format, and a rewording-invariance property keeps admission decisions stable under paraphrase. Reject rule: a value with no verifiable origin is barred from privileged parameters (parameter poisoning that preserves the intended tool call but swaps an argument is exactly what action-level checks miss). Anchored on signatures and taint propagation, deterministic end to end.
ranked.reported_results: ASR held to 1.6-2.6% across four agent models at 82-100% clean utility, with stated no-attacker-origin and rewording-invariance guarantees (arxiv:2608.27496); steganographic cross-modal leaks fall from 100% undefended to 0% under decode-time provenance binding where keyword and regex scanners leak 62.5% (arxiv:2610.31974); per-boundary intent-plus-integrity enforcement with O(log(M+N)) deterministic overhead (arxiv:2602.10465); parameter-poisoning attack success reaches 93.06% unprotected, motivating task-aware parameter authorization (arxiv:2611.04673); signed memory entries verified at retrieval prevent undetected poisoning (arxiv:2611.13696).
ranked.miniork_surface: artifact contract — declared ports, run-local manifests, transforms, and visibility limits
ranked.adoption_sketch: Sign run manifests and artifacts at write time, verify signatures at node input, and extend the artifact contract so a value may parameterize a publish, vault, or shell effect only when its manifest trace ends at kickoff or a declared input. Test: plant an instruction inside a retrieved evidence file and assert it cannot originate a vault read or a publisher argument, with benign runs unaffected.

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - signed origins for instructions and parameters
glm.rationale: Run-local manifests ship in the artifact contract; binding values to signed origins (ASR held at 1.6-2.6%) is the natural extension once dispatch signs what it writes.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - sign run manifests and artifacts at write time, verify at node input, and bar unverifiable values from privileged parameters
minimax.rationale: Origin binding is the deterministic version of the injection defense and the parameter-poisoning numbers justify it (93.06% attack success unprotected; a value with no verifiable origin must be barred from privileged parameters). It is next rather than now because signing artifacts at write and verifying at read across every node input is L effort and the snapshot's artifact contract already declares ports, which makes it an extension rather than a new substrate.

ranked.technique: Approval bound to the exact executed effect: one-use, digest-bound, transitive closure
ranked.mechanism: Bind each human approval to the full transitive effect closure of what it authorizes, not to the entry invocation: predict workflow effects (package lifecycle hooks, delegated and MCP calls, CI triggers) at approval time, freeze the proposal as a digest, and make the authorization single-use and consumed at the executor's linearization point. The accept rule revalidates the exact approved request and current state at commit; a retry, replan, or delegation that re-executes under a fresh token id is refused as semantic replay. Durable authorization-consumption state is kept outside the model so stale or re-issued approvals cannot inherit an earlier decision. Caution: measured approval records systematically omit transitive effects, and token-binding defenses block some laundering modes but not scope or argument laundering — binding to the realized effect remains the unsolved core.
ranked.reported_results: 40 of 111 approval records have a nonempty unreported-effect residual across nine mechanism classes; transitive-effect predictor attains 0.926 macro recall / 0.941 macro precision (arxiv:2609.28586). Bound-Gap Rate 1.00 for Scope and Temporal laundering modes; credential-field token binding blocks some modes but not scope/argument laundering (arxiv:2609.38983). Sandbox pre-execution effects report (median 0.9 KB vs 62.5 KB raw trace, 99.4% smaller) yields lowest harmful-outcome rate 6.7% vs 14.8-21.2% for six existing systems; hidden-harm 6.9-7.8% vs 35.3-94.1% for prior systems (arxiv:2610.40753). Under complete proposer compromise, 44/44 attacks blocked and 44/44 legitimate proposals admitted; all 210 provider-contract trials match predeclared outcomes (arxiv:2608.21159). Semantic replay observed across 10,152 agent trajectories (arxiv:2608.01710).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend merge approvals to record the effect closure — patch id plus touched paths plus the CI jobs the patch triggers — and make each approval single-use per patch id so a re-issued or mutated patch re-asks. Measure by sampling completed merges and computing the approval-record vs executed-effect residual (the laundering gap); the predictor-style closure check should drive it toward zero.

glm.rationale: mini-ork approvals are already digest-bound to the head patch id and consumed under a merge lock; transitive-effect prediction is the only new part, and mini-ork approvals govern diffs, not interactive tool graphs.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/gates/merge_approval.py, config/risk-tiers.yaml
minimax.rationale: The snapshot binds approvals to a head patch id, and this tightens that to the transitive effect closure (patch id plus touched paths plus triggered CI jobs), made single-use per patch id so a re-issued or mutated patch re-asks; the evidence shows 40 of 111 approval records carry an unreported-effect residual and semantic replay across 10,152 trajectories. It hardens an existing gate rather than filling either named hole, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Sequence-level authorization consistency and replay-resistant consumption
ranked.mechanism: Per-call authorization misses sequence-level excess: enforce behavioral properties over the execution trace, not just each request. A deterministic monitor (reference monitor, compiled temporal contract, or capability-mark supervisor) holds the session's authorization boundary as state — marks are granted, spent, and refused when preconditions are unmet or already consumed, regardless of the request's wording. The accept rule is trace-relative: a call is admissible only if the sequence so far, including approvals already consumed and budgets already spent, leaves the boundary intact; individually valid requests that compose into a harmful pattern are rejected. Typed-return provenance extends this to egress: a target value is admitted only if it arrived in a typed field from a read-only tool or a fixed delegation rule, and a deterministic record of what was consumed defeats semantic replay across retries and replanning.
ranked.reported_results: No missed-block cases on 1,248 TraceBench workflows where the strongest baseline misses 509 of 1,008 oracle-BLOCK; 92.8% block recall vs 68.8% baseline on blind LLM plans (arxiv:2609.23498). AgentDojo compromise drops from 33.0% to 0.0% with utility rising 46.7% to 63.3%; ASB direct injection blocked in 1,200 of 1,200 cases (arxiv:2608.22868). Attack success confined to 9.09-15.03% from a raw 33.5-49.7% at 98.7% clean-task success; 86.2% of L1 events close without a provider call (arxiv:2608.21101). Mean in-scope ASR .007 under a released RL attacker (arxiv:2611.07222). LTLf contracts compiled to automata match SOTA LLM-judge and rule-based guardrail baselines with deterministic reproducible verdicts and orders-of-magnitude lower per-call latency (arxiv:2609.18128).
ranked.miniork_surface: `evidence ledger and traces` — run transcripts consumed by a deterministic sequence gate at the dispatch boundary.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Replay each run's transcript through a deterministic sequence policy (allowed node-type transitions; one approval consumed exactly once; per-run egress budget) and block the dispatching node on violation. Measure on recorded transcripts seeded with drift cases (replayed approvals, out-of-order gates, repeated effect): drift caught vs missed, with zero false blocks on compliant runs.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger - deterministic sequence gate over run transcripts
glm.rationale: Trace-relative authorization (no missed blocks on 1,248 TraceBench workflows) needs a compiled property set and marks - a clean extension of run transcripts, but the properties only matter once per-node authorization exists at all.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - run transcripts consumed by a deterministic sequence gate at the dispatch boundary
minimax.rationale: Sequence-level enforcement catches harmful compositions that per-call authorization misses (no missed-block cases on 1,248 TraceBench workflows; AgentDojo compromise 33.0% to 0.0%), and replay-resistant consumption fits mini-ork's existing approval model. It is watch because it needs a compiled temporal contract or equivalent, which is a build rather than a verifier node, and it is one step removed from the named holes.

ranked.technique: Specification-to-checklist agentic auditing and formal rule-checking of agent prompts
ranked.mechanism: Convert the governing specification - a threat model for an audit, or the operating rules in a recipe/system prompt - into a machine-readable checklist of atomic checkable items, then anchor audits to it: every finding must map to a specific checklist item (unmapped findings are rejected as out-of-scope) and every item receives an explicit checked/failed/not-applicable verdict. For agent and recipe prompts, formal rule representations systematically expose contradictions between rules, authority-confusion ambiguities, and exploitable instruction patterns that prose review normalizes away. The dominant invalid-finding source is threat-model misalignment, so checklist-to-source alignment is verified before findings count. Anchored on the written specification, making each audit step auditable item by item - the same shape as kickoff Done-When criteria, extended to security.
