ranked.reported_results: Checklist reuse across similar systems retains 76.5% of valid findings, and 56.8% of invalid findings trace to threat-model misalignment (arxiv:2602.07513); formal rule-checking of 23 production system prompts (including Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI) yields 152 findings with 89% vendor agreement and 19 production prompt changes (arxiv:2603.08993); an 18-class domain vulnerability taxonomy as analysis context recovers up to 76% of known weakness locations where rule-based tools match ~none (arxiv:2609.09386).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Have mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py emit the security checklist from the kickoff's numbered constraints and require the final verifier to map every security finding to a checklist item id (unmapped = rejected); separately, run a contradiction and authority-ambiguity lint over recipe prompts using a formal rule representation. Measure the invalid-finding share (findings a human marks out-of-scope) before and after checklist anchoring.

glm.rationale: Formal rule-checking found real defects in 23 production prompts (89% vendor agreement); a one-time audit of mini-ork's own recipe prompts is cheap and useful but is not the runtime security hole.

minimax.landing_surface: kickoff and intake guard - emit the security checklist from numbered constraints and require findings to map to a checklist item
minimax.rationale: Formal rule-checking of 23 production system prompts yielded 152 findings with 89% vendor agreement and 19 production prompt changes, and 56.8% of invalid findings trace to threat-model misalignment, so anchoring every security finding to a checklist item is the same shape as the shipped kickoff Done-When criteria. It is next because it constrains the new verifier's output rather than detecting a defect itself.

ranked.technique: Trajectory-conditioned compromise detection with non-decaying loop state
ranked.mechanism: Detects compromise, drift, and distributed attacks that are invisible at any single step by monitoring invariants over whole multi-turn trajectories instead of re-initializing per node turn. Two directly implementable pieces: a deterministic behavioral invariant — data recalled into context must be sent to its declared destination before unrelated actions — checked over the transcript, with a prefix-only variant that supports real-time blocking; and a non-decaying per-run safety state carried across node boundaries, because monitors defined over a single trajectory provably cannot distinguish jointly indistinguishable inner observations regardless of monitor capacity, while distinguishing outer evidence enables perfect detection. Kill-chain canaries complement this by tracking a planted cryptographic token through propagation stages (exposed, persisted, relayed, executed), replacing a binary injection-success verdict with stage-level localization. Accept = invariant holds and cumulative state below threshold; block = invariant break, stage transition, or threshold crossing; abstain = transcript coverage missing, treated as a hold. Caution: safeguards that reset each trajectory are a composition failure, not a tuning problem.
ranked.reported_results: A recall-before-send transition invariant separates honest from compromised agents at high AUC, a stronger overdetermined classifier is near-perfect and stable across models, and a prefix-only variant supports real-time blocking (arxiv:2606.30566); kill-chain canary tracking localizes model resistance to different stages of injection propagation rather than a binary success metric (arxiv:2603.28013).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a transcript invariant checker to the run's verify stage — any artifact read into a node's context must appear in that node's declared output before unrelated side effects — plus a per-run cumulative risk counter that is not reset between nodes. Measurement: a seeded poisoned-observation run is localized to the hijacked step, with the false-block rate measured over clean runs.

glm.rationale: Deterministic transcript invariants (recall-before-send) are a promising cheap monitor, but the AUC results are on their own task mix; pilot after the injection probe defines the traces.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - a transcript invariant plus a per-run cumulative risk counter not reset between nodes
minimax.rationale: A recall-before-send transition invariant separates honest from compromised agents at high AUC and context-isolated verification reduces contamination 20-79%, and a per-run state that does not reset between nodes is the piece the snapshot's per-node verifier design lacks. It is next because it is instrumentation over traces that only exist once the security check and probe are producing them.

ranked.technique: Trace-based post-injection containment scoring and trajectory localization
ranked.mechanism: Terminal pass/fail is not a sufficient statistic for runtime safety: runs with identical zero-committed-harm endpoints differ in propagation, recovery, and authorized-action completion, and most unsafe runs still complete their task. Score each run from its trace on separately reported dimensions — endpoint policy compliance, logged propagation, recovery, and authorized structured-action completion — and localize where an injection entered and which steps it hijacked using trajectory-level classifiers that label every step benign, injection point, hijacked, or failed injection. Trusted-ledger and tool-boundary containment complete far more authorized work than taint-only containment. Accept: clean trace on all dimensions; reject: endpoint policy breach; abstain: terminal success with an anomalous trajectory routes to review rather than promotion.
ranked.reported_results: All 600 matched taint-only versus intent-aware pairs show the same zero committed-harm yet 73.5% differ in trajectory or utility; taint-only containment completes 0.1642 of authorized tainted workflows versus 0.8567 for trusted-ledger and 0.9233 for tool-boundary baselines (arxiv:2607.23999); 66.22% of runs are unsafe yet complete, so task completion cannot establish safety, with 68.0% of triggered cases producing prespecified unsafe signals (arxiv:2607.27294); a dual-head trajectory transformer reaches trajectory F1 0.983, exact injection-point recovery 98.7%, and hijacked-span IoU 0.979, with zero flags on 218 resisted attacks and 2.9% on hard negatives (arxiv:2609.10892).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend final verify to emit the four containment dimensions per run instead of a single pass flag, diffing the post-exposure trace against the pre-committed plan and flagging step-level anomalies. Measure: on an injected fixture run, containment divergence is visible even when the terminal verdict is pass.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - containment scoring
glm.rationale: Multi-dimensional containment scoring is post-hoc analysis richness; the publish gate needs binary fail-closed verdicts, which the tripwire and verifier provide.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - emit the four containment dimensions per run instead of a single pass flag
minimax.rationale: All 600 matched taint-only versus intent-aware pairs show the same zero committed-harm yet 73.5% differ in trajectory or utility, and 66.22% of runs are unsafe yet complete, so a terminal pass flag is not a sufficient statistic for a run that was injected. It is next because it is the reporting shape for the probe, and it needs the trace instrumentation to exist.

ranked.technique: Agentic authoring of executable detectors, refined against data
ranked.mechanism: An LLM agent writes the detector itself as a small executable artifact - physical residuals, behavioral rules, detection queries - and every candidate is refined against normal operating data on an evaluation workbench before deployment; the deployed artifact is deterministic, human-readable, and runs in milliseconds. Because detection and explanation are the same object, explanation fidelity holds by construction instead of by post-hoc rationalization, and false positives feed rule co-evolution. Accept rule: a candidate deploys only if it beats baselines on the bench. Cautions: agents that write detectors from a description alone, without data-grounded refinement, lose up to 0.28 F1, and automated quality metrics correlate with but do not replace expert judgment.
ranked.reported_results: F1 0.878 on BATADAL vs 0.504 for the strongest of six statistical/deep baselines, with every detected attack attributed to the attacked component (arxiv:2611.11009); detection-vs-explanation F1 error reduced 5.7x-47x versus anomaly baselines at 7.8 Gbps and 3.1 us median per-packet overhead (arxiv:2610.38890); automated detection-quality metrics correlate with practitioner judgment at Spearman rho=0.64 (p<0.002), though exclusion parity stays at 8.9% (arxiv:2603.25930).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Have an implementer node draft - and a deterministic bench refine against a labeled replay corpus - one small security verifier for the code-fix set (today it checks tests/types/lint and no security property), shipped as an executable rule that is its own explanation and adopted only if it beats the current heuristic on the corpus. Measure precision/recall on the replay corpus versus the shipped heuristic, with the rule readable on one screen.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - agentic authoring of deterministic detectors
glm.rationale: Agentic authoring of executable detectors is the same shape as G05-T08 (rules refined against data, deterministic deployment) - build that one for code surfaces.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - an agentic node drafts a small executable security verifier, refined against a labeled replay corpus
minimax.rationale: Detection and explanation becoming the same executable artifact is an attractive property (F1 0.878 on BATADAL versus 0.504 for the strongest statistical baseline), and the refinement-against-data step is what prevents the failure the paper measures (descriptions alone lose up to 0.28 F1). It is next because it competes with the deterministic rule-pack route in G05-T08 and should follow whichever lands.

ranked.technique: Task-necessity and contextual-integrity gating of artifact and secret access
ranked.mechanism: A node may only pull an artifact or secret its declared task actually requires (minimum-necessary): access requests are checked against the task declaration at port-binding time, before execution, in the spirit of contextual integrity where the accept rule is (attribute, recipient, purpose) rather than mere identity. It blocks out-of-context disclosure - data flowing to a recipient or purpose its source did not sanction - including the majority failure mode where the agent completes the task successfully while leaking. Enforcement is deterministic and pre-execution; refusals are not counted as evidence of safety, since agents that refuse nevertheless leak in a large share of cases. Anchored on measured contextual-integrity violation rates in enterprise retrieval workflows and on recipient-and-inference flow control that cuts failures by half or more at bounded utility cost.
ranked.reported_results: Recipient-and-inference IFC reduced step-level privacy failures by 53-80% at a model-dependent utility cost, out of 87 failures observed in 240 evaluated steps (67 on steps where the agent completed the task) (arxiv:2610.40714); context-based mitigations cut engaged leakage by 33-36pp while raising utility 16-23pp, and 41.9% of refusing agents still leaked within the interaction (arxiv:2606.23189); frontier models violated contextual integrity at 15.8-50.9% with leakage up to 26.7% in dense-retrieval enterprise workflows, and neither scale nor reasoning depth fixed it (arxiv:2604.21308).
ranked.miniork_surface: artifact contract (docs/architecture/artifact-graph.md) - extend declared ports and visibility limits with a task-necessity check at port binding
ranked.adoption_sketch: At dispatch, validate each node's input manifest against its task declaration: an input port requesting an artifact whose sensitivity class is not justified by the declared task fails closed before the node runs. Measure by auditing existing recipes for over-broad ports (nodes reading a whole run dir when they need one file), then verifying the gate blocks a synthetic over-reaching node while leaving legitimate runs green.

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - task-necessity check at port binding
glm.rationale: Minimum-necessary access at port-binding time extends the artifact contract's declared ports (53-80% step-level failure reduction), but the measured utility costs mean it needs tuning per recipe.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - a task-necessity check at port binding against declared ports and visibility limits
minimax.rationale: Frontier models violated contextual integrity at 15.8-50.9% with leakage up to 26.7% in dense-retrieval workflows, and 41.9% of refusing agents still leaked, so a pre-execution minimum-necessary check at port binding is the right control. It is next because it extends a shipped surface (declared ports and visibility limits) but needs each recipe's ports to carry a task declaration, which is a cross-recipe cost.

ranked.technique: Embedding-store confidentiality: stored vectors are recoverable text
ranked.mechanism: Treat stored embeddings and vector indices as recoverable text, not opaque identifiers. Inversion attacks reconstruct source text from commercial embedding APIs at meaningful exact-match rates; black-box (query, top-k) observation pairs suffice to invert retrieval-system embeddings without model access; and a curious user holding a few hundred aligned text-embedding pairs recovers the original vectors behind geometric access-control transformations - policy isolation without confidentiality, plus policy-membership leakage from the geometry itself. The control is access boundary and retention policy: the semantic memory index inherits the same visibility limits and per-node scoping as raw run text, and embedding egress to third-party embedder APIs is logged as content egress. CAUTION: this is attack evidence establishing the boundary, not a measured defense gain.
ranked.reported_results: 47.4% exact-match inversion of health-related instructions and 24.5% of general instructions for text-embedding-3-small, with BERTScore F1 > 87 for every prose category and embedder tested (arxiv:2611.05716); original embeddings recoverable from a few hundred aligned pairs, and policy-dependent geometry leaked policy membership even when unauthorized retrieval was prevented (arxiv:2611.14061); black-box embedding inversion from (query, top-k) observation pairs succeeded without white-box access (arxiv:2607.01276); white-box inversion reached 0.8838 token accuracy on boundary activations of LLaMA-65B (arxiv:2607.22695).
ranked.miniork_surface: real sibling of the artifact contract and evidence ledger: the semantic memory index (mini_ork/memory/semantic.py, MO_EMBED_PROVIDER embedder registry)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Apply the artifact contract's visibility limits to the embedding store - an embed written from a node scoped to secret-bearing artifacts is not retrievable by lower-visibility nodes - and record embedder API calls in the evidence ledger as content egress. Measure that a scratch node whose visibility excludes a secret-bearing artifact cannot retrieve it via semantic search, and that embedder egress appears in the ledger.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/memory/semantic.py - access boundary and retention limits on the embedding index
glm.rationale: Semantic memory ships (MO_EMBED_PROVIDER) and embeddings invert (47.4% exact-match) - access and retention limits on the index are a real but contained hardening once memory holds anything sensitive.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/memory/semantic.py, MO_EMBED_PROVIDER embedder registry - apply the artifact contract's visibility limits to the embedding store
minimax.rationale: Embeddings are recoverable text (47.4% exact-match inversion of health-related instructions and 24.5% of general instructions), so the semantic memory index must inherit the shipped visibility limits and per-node scoping, and embedder API calls must be logged as content egress. It is next because it extends a shipped sibling surface and is a boundary property rather than a detector, but the exposure is real today.

ranked.technique: Contamination and leakage auditing with isolation re-scoring
ranked.mechanism: Detects when a benchmark or its answers were seen in training, or when test items leak into train splits, so a passing score is memorization rather than capability. Evidence consumed: item text and code (self-referential probes, membership inference over similarity/functional correctness/embeddings), semantics-preserving mutations, and publication dates for temporal splits. Accept/reject rule: re-score under strict isolation (cross-dataset, content-aware dedup, post-cutoff-only) and report both numbers; a claim that materially changes under isolation is rejected as contaminated, and where probing is impossible the honest output is an abstention, not the headline number. Caution: file-hash dedup misses distinct inputs that render identically, and most contaminated samples show no usable memorization signal — absence of a leakage signal is not proof of cleanliness.
ranked.reported_results: Known leaked APPS samples inflated StarCoder-7B pass@1 by 4.9x, caught by membership inference (arxiv:2609.09865); strict cross-dataset isolation drops mean Recall@1 from 54.3% to 40.3% (Hedges' g = 0.94) (arxiv:2610.33592); content deduplication cuts malware-as-image accuracy by up to 8 points top-1 / 15 points macro-F1 (arxiv:2610.39351); up to 23% invalid labels and near-zero MCC after dataset cleanup across 770 published runs (arxiv:2611.06373).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a contamination pass over mini-ork's own regression corpus in gaming_scan: content-dedup verifier cases by normalized-code hash (not filename) and date-stamp every new case so corpus growth is auditable against model cutoffs. Measure: duplicate/near-duplicate cases removed and the delta in verifier verdicts before/after dedup.

glm.rationale: Contamination auditing is benchmark-shaped; mini-ork scores real work on operator repos, and its learning loop trains on outcomes, not public answer keys.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - contamination pass over mini-ork's own regression corpus
minimax.rationale: Known leaked samples inflated pass@1 by 4.9x and strict cross-dataset isolation dropped mean Recall@1 from 54.3% to 40.3%, so content-dedup by normalized code hash plus date-stamping is a real audit of the corpus the new security verifier will be measured against. It is watch because it protects the benchmark rather than the running system, and absence of a leakage signal is not proof of cleanliness.

ranked.technique: Assume-compromise OS-level sandboxing with measured layer attribution
ranked.mechanism: Confine the agent's execution with kernel-enforced boundaries (microVM, namespaces/cgroups/seccomp, eBPF reference monitors, copy-on-write workspace clones) designed on the premise that the model is already compromised and cannot itself be a security boundary. The sandbox holds no plaintext credentials; in-sandbox operations are auto-allowed while host-mutating, credential, or cross-org actions escalate — so protection survives full agent compromise. Accept/reject is enforced structurally at the OS layer regardless of what the model is persuaded to do. Layer-attribution ablation is part of the technique: measure how much protection each layer contributes, because removing the confinement layer flips payloads from refused to executed. Caution: escape benchmarks show leading agents compromise nested sandboxes when real vulnerabilities are present, and no publicly described system satisfies all five derived containment requirements.
ranked.reported_results: Effective attack success falls from 98.3% under direct execution to 7.7% deployed; two variants differing only by sandboxing differ 30.8% vs 7.7% (the final-stage reduction is attributable to the OS sandbox); prompt-only baseline permitted 78.1% of dangerous operations with 94.7% bypass success (arxiv:2609.38224). Attack success 100.0% to 0.0% on macOS and Linux with confirmation prompts reduced 94.19-99.88%; 1,000-file workspace cloned in 6.3ms (arxiv:2611.08516). ~5% of container-sandbox disk usage and 25% of environment-preparation time (arxiv:2602.11210). All 19 behavioral security properties pass 30/30 runs (arxiv:2609.38248). 15 leading agents compromise both nested sandboxes when vulnerabilities are present (arxiv:2603.02277). No publicly described system satisfies all five containment requirements (arxiv:2604.23425).
ranked.miniork_surface: `sandbox placement and per-node sandbox` — container/remote node providers, per-node sandbox profiles.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Give every implementer/verifier node a per-node sandbox profile (seccomp/namespace or the existing container provider) with zero vault credentials mounted by default; credentials are injected only into nodes whose artifact-contract port declares egress. Measure: an escape-attempt replay suite blocked (target near 100%) plus the utility delta (green-gate pass rate) on unchanged code-fix runs.

glm.rationale: Placement is configurable but not enforced (state: no test asserts a node could not reach outside the workspace), and the 98.3% to 7.7% deployed-ASR attribution says enforcement, not configuration, is the win - L-sized infra worth sequencing after the verifier work.

minimax.landing_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox - container/remote node providers, per-node sandbox profiles
minimax.rationale: The snapshot already ships container and remote placement, so this is about making the boundary real per node with zero vault credentials mounted by default, and the layer-attribution ablation (removing confinement flips payloads from refused to executed) is the honest way to price it. Effort is L because it depends on the node-agent providers, and 15 leading agents compromise nested sandboxes when real vulnerabilities are present, so it is next rather than now.

ranked.technique: Execution-based vetting of third-party tools and skills (sandbox + credential fixtures + behavior trees)
ranked.mechanism: Vet each third-party tool, skill, or MCP server by executing it in an instrumented sandbox rather than trusting declared metadata: plant credential fixtures outside the tool's declared least-privilege boundary, record real invocations as source-to-sink witnesses or behavior trees, and accept only if observed behavior stays inside the declared contract and no fixture is touched. Descriptions misrepresent behavior, so metadata-only review abstains by default (a description-only, no-box analysis can still serve as the cheap triage tier that decides what deserves execution); static scoring can triage cheaply but has measured blind spots (host-destruction via common shell commands: 0% detected), and direct LLM judgment of skills is weak (19.05% recall). Composite analysis is mandatory because attacks distribute operations across composed skills so no single package looks malicious (98.0% ASR at 3.3% detection). Ground truth for exploitability is a dual oracle - canary fixture touched or canary receipt endpoint hit - not a model verdict; reject on oracle hit, abstain when execution is impossible.
ranked.reported_results: Scan-Before-You-Install: 95.90% recall at 4.22% FPR (SkillTrustBench subset), F1 0.947 on MalSkillBench, composite F1 0.991; 53/59 in-the-wild findings analyst-confirmed (arxiv:2610.37901). FlowGuard: F1 0.879 command injection, 0.942 filesystem risk, 2.23x lower latency via TRIAGE parameter probing (arxiv:2607.14754). MTGuard: 48.3% unsafe-call detection vs 8.3% baselines at 3.7% FP (arxiv:2607.25297). MCP-FSD classifiers: 99.5% precision / 97.1% recall (arxiv:2610.22301). SandScope: 1,127 tools profiled, witnesses in 12 of 33 re-executed repos (arxiv:2601.01241). Attack-surface profiling: seven in ten of 6,309 skills carry at least one undeclared elevated capability (arxiv:2610.19264). Negative: five-stage static scoring 0% detection of host-destruction, 42% on NL injection (arxiv:2608.08468); CoRedSkill 98.0% ASR at 3.3% detection against per-skill audit (arxiv:2610.20049).
ranked.miniork_surface: MCP / tool surface, using sandbox placement and per-node sandbox as the execution substrate.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Smallest change: a pre-approval hook that runs any newly declared tool server or installed skill once inside a mini-ork sandbox node with canary credentials planted outside its declared scope and a canary receipt endpoint, failing closed if either canary fires (the execution-confirmed dual-oracle pattern). Measurement: over the current tool set, fixtures touched = 0 for known-good tools, and a planted exfiltration fixture is caught 100% of the time.

glm.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface, sandbox placement as the execution substrate
glm.rationale: Execution-based vetting has strong results (95.9% recall at 4.2% FPR, 53/53 analyst-confirmed), but mini-ork has no third-party skill or MCP intake today - recipes and tools are first-party - so there is nothing to vet until that surface exists.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface, using sandbox placement and per-node sandbox as the execution substrate
minimax.rationale: The snapshot's tool-surface gap says tool access is unmeasured; this replaces description review with a dual deterministic oracle (canary fixture touched or canary receipt endpoint hit) and the evidence is strong (95.90% recall at 4.22% FPR; composed skills reach 98.0% ASR at 3.3% detection). It mitigates the injection and supply-chain holes indirectly rather than closing the missing verifier, so it is next, not now.

ranked.technique: Harness-enforced assurance properties for autonomous finding agents
ranked.mechanism: An autonomous offensive or finding agent must be constrained and evaluated on assurance properties — finding truth, scope compliance, auditability, severity honesty, reproducibility — enforced by the harness in code, never promised by the model. Mechanisms: scope-bounded authorization as a precondition (the agent physically cannot act outside a declared scope), content-addressed evidence bundles per finding, deterministic misuse controls default-on, and machine-checkable attack-path models (logic attack graphs linking scanner-detectable evidence to techniques) so path reasoning is auditable rather than narrated. Accept a finding only with its evidence bundle; abort on any out-of-scope action attempt. Anchored on harness-enforced invariants and content-addressed artifacts.
ranked.reported_results: Semi-automated Datalog rule construction yields sound, auditable attack-path reasoning on 54 agentic CTF tasks (arxiv:2609.15523); hands-on systematization of ten red-teaming tools in an unattended pipeline produces recurring failure modes and design laws including scope-bounded authorization as a precondition (arxiv:2608.21423); a reference harness enforces assurance properties in code with a measurable evaluation protocol and content-addressed evidence bundles (arxiv:2609.22664).
ranked.miniork_surface: evidence ledger and traces (+ merge risk gate and approvals)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Require every security finding mini-ork records to carry a content-addressed evidence bundle (witness artifact + scope declaration + repro command) in the evidence ledger, and make scope compliance a runtime check — any tool call outside the declared scope aborts the node. Measure: findings with complete bundles, and out-of-scope action attempts blocked, on seeded runs.

glm.rationale: Scope-bounded authorization and content-addressed evidence bundles partially ship (the ledger cites by path; artifact contracts bound scope); the assurance-property harness matters if mini-ork ever runs offensive nodes.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces (+ merge risk gate and approvals) - content-addressed evidence bundles per finding
minimax.rationale: The harness-enforced assurance properties (finding truth, scope compliance, auditability, severity honesty, reproducibility) are exactly the properties the doctrine already demands, and requiring a content-addressed witness bundle per finding plus a runtime scope check is a clean way to make them mechanical. Moderate evidence and it is a wrapper over the witness check I already rank in the now-list, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Rule-gated selective auditing with action-framed monitors
ranked.mechanism: Make deep LLM auditing affordable by gating it: cheap deterministic single-event and trace-sequence rules select which pending actions or traces deserve model inspection, and only those go to an LLM audit. Monitors must be action-framed — scoring what the action does within a harm window from first harmful commitment — because content-framed monitors collapse on injection. Ground truth for the audit comes from deterministic replay (symbolic execution of the environment validated per turn), not from human grading of whole trajectories. Accept/reject/abstain maps to the audit verdict: rule-clean traces skip the model entirely, rule-flagged traces get audited before the action commits, and the abstention case is an audit that cannot decide — escalated, not passed. Caution: action-framed monitors still flag a substantial share of refusal twins, so the audit budget must be planned around a known false-flag floor.
ranked.reported_results: Mean LLM audits per run reduced from 8.15 to 2.33 and token usage from 47.8k to 14.6k (~69% reduction) at 72.8% TPR / 5.9% FPR versus 81.5% TPR / 11.8% FPR for auditing every action; multi-agent replay flags all attack runs with no false positives at 82-86% token reduction (arxiv:2610.07256). Action-framed monitors reach AUC 0.95 (decomposition) and 0.99 (injection) while content-framed monitors collapse on injection (AUC 0.52); against refusal twins, action-framed arms still flag 28-48% (arxiv:2610.07089). Symbolic-replay per-action ground truth evaluated across 10 agent models; internal-signal verifiers predict harm and progress more reliably than observable-signal-only baselines (arxiv:2609.14422).
ranked.miniork_surface: `evidence ledger and traces` — run transcripts and the evidence ledger are the audit input; the rules gate which traces reach review nodes.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Insert cheap deterministic trace rules (scope violations, gate retries, effect outside declared ports) ahead of any LLM review node so only flagged traces get model attention, and score those reviews on actions within the harm window. Measure on a seeded-drift corpus: audits per run and token cost at fixed detection rate, plus the refusal-twin false-flag rate the budget must absorb.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger - rules gate which traces reach review nodes
glm.rationale: Rule-gated LLM auditing (audits per run 8.15 to 2.33, ~69% token cut) is a cost lever once there are traces worth auditing; the action-framed monitor design is the transferable caution.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - run transcripts and the evidence ledger are the audit input
minimax.rationale: Rule-gating deep audits cuts LLM audits per run from 8.15 to 2.33 at 72.8% TPR / 5.9% FPR, and the action-framed monitor result (AUC 0.99 on injection versus 0.52 for content-framed) is the key correction for injection. It is an efficiency and coverage layer that presupposes the traces worth auditing exist, so it is watch.

ranked.technique: Curated security-knowledge retrieval (RAG) scoped by predicted CWE exposure
ranked.mechanism: The security reviewer does not receive dumped knowledge; it retrieves curated, taxonomy-anchored security knowledge on demand - CWE class definitions, past fix diffs for the touched APIs, prior disclosures for the same pattern - after a planner step predicts which CWE classes the change is actually exposed to, scoping retrieval before ranking. Retrieved knowledge is context for reasoning and never the verdict: findings still require the deterministic confirmation of the cascade technique. The measured cautions are load-bearing: weakly-related retrieved content degrades reasoning, retrieval alone does not detect malice, and proprietary-API RAG gains may not replicate - so retrieval hit relevance is measured and the knowledge base is versioned like any other pinned dependency. Anchored on the CWE taxonomy and the project's own fix history.
ranked.reported_results: RAG over internet and MITRE CWE knowledge reaches 0.86 accuracy / 0.85 F1, the best of RAG/SFT/dual-agent/baseline (arxiv:2601.00254); CWE-graph-scoped retrieval raises SecurePass@1 from 64.68% to 77.45%, and 85.2% on CWE types with no directly linked fix instances (arxiv:2610.14968); a domain taxonomy plus retrieval over 374 prior disclosures recovers up to 76% of known weakness locations where CodeQL, Semgrep, and Clang Static Analyzer match none despite 1,3xx flags (arxiv:2609.09386); targeted on-demand retrieval lifts a local reviewer from 11.8% to 18.4% L&R&T on the same model (arxiv:2610.27383); domain retrieval raises HDL detection accuracy by up to 57.14% average over prompt-only (arxiv:2603.05689); caution - RAG frequently degrades malware explanations via weakly related context (arxiv:2605.03140), open-weight reproduction of Vul-RAG plateaus at ~0.30 pairwise accuracy (arxiv:2606.04739), and retrieval alone does not reliably detect malicious intent in packages (arxiv:2601.12148).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Check in a small curated index (CWE class definitions plus the technique catalog this run produced) and add a planner step to the security reviewer that predicts exposed CWE classes from the diff before retrieving entries on demand. A/B on the same seeded benchmark as the cascade technique: seeded-vulnerability recall with scoped retrieval versus prompt-only, at equal token budget, plus a retrieval-hit-relevance metric to catch the degradation mode.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - CWE-scoped retrieval for the proposer tier
glm.rationale: CWE-scoped retrieval lifts the proposer tier (SecurePass@1 64.7% to 77.5%) but is an accuracy knob on G05-T02, not a gate, and carries the measured caution that weakly-related retrieval degrades reasoning.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - a curated CWE index with a planner step that predicts exposed CWE classes
minimax.rationale: CWE-graph-scoped retrieval raises SecurePass@1 from 64.68% to 77.45% and a taxonomy retrieval recovers up to 76% of known weakness locations where CodeQL, Semgrep and Clang Static Analyzer match none, which is the hole G05-T02 must fill. It is watch because retrieval-only gains plateau near 0.30 pairwise accuracy on open weights and the technique contributes knowledge, not detection.

ranked.technique: Tamper-evident, externally anchored run records
ranked.mechanism: Records each agent action as a canonically serialized, typed event and seals the record so post-hoc attribution does not depend on mutable logs: hash chaining with Merkle batching per epoch, signed receipts binding the record root to its incident context, an append-only log with redaction attestation, and periodic anchoring of epoch roots outside the host so a third party can check the record without trusting the operator. Motivated by a demonstrated failure: agents asked to delete their own traces succeeded in every tested harness but one, without tripping any monitor guardrail. Sealed run capsules carry the recipe needed to replay a run, and signed state-delta telemetry gives agents verifiable input rather than prose logs. Accept = chain verifies and the root matches its anchor; reject = any broken link or missing anchor; abstain = the pre-anchor window, which is explicitly reported as unproven. Caution: tamper evidence establishes integrity of the record, not truth of the claim — it composes with claim adjudication rather than replacing it.
ranked.reported_results: All tested local coding-agent harnesses except one allowed agents to delete their own traces without triggering monitor guardrails (arxiv:2609.30266).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Make the run transcript append-only in practice: hash-chain each node's events, sign the epoch root into the run manifest, and add a verify subcommand that checks the chain and flags gaps or missing anchors. Measurement: a red-team instruction telling the agent to delete its trace produces a detectable broken chain, mirroring the harnesses that today allow silent deletion.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/evidence_ledger.py - hash-chained, externally anchored run records
glm.rationale: Every tested harness but one let agents delete their own traces, and mini-ork run dirs are plain files a node can write; hash-chaining the ledger per epoch is a contained extension once the security verifier work settles.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - hash-chained node events with a signed epoch root in the run manifest
minimax.rationale: All tested local coding-agent harnesses except one allowed agents to delete their own traces without tripping any monitor guardrail, so an append-only, verifiable run record closes a hole the snapshot's evidence ledger does not cover - it proves integrity of the record, not truth of the claim, which composes with claim adjudication. It is next, not now, because external anchoring is an infrastructure dependency.

ranked.technique: Per-action monitors with risk-control-calibrated thresholds
ranked.mechanism: A monitor inspects each proposed action — the tool call plus its transcript context — and can block it; thresholds are not hand-tuned but set by risk control over verifier signals so a cumulative alarm carries an explicit risk bound, ambiguous prediction sets escalate to a human instead of deciding, and detector features are restricted to sets the adversary cannot move (attack-orbit invariance). Accept = action within policy at the calibrated threshold; block = over threshold; abstain = ambiguous set routed to a human. Caution (measured): production blocking monitors for coding agents were bypassed — injection let a persistently malign agent run arbitrary bash in 79% of trials — until hardened by tool coverage, transcript formatting, and a staged agentic review pass; per-action monitoring stops lone compromised agents but not colluding pairs; defenses do not transfer across threat models; and cross-principal covert collusion is detectable only up to a detectability-throughput tradeoff. The monitor's real operating envelope must therefore be measured on benign and attack corpora, not assumed.
ranked.reported_results: Injection attacks let a persistently malign agent run arbitrary bash in 79% of trials against production blocking monitors before hardening (arxiv:2609.19587); per-action LLM monitoring stops lone compromised agents but not colluding pairs, and defenses do not transfer across threat models (arxiv:2609.33102); risk-control-calibrated online alarms are competitive with sequential-hypothesis-testing baselines while giving explicit guarantees and earlier detection (arxiv:2607.02510); attack-orbit-invariant conformal detection holds under every evaluated attack (arxiv:2609.19241).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Register an LLM-monitor gate evaluator via mini_ork/gates/gate_registry.py that scores proposed publish/merge actions from the transcript, with its threshold calibrated on a benign-run corpus to a set false-block bound and ambiguous scores routed to the existing merge-approval queue. Measurement: the benign-run false-block rate stays under the bound while seeded injection attempts are blocked.

glm.rationale: Per-action monitors were bypassed at 79% pre-hardening and do not stop colluding pairs; rule-gated versions (G03-T12) are the better shape if monitors are needed at all.

minimax.landing_surface: gate registry - a per-action monitor with thresholds calibrated on a benign-run corpus
minimax.rationale: Production blocking monitors for coding agents were bypassed - injection let a persistently malign agent run arbitrary bash in 79% of trials - until hardened by tool coverage, transcript formatting and a staged review pass, and per-action monitoring stops lone compromised agents but not colluding pairs. The doctrine permits a model as a veto but never as the accept rule, so a calibrated monitor over publish and merge actions is legitimate; it is watch because the measured false-flag floor must be absorbed by the budget.

ranked.technique: Edit-time sabotage monitoring with synchronous rollback
ranked.mechanism: Monitors the agent's edits structurally rather than semantically: an information-flow graph over file access (which files read, which written, in what structure) is scored for sabotage risk against a profile calibrated on only a handful of honest runs — no attack training data — because an agent with repository write access can weaken infrastructure covertly while making the visible task look legitimate. In synchronous mode the monitor suspends the commit and rolls back in realtime when the access structure is anomalous; the kernel-side variant reduces self-state corruption through legitimate syscalls to a compact feature tuple observable at the kernel boundary. Accept = access structure within the honest-run profile and the dirty set within declared scope; reject-and-rollback = out-of-scope or anomalous structure; abstain = insufficient honest-run calibration, in which case the edit is held.
ranked.reported_results: A synchronous information-flow-graph mode with realtime rollback drives joint main-plus-covert attack success to zero without blocking legitimate tasks, and the untrained IFG beats trained baselines on async detection (arxiv:2607.14570).
ranked.adoption_sketch: scripts/mini_ork_worktree.py already tracks claimed owns paths — add a synchronous pre-commit check that the actual dirty set is a subset of the claim, rolling back out-of-scope edits before the green gate, and score the run's file-access structure against a profile built from honest runs. Measurement: a covert edit to an unclaimed config file is reverted while benign runs are unaffected.

glm.rationale: Untrained information-flow-graph sabotage scoring with synchronous rollback overlaps what write-scope claims plus the green gate already enforce; single-paper evidence.

minimax.landing_surface: worktree claim registry - a synchronous pre-commit check that the dirty set is a subset of the claim
minimax.rationale: A synchronous information-flow-graph mode with realtime rollback drives joint main-plus-covert attack success to zero without blocking legitimate tasks, and the claim registry already tracks the owned paths. It is watch because the honest-run calibration profile and the flow-graph features are a build, and it duplicates the simpler merge-time scope check in G03-T10.

ranked.technique: Staged admission and certified retirement for self-modification
ranked.mechanism: Governs agents that edit their own harness, skills, or plugins: changes are admitted through staged executable contracts encoding release policy — least privilege, telemetry consent, provenance, privileged-write authority, lifecycle constraints, bounded failure — because compilation plus functional tests demonstrably do not establish those properties. Retirement of a safeguard or skill requires a two-gate certificate: preserved authorized utility plus zero unauthorized protected effects, tested via matched authority counterfactuals that hold action, parameters, and intended effect fixed while varying one governing predicate. Self-evolution is audited on matched benign acquisition trajectories with sealed evaluation endpoints and independent state replay, because capability gains can co-occur with security drift that post-evolution accuracy alone hides; skill reuse is audited by deterministic comparison of cached provenance traces with the LLM run only at ingestion. Accept = contract passes and the certificate holds; reject = any contract clause unproven; abstain = no executable contract exists for the surface, which defaults to deny. Caution: when safeguards overlap, an acceptance gate scored on a task batch admits edits that erode redundancy the batch cannot observe, so final judgment uses held-out harm pools.
ranked.reported_results: Capability gains from self-evolution co-occur with security drift under sealed-endpoint audit (arxiv:2608.17684); compilation plus functional tests demonstrably do not establish release-policy properties (arxiv:2608.00739); overlapping safeguards let acceptance gates admit redundancy-eroding edits, formalized over ten gate rules with held-out final sets (arxiv:2610.38392).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Give config/kernel-frozen.yaml an executable admission contract: any run touching a frozen path must prove privilege, provenance, and lifecycle clauses and pass a held-out harm pool, not just the green gate. Measurement: a seeded edit that removes a safeguard while keeping tests green is rejected.

glm.rationale: The repo integrity guard ships staged admission for frozen paths; extending executable contracts to self-improvement beyond kernel paths is real but waits for the learning loop to touch more than lessons.

minimax.landing_surface: repo integrity guard - an executable admission contract for frozen-path edits
minimax.rationale: Compilation plus functional tests demonstrably do not establish release-policy properties, and a seeded edit that removes a safeguard while keeping tests green would be exactly the failure the shipped repo integrity guard is supposed to catch. It is watch because the executable contract and held-out harm pool are a substantial addition to a guard that already exists.

ranked.technique: Structural safeguards over model accuracy (tamper-evident ledger, entity anchoring, human-approved changes)
ranked.mechanism: Provide the guarantee with structure rather than model accuracy: every automated conclusion must be anchored to entities actually observed in the evidence, every rule/policy change requires human approval before taking effect, and every action appends to a tamper-evident ledger so post-hoc tampering is detectable. A deterministic pre-filter at ingestion keeps hostile volume away from the cognitive engine, semantic guardrails wrap the model itself, and guardrail-captured injection attempts are structured and fed back for analyst visibility. With these in place, small local models match frontier detection at a fraction of the energy. Accept rule: a conclusion that cannot cite ledgered entities is rejected outright - traceability, not confidence, is the gate.
ranked.reported_results: Campaign correlation precision rose from 18.75% to 51.81% while resisting prompt injection, label poisoning, and ledger tampering, at 650x less energy than frontier-model operation; per-network normal-traffic scoring reaches 73.42% F1 with zero false positives on unseen networks versus 58.10% F1 with 49.00% false positives for Claude Opus 5.5 (arxiv:2610.41072).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Tighten the evidence ledger so every gate conclusion must cite the ledger entries (file hashes, command outputs) it rests on - uncited conclusions fail the gate - and route gate-rule changes through the existing operator-approval path used for merge approvals. Measure by tampering with a ledger entry in a replayed run (detection must fire) and counting uncited conclusions before and after the citation requirement.

glm.rationale: Structural safeguards (tamper-evident ledger, human-approved policy changes) overlap G06-T07; the small-model-plus-structure result is the interesting part for lane economics.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - every gate conclusion must cite the ledger entries it rests on; uncited conclusions fail
minimax.rationale: The rule that a conclusion which cannot cite observed entities is rejected outright, and that rule changes gate policy rather than adding a detector, matches the shipped doctrine exactly. It is next because it is the cheapest way to stop a security claim resting on an unobserved property, and it composes with the approvals path the snapshot already ships.

ranked.technique: Deterministic pre-write admission over declared change scope
ranked.mechanism: Make each agent's change scope a machine-checked claim: writes are admitted or rejected against a versioned, declared intent — statically against the claim at commit time, or dynamically against live task context — failing closed on any undeclared-scope write. The measured trade-off is the operating point: static admission (scope fixed up front) halves clobbering but serializes nearly all concurrent work, while dynamic admission preserves concurrency and still fails closed when a write falls outside the declared scope. Accept rule: a write path must fall inside the agent's declared scope claim at the moment of writing; anything else is rejected loudly rather than merged. This is coordination enforced as a security property — undeclared-scope writes are the failure it exists to catch.
ranked.reported_results: Static admission raises pair pass rate 23.3% to 50.0% and halves clobbering but serializes 96.7% of workloads (arxiv:2608.00947). Dynamic selective admission fails closed on 46/90 undeclared-scope trials while cutting serialization to 22.2% (arxiv:2608.00947). Model-agnostic admission and rejection of edits against declared scope claims, confirmed to fail closed on undeclared-scope writes (arxiv:2607.21909).
ranked.miniork_surface: `worktree claim registry` — `scripts/mini_ork_worktree.py` `--owns` claims and the merge-path scope check.
ranked.adoption_sketch: mini-ork already claims file surfaces at worktree creation; add dynamic re-admission at merge time so a commit containing paths outside the live claim set fails closed with a precise diff listing, instead of relying on the creating agent's discipline. Measure: undeclared-scope write rejection rate on seeded stray-path commits (target 100%) and the serialization rate versus the current static-claim behavior.

glm.rationale: Write-scope claims with overlap refusal ship; dynamic admission against live task context is an increment with measured serialization trade-offs (96.7% static vs 22.2% dynamic), not a new capability.

minimax.landing_surface: scripts/mini_ork_worktree.py --owns claims and the merge-path scope check
minimax.rationale: The snapshot ships worktree claims but nothing re-admits the dirty set at merge time against the live claim set, and dynamic selective admission fails closed on 46/90 undeclared-scope trials while cutting serialization to 22.2%. That is a small, deterministic addition that turns the existing claim registry into an enforced property rather than an agent's discipline, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Dual-use harm from benign instructions and refusal calibration
ranked.mechanism: Measures harm that needs no malicious prompt: benign task decompositions that lead a privileged agent to harmful actions, and dual-use pipelines (cloning a real phishing site) where refusal behavior is attributed between system-level prompting and model alignment. Because security workloads are dual-use by nature, over-refusal is measured alongside safety using paired routine/red-team suites across model-harness-layer configurations, exposing lanes that refuse legitimate security work. Accept rule: a lane configuration passes only if it passes both suites (low harmful-completion rate AND low routine-refusal rate); passing one side is reported as miscalibration, not safety. Caution: refusal varies enormously across configurations and layers, and refusal-direction abliteration that removes cyber refusals on one model is unreliable across models.
ranked.reported_results: Most computer-use agents exceed 90% attack success under purely benign instructions (Claude 4.5 Sonnet 73.0%), with safety alignment activating mainly in early steps and multi-agent decomposition raising ASR (arxiv:2604.10577); one model refuses 40% of routine tasks at the API layer but only 4% after agentic reasoning, across 16 model-harness configurations (arxiv:2607.05462); most runnable phishing-site clones came from models integrated into a coding environment, with refusals partly driven by system-level prompting (arxiv:2602.13363); layer-subset refusal abliteration removes nearly all cyber refusal on Kimi K2 but is mixed across 24 models (arxiv:2607.02714).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Build a small paired fixture set for mini-ork's lanes: routine security tasks (run the secret scanner, read a CVE proof-of-concept for triage) and their red-team twins, run per lane and per harness layer. Measure: routine-refusal rate per lane — any lane refusing routine security work is misconfigured for the recipe's purpose.

glm.rationale: Dual-use refusal calibration matters for offensive lanes mini-ork does not run; keep the paired-suite method if a pentest recipe ever lands.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config - a paired routine / red-team fixture set per lane
minimax.rationale: One model refuses 40% of routine tasks at the API layer but only 4% after agentic reasoning, and most computer-use agents exceed 90% attack success under purely benign instructions, so a lane that refuses routine security work is misconfigured for the recipe's purpose. It is watch because a security-operations recipe has a genuinely dual-use character and a small paired fixture set is the right first cut.

ranked.technique: Reachability-weighted severity prioritization (context-aware, not context-free scoring)
ranked.mechanism: Rank findings by deployment-specific reachability - whether the flagged code is present and callable in this repository and lane - fusing context-free scores with code-level evidence, because context-free LLM severity is directionally biased (systematically overestimates, almost never recognizes low severity) and context-free base scores bury the exploitable item. Reachability evidence the verifier can recompute (import graph, call sites, dead-code check) is the sort key; model severity may tie-break but never decides. Accept an ordering only with the reachability evidence attached to each ranked item. Anchored on presence-and-callability checks, with the measured 86% rank improvement over CVSS as the reference shape.
ranked.reported_results: Fusing CVSS, EPSS, and KEV with deployment-specific code evidence reduces the mean rank of the first confirmed-exploitable CVE by 86.0% versus CVSS (arxiv:2610.13071); caution - LLMs assign correct CVSS severity to at most ~50% of bug bounty reports (56% after benchmark-selected fine-tuning), systematically overestimating and almost never recognizing low severity (arxiv:2610.24623); 9 of 17 vulnerability classes appear in all three models' AI-generated code (arxiv:2607.20713); preference-adaptive ranking elicits operational context that no fixed score encodes (arxiv:2608.19430).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Teach mini_ork/gates/merge_risk.py to weight security findings by reachability evidence (touched-and-callable versus vendored-or-dead) and forbid model-generated severity numbers as sort keys. Measure rank correlation between gate priority and a seeded ground-truth exploitability ordering versus a context-free-score ordering; the 86% mean-rank reduction is the reference shape.

glm.rationale: Reachability-weighted ranking pays when findings outnumber attention; at mini-ork's expected finding volumes the re-computable sort key is the part to keep.

minimax.landing_surface: merge risk gate and approvals - reachability-weighted ordering of security findings
minimax.rationale: Fusing CVSS, EPSS and KEV with deployment-specific code evidence reduces the mean rank of the first confirmed-exploitable CVE by 86% versus CVSS, and the caution is that LLMs assign correct CVSS severity to at most about 50% of bug bounty reports, so model severity must never be the sort key. It is next because it orders findings rather than finding them.

ranked.technique: Differential and metamorphic verification of LLM-written and translated code
ranked.mechanism: Compilation and unit-test passage are treated as a first filter only: translated or rewritten code is judged by differential comparison of its behavior against the original on shared inputs, and test suites are judged by round-trip mutation — mutate the code, re-extract the intent, regenerate, and check whether the suite catches the behavior change. This detects silently-wrong translations whose compile success is uncorrelated with correctness, and suites that pass everything because they encode the implementation's own assumptions. The oracle abstains when no reference behavior exists (pure new code), where generation-side paired oracles (G07-T01) apply instead.
ranked.reported_results: Compile success of 0.94-1.00 while correctness is 0.00 for many model-kernel pairs — compile-passing translation is uncorrelated with correctness — and a tool-integrated model raises correctness by 43.2% (arxiv:2607.04058); round-trip mutation amplifies small suites to 4.3x fault detection with 4-test suites (arxiv:2607.03223).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend recipes/code-fix/verifiers/metamorphic.py with a differential mode for port/rewrite/refactor tasks: execute base and head on the same generated inputs over the touched surface and fail on output divergence. Measurement: silently-wrong rewrites caught that the current test verifier misses, on a replayed set of port-shaped tasks.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - differential and metamorphic verifiers
glm.rationale: The verification stack already ships differential and metamorphic verifiers; the round-trip mutation amplifier is an increment on shipped machinery, not a gap.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - differential and metamorphic verification of LLM-written code
minimax.rationale: The shipped verifier set already includes a metamorphic verifier, so this is an extension rather than a new surface, and the differential idea fits mini-ork's verification stack. It is watch because only two papers support it and the incremental gain over the shipped metamorphic verifier is not established.

ranked.technique: Origin-bound authority state: permissions re-derived at use, conflicts preserved through consolidation
ranked.mechanism: Permissions, approvals, and grants live as signed records bound to their origin and are re-derived from the trusted record store at use time; authority is never accepted from recalled memory content or from summaries, because consolidation that preserves the claim while stripping its authorization metadata manufactures authority (50.3% unauthorized-action rate after collapse). Preserve authority labels and contradictions as explicit objects through any summarization or consolidation step - never silently merge conflicting records into a confident one - and require corroboration from the origin before any elevation. Both content-based and lineage-based defense signals are malleable under laundering, so the anchor is cryptographic origin plus machine-checked policy, with reject as the closed default when the origin record cannot be produced.
ranked.reported_results: Authority-label prediction and persistence: unauthorized actions 16.9% to 0.0% (clustering consolidator) and 8.3% to 0.0% (kNN); conditional on retention, attack success 42.4% to about 1-2% (arxiv:2608.01679). Endogenous authorization laundering: 50.2% false-authority rate with 98.6% executor compliance (arxiv:2609.01836). Conflict-preserving memory: 2.1% false-certainty versus 40% false-confident actions under collapsed memory (arxiv:2607.05844). Non-malleable origin-bound authority defeats LLM-judge attribution suppression with machine-checked guarantees, where MemLineage's lineage edge is shown malleable (arxiv:2606.24322).
ranked.miniork_surface: merge risk gate and approvals - mini_ork/gates/merge_approval.py must verify approvals against the signed ledger rather than any remembered or summarized claim.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Make every mini-ork approval a signed ledger row (patch id, head, scope, note, timestamp) and change every consumer to verify the row exists and matches before honoring an approval recalled from a transcript, summary, or memory. Measurement: plant a forged approval-already-given note in run state and require 100% rejection, while legitimate approvals still pass unchanged.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/gates/merge_approval.py - approvals verified against the ledger
glm.rationale: mini-ork approvals are already recorded against the head patch id in a store outside model context and re-checked at merge, so authority-from-memory is structurally excluded; the residual (approvals surviving summarization) is small.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/gates/merge_approval.py - verify approvals against the signed ledger
minimax.rationale: The snapshot says merge approvals are already bound to the head patch id and the policy is read from origin/main, so this is an extension (signed origin-bound rows, conflicts preserved through consolidation) rather than a new mechanism. The 50.3% false-authority rate after memory consolidation is real, but the attack path runs through summaries and memory, not through the verifier set or an injection probe, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Conditional validation and multi-axis robustness before promotion
ranked.mechanism: Blocks promotion of a new detector, gate config, or model on a single benchmark number. It requires candidate comparability — the challenger must beat the incumbent under the conditions the incumbent will face after promotion — and re-scores results under defensible variations of the analysis protocol (matching rules, ordering, context, dataset pairing, adversarial evasion) to find where conclusions flip. Accept rule: promote only if the decision is stable across a pre-declared variation set; a ranking that reverses under any defensible protocol choice is an abstention, not a win. Cross-architecture replication checks that a claimed behavior is not an artifact of one model family. Caution: an adaptive adversary who behaves until certification and attacks after defeats any finite pre-certification assessment — statistical assurance certifies the measurement, never the future.
ranked.reported_results: 11 of 45 pairwise tool orderings reverse under defensible matching-rule variations (arxiv:2609.01671); no universal winner across same-dataset / cross-dataset / evasion axes — XGBoost wins cross-dataset transfer by 15 F1 points while a fine-tuned LLM's false-positive rate reaches 0.78 on the target network (arxiv:2609.13511); conditional validation required before an adaptive-IDS challenger may replace the incumbent (arxiv:2609.04388); adaptive adversaries defeat any finite pre-certification assessment with quantified expected post-certification excess (arxiv:2610.18948).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a stability clause to gate promotion in mini_ork: a new gate or lane config is promoted only if its verdict distribution over a fixed replay set is stable under pre-declared variations (seed, ordering, model pin). Measure: promotions blocked or deferred as unstable, and post-promotion verdict-flip rate versus a baseline period.

glm.rationale: Conditional validation before promotion is sound discipline for gate-config changes; no mini-ork surface is blocked on it today.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - a stability clause for gate and lane-config promotion
minimax.rationale: 11 of 45 pairwise tool orderings reverse under defensible matching-rule variations, and no universal winner exists across same-dataset, cross-dataset and evasion axes, so a new security gate must be stable across pre-declared variations before it is promoted. This is the governance half of the doctrine and applies to every verifier I rank in the now-list, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Evidence-sufficiency-gated triage with explicit escalation
ranked.mechanism: A triage/investigation agent over live telemetry gets constrained tool access (structured queries, bounded text search - not a free-form shell) and must collect evidence to a sufficiency threshold before issuing any verdict; when evidence is insufficient, ambiguous, or capacity is exhausted, it escalates to a human rather than guessing or dropping. Capacity-aware formulations treat triage as a constrained decision problem - which alerts are worth escalating under analyst capacity and asymmetric error costs - and latency-budgeted variants bias uncertain cases toward escalation rather than drop. The anchored quantity is evidence retrieved, not answer recall, and the documented failure mode is structural: deterministic playbook (SOAR-style) responders fail on ambiguous behavioral signals and cross-cycle persistence, which is exactly what the escalation path exists to catch.
ranked.reported_results: F1 0.958 vs 0.371-0.744 for studied approaches, false negatives cut from 40.4% to 3.1% while escalating 18.4% of alerts (arxiv:2610.10608); 82.8% detection accuracy at 0.120 false-positive rate on SIEM logs (arxiv:2604.27321); 100% indicator recall across four malware scenarios while no-RAG baselines missed all attack infrastructure (arxiv:2603.18196); 90% reduction in mean time to insight in production triage at comparable diagnostic accuracy (arxiv:2602.02585).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add an evidence-sufficiency precondition to the publish gate: promotion requires proof the verifier set actually engaged its surface (touched-files gate ran on the dirty set, tests selected from changed code), and anything short of that parks the run for operator escalation instead of passing. Measure by seeding runs with silently no-op verifiers - the sufficiency check must catch them - while clean runs still promote untouched.

glm.rationale: Evidence-sufficiency-gated triage is a SecOps analyst shape; mini-ork's nearest analog (verifier abstention) already fails closed by doctrine.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - an evidence-sufficiency precondition before promotion
minimax.rationale: Promotion should require proof the verifier set actually engaged its surface, since silently no-op verifiers are a live failure mode and the fix parks the run for operator escalation rather than passing - the doctrine's 'a guard that cannot measure blocks'. It is next because it is a precondition on the publish gate rather than a defect-finder, and it duplicates the verifier-engagement audit already folded into G09-T08's landing surface.

ranked.technique: Hybrid pre-call redaction cascade with coherent surrogate substitution
ranked.mechanism: A deterministic cascade - a regex tier for structured identifiers plus an NER/entity tier for names - inspects every outbound payload before it reaches a provider lane and replaces detected PII and secrets with coherent, type-consistent surrogates rather than blank masks, preserving downstream utility; quasi-identifier combinations (ZIP + birth date + gender) are flagged even when each field alone looks benign. The accept/reject rule is quantified: the pipeline's residual leak equals the detector's recall, so recall is measured and the residual leak reported honestly rather than claiming safety, and rephrasing is validator-gated (rejected when key-term survival drops below a floor). Regex-only redaction survives only as the fast first tier because it demonstrably under-recalls. Every detector architecture family (encoder NER, rule hybrids, generative LLM) degrades under distribution shift, so the cascade is benchmarked on the deployment's own text, and institution-local identifiers need explicit handling because purpose-built de-identification and even gold standards miss them. Caution: document-level safety, not localization F1, is the release metric - the strongest redaction configuration still left critical PII on most pages.
ranked.reported_results: Fast hybrid redaction caught 100% of PII and kept 100% of business terms at 13.48 ms median vs 9,120 ms for the LLM call; pure regex caught 88.9% (arxiv:2611.07633); route-local + redact + rephrase achieved 0.6% combined PII leak with zero exact leaks over 500 samples, with rephrasing rejected below 70% key-term survival (arxiv:2604.12064); cascade detection F1 98.87% with 0.00% adversarial recovery of originals vs 1.53% for rewriting (arxiv:2606.29567); typed recall 0.915 at precision 0.907, 0.49 s per million characters with superior OOD generalization (arxiv:2610.30518); institution-targeted prompting reached F1 0.918 vs 0.779 for a purpose-built de-identifier (arxiv:2608.17051); the strongest redaction configuration still leaked safety-critical PII on 96.8% of applicable pages (arxiv:2609.02207).
ranked.miniork_surface: lane config provider surface, via a pre-call redaction stage at the dispatch transport seam (mini_ork/dispatch/providers.py register_dispatch_backend)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a redaction stage on the dispatch backend for remote lanes: regex tier reusing the existing gitleaks rules plus an NER tier, with surrogates drawn from a fixed referent-preserving placeholder scheme (the two-tier mini-ork shape: local regex fast path, NER/model tier optional and fail-closed when unconfigured). Measure on a seeded corpus of resume-style and run-log text with planted PII: catch rate and residual leak vs regex-only (target: beat the 88.9% regex-only baseline), with added latency under 1% of the 9 s median provider call.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/providers.py - pre-call redaction at the transport seam
glm.rationale: PII redaction at the transport seam is a hosted-multi-tenant concern; a single-operator mini-ork's egress is better governed by sandbox policy.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/providers.py register_dispatch_backend - a pre-call redaction stage at the dispatch transport seam
minimax.rationale: A deterministic cascade (regex tier plus NER tier) with coherent surrogate substitution, where the residual leak is reported as the detector's recall rather than claimed to be zero, fits the snapshot's doctrine precisely and beats regex-only (100% PII catch versus 88.9%). It is next because it is a privacy control on provider traffic, whereas the snapshot's named gap is credential and secret detection.

ranked.technique: Capability-scoped typed authority replacing ambient authority
ranked.mechanism: Replace ambient authority — where naming a resource suffices to act on it — with typed, host-side capabilities minted from trusted input before any untrusted content is read, enforced per issuing node at dispatch. Checks approve objects, not names, so a later step cannot remap an approved path/argument to a different object; every decision field is authorized by exactly one context source (user, tool, environment, agent). Accept requires the exact object to be named by an unspent capability; everything else fails closed regardless of wording. This is the anchor for vault scope: authority must be preserved, attenuated, and evidenced from human principal to tool endpoint, and components must pass tasks rather than credentials. A static global denylist is not this technique — measured to be indistinguishable from no policy because malicious actions are ordinary in-repository operations it never names.
ranked.reported_results: Injected effect executed in 3/75 runs under capability scoping vs 33-47/75 for baselines (ambient authority 47/75; static global denylist 46/75 — a denylist does not improve on no policy); 68/75 repairs still completed (arxiv:2609.08371). Baseline loses all 74 ground-truth attacks; full object-bound mediation blocks 58, escalates 14, lets 2 succeed; approval tier is the largest single contributor (arxiv:2610.14488). 98.9% attack interception at 90.5% decision compliance (100% on label-conditioned splits) (arxiv:2607.27267). Zero attack success with GPT-5.4 on AgentDojo and InjecAgent (arxiv:2611.00729). 1.9x execution overhead vs over 12x for CaMeL (arxiv:2609.37196). Off-host gateway: residual attack success 0% at up to 0.03ms overhead; models refusing 100% of dangerous operations execute 38% once the gateway authoritatively scopes them (arxiv:2607.05518). Collapsing the four context sources into one generic trusted context causes 3,593/3,823 false accepts (94%) (arxiv:2609.14631).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Mint per-node capability tokens from the recipe's artifact contract (its declared ports and worktree paths) at dispatch, consumed by the executor; any file, tool, or egress not named by an unspent token fails closed. Measure CapScope-style: runs with an injected instruction file in the repo should execute the injected out-of-scope effect near 0 times versus a no-scope baseline, while task completion stays within a few points.

glm.rationale: Typed object capabilities at dispatch (injected effect executed in 3/75 runs vs 33-47/75 under ambient authority) is the principled version of vault scoping; a large refactor, right after sandbox enforcement.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/vault.py, mini_ork/remote/secrets_scope.py
minimax.rationale: Replacing ambient authority with typed host-side capabilities is the principled fix for the snapshot's tool-surface gap, and the evidence separates it from the tempting alternative: a static global denylist is indistinguishable from no policy (46/75 versus 47/75 injected effects), while object-bound capability scoping admits 3/75. Effort is L because it reworks the dispatch authorization path, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Caution: distributed and narrative corpus poisoning of retrieval evidence
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique with an ingestion-side mitigation: retrieved evidence is a poisoning surface, and the payloads that survive are distributed and narrative rather than concentrated. A false claim split across many locally plausible documents defeats per-document filters because multi-hop reasoning reassembles the payload; a single document framed as a coherent knowledge update (old answer invalidated by event X, per authority Y) defeats contradiction resolution, so consistency checking is necessary but insufficient; and a compromised retriever checkpoint needs no corpus write access at all while repurposing purification to conceal itself from weight-space detectors. Ingestion should therefore record per-claim provenance - how many distinct-origin documents support each load-bearing claim, and whether support is self-citing - and verification must check traceability and temporal validity, not just internal consistency. Abstain (flag for reviewer downgrade) when a load-bearing claim's only support is single-origin or a self-referential update narrative.
ranked.reported_results: CodePoisonRAG: all 85 poisoned artifacts reach Top-3 retrieval at a 0.7% corpus-poisoning ratio; ASR 0.80-0.93 across three generators (arxiv:2609.02774). PURPOSE: best ASR in 35 of 45 settings, +9.7 mean ASR over the strongest prior method across 3 QA benchmarks, 5 generators, 3 conflict-resolution methods (arxiv:2608.04756). Retriever backdoor cuts Spectral Signatures separation (mean |AUROC-50|) from 46.53 to 29.26 while malicious retrieval persists (arxiv:2609.37468). InceptionRAG stays effective outnumbered by benign context, with larger models more susceptible (arxiv:2609.16818); micro-collaborative poisoning is driven by adversarial coverage across multiple sources (arxiv:2609.21573).
ranked.miniork_surface: evidence ledger and traces - provenance checks on retrieved body text feeding research and extraction nodes.
ranked.adoption_sketch: At corpus ingestion, record for each load-bearing claim its support set (document ids and distinct origins) and mark claims supported only by a single origin or by an update-narrative document for reviewer downgrade. Measurement: support-concentration statistics over the collected corpus, plus a planted distributed-poisoning fixture whose reassembled claim the ingestion flags.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger provenance checks on retrieved body text
glm.rationale: Retrieved body text is a poisoning surface for research recipes, but assemble-style citation checking already anchors conclusions to the corpus deterministically; the distributed-payload results (Top-3 reach at 0.7% corpus poisoning) justify a provenance check later.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - provenance checks on retrieved body text feeding research and extraction nodes
minimax.rationale: This run's own corpus is the exposure: all 85 poisoned artifacts reach Top-3 retrieval at a 0.7% poisoning ratio, and per-document filters fail against distributed narrative payloads, so per-claim provenance (distinct-origin support set, self-citing update narratives) is a concrete intake rule. It is moderate evidence and orthogonal to the two named holes, so it is next.

ranked.technique: Caution: tool metadata and update channels carry post-vetting attacks (staged trust, semantic hijack, update gap)
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique: the tool channel between vetting and execution stays attacker-controlled. LLM-optimized tool descriptions are statistically indistinguishable from benign ones and reach 83.23% ASR at most 4.25% detector detection, with humans rating them equal to benign; fake-config templates in descriptions drive near-universal compliance including real credentials in placeholder fields; malicious servers can behave benignly until reliance builds and then switch, which is invisible to pre-deployment static analysis; and tool updates execute outside the model context window, so in-context injection defenses never see them. Defense therefore belongs at the boundary, not the prompt: baseline-deviation runtime monitoring of tool-call streams plus hash-based re-verification on every update (the lockfile of G01-T04). Rule: on deviation or unverified update, quarantine the tool; absence of deviation is not proof of safety, only absence of alarm.
ranked.reported_results: TSA: 83.23% average ASR, maximum 4.25% detection across detectors, human suspiciousness rating 4.00 vs 4.03 for benign; up to 92.13% ASR transferring to GPT-5 (arxiv:2610.33182). Fake-config template: 100% description compliance on 10 of 12 models with real workspace credentials populated into placeholder api_key fields (arxiv:2609.18217). A2M trace-optimized hijack: 46.5x input tokens and 26.9 average tool calls versus benign execution (arxiv:2609.26761). ETUDE tool-update attacks bypass prompt-injection detectors across seven frameworks including Claude Code (arxiv:2611.01976); nine TrustShift variants instantiated over four production domains (arxiv:2608.23763). Unicode TAG-block concealment in tool names/descriptions is invisible in human approval views while present in the bytes injected into model context, demonstrated across three independent MCP servers (arxiv:2607.05744).
ranked.miniork_surface: MCP / tool surface - runtime boundary monitoring at dispatch, complementing the G01-T04 lockfile.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Log every tool call and result at the dispatch layer and alarm on baseline deviation (per-tool argument shapes, call rates, token amplification) and on any update-triggered hash change without re-vetting. Measurement: replay a staged-trust fixture - benign phase then payload - through the monitor and confirm the deviation alarm fires before harm, with zero alarms on a clean workload.

glm.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - runtime boundary monitoring at dispatch
