glm.rationale: Tool-metadata attacks (83.2% ASR at 4.25% detector detection) presume an attacker-controlled tool channel mini-ork does not expose; revisit alongside G01-T04 when external tools arrive.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - runtime boundary monitoring at dispatch
minimax.rationale: The gap between vetting and execution is real and measurable (LLM-optimized descriptions reach 83.23% ASR at at most 4.25% detector detection, human-rated equal to benign; fake-config templates reach 100% compliance with real credentials), so runtime deviation monitoring plus hash re-verification is justified. It is a caution against trusting a static scan, not a closure of the verifier or probe hole, so it is next.

ranked.technique: MCP/tool approval-pathway audit: both-sides confirmation and signature insufficiency
ranked.mechanism: Audit the approval pathway end to end, because a destructive tool call can be denied on neither side: the server may omit a confirmation annotation or elicitation, and the host may not prompt — split responsibility means no one confirms. The repair is annotation-gated prompting (hosts prompt exactly when a tool declares destructive effect) plus an authentication gateway that unifies heterogeneous tool credentials with explicit identity delegation and one fleet-wide audit log. Parameter poisoning is the adjacent hole: action-level defenses miss attacks that preserve the intended tool but swap arguments, so parameters need task-aware authorization. Caution: signature verification is not a disclosure control — a legitimately signed tool can still embed sensitive data in requests to policy-allowed destinations; disclosure limiting requires execution-level confinement, not authenticity.
ranked.reported_results: An estimated 90% of destructive tools (95% CI 82-95) in a 1,000-repository registry sample have no server-side confirmation; 60.7% of destructive-tool/application pairs lack enforced approval by default; annotation-gated prompting would reduce the unapproved share from 60.7% to 5.4%; four of five low-cost models executed an injected deletion in 479 of 960 runs (arxiv:2611.02527). Parameter-poisoning attack success reaches 93.06% unprotected (arxiv:2611.04673). Signature-verified tools still leak (5.9-74.5% under baselines) while germline execution shows 0 unauthorized disclosures across 153 attack runs (arxiv:2611.06585). Gateway unifies auth along a user/non-user persona x credential-type axis with three generalized identity flows and one queryable audit log (arxiv:2608.10760).
ranked.miniork_surface: `MCP / tool surface` — the tool servers and IDE actions an agent may call.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a deterministic intake check over the tool/IDE-action registry: every state-mutating tool must declare its effect class and map to an enforced host-side approval or a scoped credential — no signature-only admissions — and parameter fields need per-field authorization against the task. Measure the share of mutating tools without enforced approval before and after (the 60.7%-to-5.4% shape), and re-run a signature-trust probe to confirm signed-but-leaky tools are caught by scope, not trust.

glm.rationale: Both-sides confirmation and annotation-gated prompting are MCP-registry findings (90% of destructive tools lack server-side confirmation); mini-ork has no tool servers to audit.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - the tool servers and IDE actions an agent may call
minimax.rationale: The measurement is sharp (an estimated 90% of destructive tools have no server-side confirmation; 60.7% of destructive-tool pairs lack enforced approval) and the fix - annotation-gated prompting plus per-field parameter authorization - is concrete. It is watch rather than next because mini-ork's own MCP surface is far smaller than the surveyed registries and the split-responsibility gap is not yet demonstrated here.

ranked.technique: k-rollout reliability and deterministic replay of gated verdicts
ranked.mechanism: Replaces single-run pass/fail with measured consistency: run the same task k independent times (rollouts — not unit tests misread as trials) and report the distribution, because an agent that succeeds once in k trials is not a 100% agent. Replay fidelity is engineered by pinning the nondeterminism sources the harness controls (seeds, model and version pins, environment snapshots, deterministic execution constraints) and grounding subjective oracles in recorded state; a trajectory that cannot be replayed is marked unauditable rather than trusted. Accept rule: gate on the lower bound of the k-rollout distribution, not the best draw, and flag any verdict that flips across replays as a measurement defect. Caution: the free-text planning step, not execution, can be the dominant residual source of run-to-run variance — determinism work aimed only at the execution layer will not fix it.
ranked.reported_results: pass@k misuse (n set to unit tests rather than independent rollouts) proven by counterexample, with quantified synthetic inflation and a security-adjusted reliability@k (arxiv:2608.14711); k-trial consistency framework exposes outcome variance of the same agent on the same task (arxiv:2601.06112); deterministic execution constraints identify the free-text planning step as the dominant residual variance source (arxiv:2608.26197); replay-fidelity methodology via deterministic replay harnesses, state snapshots and oracle grounding (arxiv:2611.11216).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Have the evidence ledger stamp each verifier verdict with the run's determinism envelope (seed, model pin, env snapshot id) and re-execute a sampled fraction of gated verdicts to measure replay agreement. Measure: replay-agreement rate per verifier; any verifier below a set floor is flagged flaky in its gate output.

glm.rationale: Deterministic replay partially ships (deterministic stages are replayable by design); k-rollout cost accounting matters when LLM verdicts gate, which doctrine forbids.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - stamp each verdict with the run's determinism envelope and re-execute a sample
minimax.rationale: Gating on the lower bound of a k-rollout distribution rather than the best draw, and flagging verdict flips across replays as measurement defects, is correct methodologically and cheap to approximate for deterministic verifiers. It is watch because the dominant residual variance is the free-text planning step, which mini-ork does not control, so the measured gain on a code-fix gate is uncertain.

ranked.technique: Compliance-conditioned monitor and guardrail evaluation
ranked.mechanism: Evaluates monitors and guardrails against what they actually prevent: a catch only counts as protection if the target would otherwise have complied. It samples repeated responses from the monitored model to identify elicitable prompts (complied at least once) and reports monitor performance separately on elicitable vs non-elicitable sets; the same base model is re-measured inside each harness configuration to isolate harness-induced safety deltas rather than mis-attributing them to the model. Accept rule: protection claims must be conditioned on elicitable-rate and harness configuration — an unconditioned recall number is rejected as a protection claim. Extends to guardrail benchmarking across multiple attack families and to continuous risk measurement over first-token branches instead of one binary outcome per prompt, which exposes safe-rerouting capacity a single-response ASR hides.
ranked.reported_results: Monitor recall on elicitable prompts falls 0.22–0.38 below recall on non-elicitable prompts across six monitor configurations / three model families (arxiv:2609.05797); harness-induced safety regression: GPT-5.2 harmful-compliance ASR rises from 2% to 20% (ChemToolAgent), 24% (Biomni) and 72% (DrugAgent) while one harness stays at baseline (arxiv:2610.32045); guardrail benchmark over 1000 malware-generation prompts, 7 jailbreak attacks and a fictional-scenario attack across 9 guardrails / 7 LLMs (arxiv:2609.09798); continuous first-token risk landscapes reveal decoder exposure and mis-ranking binary ASR causes (arxiv:2610.38595).
ranked.adoption_sketch: When mini-ork measures a gate or monitor's catch rate, condition it on elicitability: sample the lane model k times per fixture and report catches only on fixtures the model ever fails open. Measure: the conditioned-vs-unconditioned catch-rate gap on the gate's fixture set — that gap is the overstatement in today's numbers.

glm.rationale: Compliance-conditioned monitor evaluation presumes deployed refusal monitors; mini-ork's gates are deterministic, where refusal is not a state.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - condition catch rates on elicitability
minimax.rationale: Monitor recall falls 0.22-0.38 below unconditioned recall on elicitable prompts across six monitor configurations, so an unconditioned catch rate overstates protection - a real correction for any number mini-ork publishes about its own gates. It is watch because it is a reporting refinement over gates that must exist first.

ranked.technique: Attacker-controllability-scoped robustness checks with calibrated abstention
ranked.mechanism: Partition the input features of any detector or gate by what the adversary actually controls (directly, indirectly, not at all) and build adversarial tests only over the controllable set - a robustness number computed over features the attacker cannot touch is theater. On the defense side, restrict or transform the representation so the adversary's controllable set cannot move it (attack-orbit invariance), and pair it with conformal-style prediction sets: an ambiguous set is an escalation trigger, not a silent pass. The trade is explicit - invariance costs 7-14 points of clean accuracy - so the rule is calibrated abstention under a stated coverage guarantee rather than unmeasured confidence.
ranked.reported_results: Zero constraint violations across attacks spanning 27 LLM cells and 5 datasets, with controllability gaps keeping even F1>=0.70 detectors from being fully evaded on high-traffic datasets (arxiv:2607.07739); attack-orbit-invariant feature restriction leaves the representation completely unchanged under every evaluated attack at a 7-14-point clean-accuracy cost, with split conformal prediction at alpha=0.05 (arxiv:2609.19241); 99.77% detection accuracy under FGSM-adversarial inputs (arxiv:2608.28889).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Audit the gaming-scan corpus so every perturbation varies only what an implementer node truly controls (its diff text, generated files, commit messages) and never framework files it cannot touch, then make the gate treat ambiguous perturbation outcomes as block/escalate rather than pass. Measure the audit's out-of-scope perturbation count and the clean-run false-block rate after adding abstain-on-ambiguity.

glm.rationale: Controllability-scoped robustness checks are evaluator discipline for detectors mini-ork has not deployed; the conformal-abstain rule is doctrine-compatible when one exists.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - restrict adversarial perturbations to features an implementer node actually controls, with abstain-on-ambiguity
minimax.rationale: A robustness number computed over features the attacker cannot touch is theater, and invariance costs 7-14 points of clean accuracy, so calibrated abstention is the honest trade. It is watch because it refines the gaming scan's corpus rather than closing a hole, and the gaming-scan corpus is a smaller surface than the two named holes.

ranked.technique: Preemptive leakage-pattern scanning of recipes and tool surfaces at intake
ranked.mechanism: Before a run starts, statically scan the recipe's prompt templates, tool descriptions, and tool-invocation code for leakage-enabling patterns - unvalidated interpolation of whole upstream artifacts into outbound calls, context echoed into logs, tool arguments accepting arbitrary payloads toward unlisted hosts - and generate actionable patches before deployment instead of relying on continuous runtime policy enforcement. Detection is deterministic pattern-matching over the recipe DAG at kickoff; the accept rule is intake-gating: a recipe with an unpatched leakage-enabling pattern fails to start, which is cheaper and fail-closed relative to runtime policing. Complemented by LLM-assisted privacy-impact assessment that surfaces risks and mitigations pre-deployment. Anchored on measured leakage reduction from patching the pipeline before it runs.
ranked.reported_results: Pre-deployment scanning and patching achieved 100% leakage reduction under basic jailbreak/instruction-override attacks and 91% under stress-induced manipulation, without runtime policy enforcement (arxiv:2607.18847); an automated privacy-impact-assessment benchmark measures how well LLMs identify privacy risks and mitigation strategies before deployment (arxiv:2609.12571).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a deterministic pattern set to kickoff_guard over recipe DAGs: flag prompt slots that interpolate a whole upstream artifact into a tool-call argument or an outbound URL, and recipes whose tool nodes accept unbounded payloads. Measure on the existing recipe corpus: patterns found, zero false blocks on clean recipes, and patched-vs-unpatched behavior demonstrated on one seeded recipe.

glm.rationale: Recipes are first-party; scanning them for leakage-enabling interpolation is cheap hygiene with weak evidence behind the specific patterns.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py, mini_ork/intake/ - deterministic pattern set over recipe DAGs for leakage-enabling interpolation
minimax.rationale: Pre-deployment scanning and patching achieved 100% leakage reduction under instruction-override attacks without runtime policy enforcement, and intake-gating is fail-closed and cheaper than runtime policing - a recipe whose prompt slots interpolate a whole upstream artifact into a tool-call argument is a concrete, checkable defect. It is next because it is preventive rather than detecting.

ranked.technique: CAUTION: interpretability-based privacy defenses need matched-magnitude controls
ranked.mechanism: CAUTION - a verification-method finding: SAE-feature-based PII suppression in LLM representations is a magnitude artifact. The identified 'PII features' mostly encode token frequency/position magnitude, and ablating random directions with matched magnitude produces equivalent suppression, so with proper controls the technique provides no advantage. Any future adoption of activation- or feature-based privacy defenses must therefore be validated against random-direction and matched-activation controls before the mechanism is trusted. For mini-ork this is an admission rule for defenses rather than a defense: a guard whose measured effect does not beat its magnitude-matched control is an abstention, in line with a fail-closed, evidence-anchored posture.
ranked.reported_results: SAE-based PII suppression provided no advantage with proper controls; the identified features mostly encoded token frequency/position magnitude, and random matched-magnitude directions produced equivalent suppression (arxiv:2611.04782).
ranked.miniork_surface: real sibling: the verification stack's differential checks (docs/architecture/verification-stack.md) - a claimed defense must beat a matched control arm before admission
ranked.adoption_sketch: Encode the control rule in gate admission: a new security gate must be differential-tested against a magnitude- or shuffle-matched control arm, and a gate that does not beat its control is recorded as an abstention rather than a pass. Measure by applying the rule to one existing gate (e.g. gaming scan): its effect size versus a matched control becomes part of the gate's recorded validity.

glm.rationale: The verification stack's differential checks already require a claimed defense to beat a matched control arm, which is exactly the admission rule this caution asks for.

minimax.landing_surface: verification stack's differential checks - a gate must beat a magnitude- or shuffle-matched control arm before admission
minimax.rationale: SAE-based PII suppression provided no advantage with proper controls, and random matched-magnitude directions produced equivalent suppression, so this is an admission rule rather than a defense: a guard whose measured effect does not beat its control is an abstention. It is watch because it rests on one paper and the rule is already covered in substance by G07-T02's marginal-separation requirement for promoting a check to a hard gate.

ranked.technique: Vault-mediated credential execution boundary (secrets never become model context)
ranked.mechanism: Every authenticated action is mediated by the vault at the execution boundary: agent code names a connector or role and the vault performs the authenticated service call, so no reusable credential ever becomes a token in the model's vocabulary - it cannot appear in a prompt, transcript, retained history, log, memory write, or error payload. What it blocks is any path where a configured or pasted key crosses into the data pipeline, from which prompt injection or excessive agency can exfiltrate it. The accept rule is capability-based and deterministic: a node's declared ports authorize the vault to act on its behalf, and everything the LLM itself emits is untrusted - the model is never the enforcement point. It is anchored on an empirical vault-boundary evaluation and on runtime-credential-exposure measurement showing that storage-side hygiene (scanning, rotation, config hardening) leaves most runtime-exposed credentials invisible to static scanners.
ranked.reported_results: Vault-mediated boundary completed authenticated service calls with the agent never holding a reusable credential, and unrelated origins received none (arxiv:2609.33371); best static scanner recovered 36.6% of runtime-exposed credentials vs 77.8% for runtime-aware scanning, F1=0.818, McNemar p<0.001 (arxiv:2609.23042); malicious model code in local fine-tuning stole secrets at over 98% strict ASR in the default LoRA setting (arxiv:2604.27426).
ranked.miniork_surface: vault and per-node secret scope (mini_ork/dispatch/vault.py, mini_ork/remote/secrets_scope.py)
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend the existing per-node secret scope with connector-mediated execution: a node declares a vault connector on its port and the dispatch transport performs the authenticated call, so provider keys are never rendered into prompt env or node scripts. Measure it by minting a canary credential per test run and asserting zero canary bytes across every transcript, log, artifact, and env dump the run produces - today a key in config/secrets.local.sh is one env print away from a transcript.

glm.rationale: The vault ships per-node secret scope, but secrets can still transit prompts when a node invokes a provider directly; moving authenticated calls behind a vault-mediated connector (the agent never holds the credential) is the principled close, L effort.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/dispatch/vault.py, mini_ork/remote/secrets_scope.py - connector-mediated execution so no reusable credential becomes a token in model context
minimax.rationale: The snapshot ships a vault with per-node scoping, but this closes the specific path where a credential crosses into the data pipeline: the best static scanner recovers 36.6% of runtime-exposed credentials against 77.8% for runtime-aware scanning, and malicious model code in local fine-tuning stole secrets at over 98% strict ASR. It is next rather than now because L effort (the dispatch transport must perform the authenticated call) and it does not touch the two named holes.

ranked.technique: Neuro-symbolic verification: LLM-synthesized specifications checked by deterministic engines
ranked.mechanism: The LLM writes what to prove — assertions, invariants, environment models, and verification harnesses — and a deterministic engine (symbolic executor, model checker, solver, proof assistant) renders the verdict, so the verdict never rests on model judgment; every reported bug ships a concrete reproducing test as its evidence. Harnesses are derived from traces of real usage (how tests actually invoke the library) rather than invented, and LLM-inferred invariants serve as relaxed oracles where exact input-output pairs are unavailable. Ablations show the deterministic stage is load-bearing: removing the formal translation collapses recall. Cautions: a fuzz harness reused as a specification proves a single calling scenario rather than the library, and coarse specifications can admit safe but functionally vacuous repairs — so the specification surface must be scoped to the declared contract and reviewed.
ranked.reported_results: Agentic symbolic execution over 1,156,044 lines found 1,050 bugs each reproduced by a concrete test, and its synthesized environment lets the engine execute 81% of 5,406 contracted functions versus 4.5% without (arxiv:2611.15596); removing the deterministic Lean translator collapses recall from 0.5732 to 0.2754 (arxiv:2607.03963); trace-derived harness scenarios extract at 94.66% precision with 100% harness-generation success versus 41% for the prior baseline (arxiv:2607.22161); multi-agent auto-formalization produced verifier-checked outputs for all 220 examples, with vacuity caveats (arxiv:2609.19391); invariant-relaxed oracles detect more functional bugs than fuzzing and prior LLM test generation (arxiv:2607.18711).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Pilot an opt-in symbolic verifier beside metamorphic.py: for the touched Python files of a run, an LLM node proposes assertions scoped to the declared artifact contract, a deterministic engine (CrossHair-style) checks them, and each confirmed bug is emitted with a concrete reproducer into the evidence ledger. Measurement: confirmed bugs per run and false-positive rate on a replayed run set, with an engine-only ablation as the control for the LLM's contribution.

glm.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - LLM-authored specs, deterministic engine verdicts
glm.rationale: LLM-writes-spec, solver-decides is doctrine-perfect and produced 1,050 replayable bugs, but symbolic execution over mini-ork's Python targets is L effort; aim it at authz and invariant properties the deterministic tiers miss.

minimax.landing_surface: code-fix verifier set - an opt-in symbolic verifier beside metamorphic.py
minimax.rationale: Agentic symbolic execution over 1,156,044 lines found 1,050 bugs each reproduced by a concrete test, and removing the deterministic Lean translator collapses recall from 0.5732 to 0.2754, so the deterministic stage is load-bearing. It is watch because a CrossHair-style engine for Python is a large dependency and coarse specifications can admit vacuous repairs, which the technique itself flags.

ranked.technique: Model-internal and inference-time injection defenses (portability caveat)
ranked.mechanism: Defenses that act inside the model at inference time. Causally-gated activation steering fits an instruction-following direction from paired episodes and subtracts it from the residual stream, kept only if it passes pre-specified causal and capability gates; constrained diffusion decoding restricts generation to user-signed workflows; semantic consensus decoding samples responses to paraphrase variants and withholds on divergence; judgment-against-findings re-verification checks every derived judgment against grounded findings so unsupported injections are rejected. Caution on adoption: the white-box variants require weight or serving-stack access that mini-ork does not have over its glm/minimax API lanes. Only the training-free variants — consensus over paraphrased plans and judgment-versus-evidence re-verification — port to verifier nodes. Trained variants additionally fail under adaptive distribution shift unless explicitly trained for it.
ranked.reported_results: Held-out attack success falls from 0.21-1.00 undefended to 0.00-0.17 and AgentDojo compromise from 0.10-0.49 to 0.006-0.079 at 93-100% benign utility across five open-weight models (arxiv:2609.36570); constrained diffusion agents hold 0% ASR across all query budgets including under adaptive attacks where prior defenses exceed 90% (arxiv:2610.15177); semantic consensus decoding cuts ASR 89% to below 3% (arxiv:2602.04195); continual preference optimization yields ~6.3x and 4.4x ASR reductions (arxiv:2608.19982); principled adversarial training keeps adaptive ASR under 5% across 7 benchmarks at 90%+ clean utility (arxiv:2610.41998); judgment-against-findings verification lowers medical multi-agent ASR from up to 61% to 4-7% with clean accuracy maintained (arxiv:2610.22594); POMDP latent-intent inference cuts effective ASR to 3.36%, a 6.50x reduction on 43,777 instances (arxiv:2602.21447); latent instruction-manifold detection reduces over-refusal (arxiv:2608.22248); erased-reference self-distillation reaches near-zero ASR at utility within 0.5 points of clean input (arxiv:2610.41307).
ranked.miniork_surface: lane config — agents.yaml / providers.yaml credential and provider surface
ranked.adoption_sketch: Where a lane serves open weights, fit the steering direction per model behind its causal gate; the API-portable slice is the training-free pair — verify-node re-derivation of each judgment against grounded findings, and consensus checks over paraphrased plans. Measure held-out injection ASR on verify nodes with benign utility held at baseline.

glm.rationale: Activation steering and constrained decoding live inside model serving, which mini-ork rents via glm/minimax lanes; the technique's own portability caveat is decisive.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config - the training-free slice only: consensus over paraphrased plans and judgment-versus-evidence re-verification
minimax.rationale: The white-box variants require weight or serving-stack access that mini-ork does not have over its glm and minimax API lanes, and trained variants fail under adaptive distribution shift unless explicitly trained for it, so only the two training-free mechanisms transfer. It is watch because those two are already covered by techniques inside mini-ork's reach, and the strong numbers behind them (ASR 89% to below 3%) are for the settings mini-ork cannot adopt.

ranked.technique: Lane memorization and extraction audit before routing secret-bearing runs
ranked.mechanism: Before routing sensitive runs to a provider lane, audit the model's regurgitation behavior with planted canaries: seed distinctive synthetic secrets into qualification conversations, then probe in later unrelated queries whether the model reproduces them - output-only and black-box, requiring no weights or token probabilities. Reference-model scoring (a model trained on the complementary half of the corpus) separates true memorization from plausible completion and enables mitigation without knowing sensitive spans in advance, and lifecycle benchmarks warn that defense effectiveness must be compared across attacks and access assumptions rather than a single probe. Accept rule: a lane qualifies for secret-bearing runs only if canary regurgitation stays at zero across the probe battery; otherwise the lane is scoped to non-sensitive runs. Anchored on practical output-only extraction of memorized secrets - including credentials sourced from public repositories - from black-box LLMs.
ranked.reported_results: Output-only access can expose memorized secrets from black-box LLMs, establishing a practical risk for commercial deployments including autonomous coding agents (arxiv:2609.36941); a complementary-corpus reference model isolates targeted memorization and supports prevention without knowing sensitive spans in advance (arxiv:2609.32293); a unified lifecycle benchmark compares 6 attacks, 10 defenses across 4 security objectives, and 2 adaptive attacks under a common threat model (arxiv:2610.00839); decodable-vs-used membership decomposition separates what representations hold from what behavior exposes (arxiv:2610.41445).
ranked.miniork_surface: lane config (agents.yaml / providers.yaml credential and provider surface) - lane qualification for secret-bearing runs
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a lane-qualification script: send N planted canary strings in throwaway conversations, then probe with unrelated prompts and completion prefixes, requiring zero regurgitation before a lane is marked eligible for runs whose artifacts contain real secrets. Measure canary recall rate per lane across a repeated battery with a fixed seed, recorded in the evidence ledger as the lane's recorded validity.

glm.landing_surface: lane config - provider qualification for secret-bearing runs
glm.rationale: Lane memorization audits qualify providers before secret-bearing runs; sensible procurement hygiene once multiple providers routinely see sensitive repos.

minimax.landing_surface: agents.yaml / providers.yaml - a lane-qualification script that probes for regurgitation of planted canaries
minimax.rationale: Output-only access can expose memorized secrets from black-box LLMs, and a complementary-corpus reference model separates true memorization from plausible completion, so a lane must qualify before carrying secret-bearing runs. It is watch rather than next because it is a lane-qualification policy question with only two papers of support and mini-ork's lanes are already configured per-profile.

ranked.technique: Workflow-level fuzzing of agent DAGs with source-to-sink evidence
ranked.mechanism: Single-tool, single-turn safety tests miss vulnerabilities that emerge only across steps: data from one tool persisted and later reused as input to another, long-horizon intent hijacking, task injection, objective drift, memory poisoning. Fuzz at workflow level: enumerate and mutate tool-call chains over the system's real structure, and keep only findings backed by strict source-to-sink dataflow evidence plus an execution trace — mutations that break the graph or lack traces are discarded, so attacks are validated against real structure. Meta-audit your own safety suites the same way (who tests the testers): enumerate valid workflows to find unsafe interactions the suite never covers. Accept a finding only with a reproducing trace; abstain when the trace cannot be grounded.
ranked.reported_results: Evidence-grounded safety suites built this way make existing safety configurations of four production agent frameworks fail almost completely (arxiv:2607.01793); a long-horizon attack benchmark (5 attack types, 644 test cases, 28 environments) shows representative agents highly susceptible and single-turn defenses fail to mitigate (arxiv:2602.16901); enumerating valid tool-call workflows uncovers many unsafe interactions missed by three safety benchmarks across 12 environments (arxiv:2603.18245); the same model is safe or unsafe depending on harness configuration across 6 agents x 24 harnesses (arxiv:2611.11971).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a deterministic workflow-fuzzer pass over the recipe DAG skeleton (nodes + declared ports): generate chain mutations where an untrusted input port feeds a privileged downstream port and assert the artifact contract's visibility limits block them, discarding mutations without a trace. Measure: undeclared source-to-sink paths found and blocked per recipe.

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - fuzzing over the run DAG
glm.rationale: Workflow-level fuzzing of mini-ork's own DAG is a real self-audit but needs a sandboxed target harness and source-to-sink instrumentation that does not ship.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - a deterministic workflow-fuzzer pass over the recipe DAG skeleton
minimax.rationale: Evidence-grounded safety suites built this way made four production agent frameworks fail almost completely, and enumerating valid tool-call workflows found unsafe interactions three safety benchmarks missed, so DAG-level fuzzing is the right shape for the artifact contract. Evidence is moderate and the fixture machinery is substantial relative to the two named holes, so it is watch.

ranked.technique: Blast-radius-aware verification and provenance containment before promotion
ranked.mechanism: Verify an agent-proposed change in a twin or sandbox that models the protected system's state and dependency blast radius, gating production execution on verified effects with rollback confidence — approval rests on what the change does, not its text. Containment composes with provenance: a DAG recording which agent consumed which upstream output lets an alert trace forward and isolate only tainted executions, rather than cancelling the faulty source (missing downstream consumers) or rolling back everything (killing healthy work). After a contamination event, reachability analysis restricts future capabilities to disconnect agent state from forbidden states. Accept rule: promote only if the twin-observed effect set stays inside the declared blast radius; otherwise reject or roll back with the recorded provenance identifying what must be isolated.
ranked.reported_results: Collateral damage rate reduced from 25.6% to 5.2% while maintaining 87.4% recovery rate, at roughly 8 seconds MTTR overhead; sandbox, blast-radius predictor, and rollback-confidence gate each contribute in ablation (arxiv:2609.11264). Provenance-DAG containment blocks all post-alert faulty actuations with zero post-convergence leaks and retains +46 pp more work than full quarantine; native A2A/LangGraph controls contain at most 33.3% of faults (arxiv:2611.06727). Contamination-triggered capability confinement eliminates attack success on three of four AgentDojo suites (4.8%/14.3% on Slack) and outperforms Spotlighting, CaMeL, AttriGuard compositionally (arxiv:2608.30041).
ranked.miniork_surface: `artifact contract` — declared ports and visibility limits give the dependency graph the blast-radius check runs over.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Before the publish gate, run each candidate change's verifier set inside the run's own sandbox twin and diff observed effects (files, egress, transforms) against the artifact contract's declared outputs; anything outside the declared port set blocks promotion with the provenance chain of which node produced it. Measure: collateral-effect rate on seeded bad changes versus the declared-contract baseline, and recovery/utility on unchanged runs.

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - blast-radius check over declared ports
glm.rationale: Verification-in-twin before promotion is roughly mini-ork's worktree-plus-green-gate shape already; the blast-radius predictor and provenance-DAG containment are the new parts and need a contamination event to pay for.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - declared ports and visibility limits give the dependency graph the blast-radius check runs over
minimax.rationale: Verifying a change in a twin and diffing observed effects against the declared port set is the right shape (collateral damage 25.6% to 5.2% with 87.4% recovery; provenance-DAG containment retains 46pp more work than full quarantine). Effort is L because it needs a sandbox twin of the protected system, and it overlaps the effect-validation work inside the verifier, so it is watch.

ranked.technique: Caution: third-party model artifacts carry benchmark-passing backdoors - procurement, not scanning
ranked.mechanism: Caution technique: any third-party model is a supply-chain artifact that can carry trigger-conditioned behavior while passing utility benchmarks. Structured-output backdoors emit attacker-chosen tool calls at up to 96.2% ASR in coding agents and the backdoored model can beat the clean baseline on utility benchmarks; 0.1% pretraining poisoning survives SFT, DPO, and RLVR; 1,000 SFT-then-GRPO samples evade leaderboard evaluation and conventional safety checks; and benchmark-incentivized poisoning keeps at least 90.33% attack success after decontamination. Theory shows a broad class of backdoored networks is statistically undetectable even with white-box access, so weight scanning cannot be the control. For an API consumer the mitigations are procurement-grade: heterogeneous-model cross-checking where independent lanes must agree before promotion, evidence-ledger recording of model and version per node, and treating a model or version swap as a re-vetting event rather than a drop-in replacement.
ranked.reported_results: Kerkoporta: up to 96.2% ASR; backdoored models can outperform the clean baseline on utility benchmarks (arxiv:2611.00138). Pretraining poisoning at 0.1% of the corpus persists through SFT, DPO, RLVR and strengthens with scale (arxiv:2610.37741). Sleeper Cell: 1,000 samples suffice while evading leaderboard evaluation (arxiv:2603.03371). BenchDoor: 82.33-100.00% held-out ASR with positive benchmark gains in all 30 configurations; at least 90.33% ASR survives decontamination (arxiv:2610.27533). Weight-space defenses exist but assume weight access: null-space purification 100% to 0.5% ASR (arxiv:2610.00685), LLM trigger inversion cuts ASR 76.2% (arxiv:2603.15692), black-box test-time purification drops image-text backdoor ASR 99.18% to 3.43% (arxiv:2606.29451), activation realignment drives ASR below 1% (arxiv:2611.14143); undetectability is proven for a broad network class (arxiv:2607.09532). For code models specifically, black-box vulnerability-oriented probing improves recall where token-level inversion fails (33.3-50% even with the ground-truth first token) (arxiv:2603.17174), and a tool-use backdoor exfiltrates memory via disguised retrieval calls at >96% ASR and <0.3% FPR (arxiv:2604.05432).
ranked.miniork_surface: lane config - agents.yaml / providers.yaml model and provider selection.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Record model plus version per node in the evidence ledger, require the dual-reviewer disagreement flag to block promotion of any single-lane verdict, and route model/version changes in providers.yaml through the merge risk gate as a high-risk path. Measurement: the historical share of promotions resting on a single model family, before and after the rule.

glm.landing_surface: lane config - agents.yaml / providers.yaml model selection
glm.rationale: A procurement caution for hosted lanes: pin providers and record model ids per run, which providers.yaml already does implicitly; no verifier-node-sized build exists here.

minimax.landing_surface: agents.yaml / providers.yaml model and provider selection; evidence ledger records model plus version per node
minimax.rationale: The snapshot says a model swap is a procurement decision, not a scanning one, and the actionable slice is cheap: record model and version per node in the evidence ledger, treat a version change as a re-vetting event, and require the two independent lanes to agree before promotion. Weight-space defenses are unreachable for API lanes and the whole class is provably undetectable, so the impact is bounded at 3.

ranked.technique: NL/PL boundary information-flow labels for secret flow through model calls
ranked.mechanism: Give dataflow analyses callee summaries at LLM API calls: label each model-call edge with an information-preservation level - from output fully determined by input to output potentially containing anything, including injected or training-derived content - derived from measured real call pairs, so taint tracking crosses the natural-language/programming-language boundary instead of stopping (or silently assuming transformation) at every model call. The enforcement consequence: a secret that flows into a prompt at a low-preservation call is treated as disclosed to logs and downstream systems, not as confined, and secret scanning extends from source files to run transcripts and prompts. The conservative default fails closed: unlabeled call edges are treated as non-preserving. Anchored on measured preservation labels, not assumptions about model behavior.
ranked.reported_results: A 24-label taxonomy of information-preservation levels and output modalities, labeled on 9,083 placeholder-output pairs from 4,154 real LLM calls and grounded in quantitative information flow theory (arxiv:2603.28345).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Start conservative: treat every LLM-call edge in run transcripts as non-preserving, extend the secret scan to prompts and transcripts under the run dir, and fail closed on any secret appearing in a prompt. Measure secrets detected in existing transcripts (seeded fixtures should give a controlled nonzero count) and false negatives on seeded transcript fixtures, then refine edge labels from measured call pairs.

glm.landing_surface: secret scan - information-flow labels at model-call edges
glm.rationale: A research taxonomy from one paper; the vault already keeps secrets out of prompts, which is the flow that matters.

minimax.landing_surface: secret scan - conservative labels on LLM-call edges, with the scan extended to run transcripts and prompts
minimax.rationale: The information-preservation taxonomy (24 labels over 9,083 placeholder-output pairs from 4,154 real calls) is the principled way to stop a secret flowing into a prompt from being treated as confined, and the conservative default - treat every LLM-call edge as non-preserving - is cheap. It is watch because the label measurement campaign is a project in itself.

ranked.technique: Telemetry-only anomaly monitoring with budgeted audit-point placement
ranked.mechanism: Detects failing or runaway agents from observable telemetry alone — step embeddings, token-level uncertainty, action metadata, heartbeats — using one-class ensembles trained only on healthy runs (no failure labels) with CUSUM change detection plus deterministic completion checks, at microseconds per step. Unbounded agentic loops, the budget-exhaustion failure, are caught by static analysis plus framework modeling with LLM confirmation and benign-loop filtering. In a DAG runtime, audit points are placed under a fixed budget that minimizes cumulative unchecked exposure — a greedy schedule favoring influential and long-unaudited regions — with trusted checkpoints enabling localized recovery, and failures are attributed to the faulty node via influence graphs over agents, tools, and artifacts rather than by humans rereading raw logs. Accept = telemetry within control limits; alarm = CUSUM threshold crossing, an abstention from 'healthy' that triggers recovery; regions left unmeasured by the budget are explicitly accounted, never silently trusted.
ranked.reported_results: One-class echo-state monitors with CUSUM alarms over step telemetry cost microseconds per step, trained only on healthy runs (arxiv:2608.02464); adaptive influence graphs achieve state-of-the-art failure attribution on Who&When-style benchmarks (arxiv:2608.24361).
ranked.adoption_sketch: In each recipe's workflow.yaml, choose which nodes get verifier gates by minimizing cumulative unchecked exposure under the existing gate budget (greedy: influential and long-unaudited first), and run a CUSUM monitor over per-node heartbeat and turn telemetry trained on healthy runs only. Measurement: same verification budget with lower maximum unchecked path length, and a seeded runaway loop alarms before the node timeout.

glm.rationale: Telemetry anomaly monitoring detects failing runs, not security defects; the shipped heartbeat and timeout envelope already catches the runaway class.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - audit-point placement under a fixed gate budget plus a CUSUM monitor over per-node telemetry
minimax.rationale: One-class monitors with CUSUM alarms over step telemetry cost microseconds per step trained only on healthy runs, and placing audit points by influence under a fixed budget is a principled answer to the snapshot's unstated coverage question. It is watch because it optimizes where the gates should go, which only becomes urgent once there are enough gates to budget.

ranked.technique: Agent census, incident registry, and tier-accountable safeguard mapping
ranked.mechanism: Governance infrastructure that knows which agents are actually deployed and which mitigation is accountable for which threat: censuses of repository instruction files and CI workflow histories surface agent invocations that resemble ordinary automation; shadow-agent detection on endpoints separates sanctioned from unsanctioned agents by service identity rather than behavioral-twin rules; and a coded incident registry keeps causal role, disclosure class, and realized outcome separate so a demonstrated vulnerability is not counted as field harm. Threats map to accountable mitigations through atomic attack-safeguard taxonomies and a cascading decision tree assigning each vulnerability (e.g., the OWASP MCP Top 10) to the tier — server, gateway, or protocol — that can actually mitigate it, since some vulnerabilities cannot be fixed within a server's development lifecycle. Accept = every registered tool and agent has a tier assignment plus an accountable mitigation owner; reject = unassigned exposure blocks admission; abstain = unmapped novel threat, escalated to a human.
ranked.reported_results: Agent instructions appear in 26.3% of 22,854 repositories (59.6% of the most-starred) and 74.0% of directives give no reason (arxiv:2610.31715); an SoK screens 186 sources, retains 98, and yields 284 atomic attacks, 452 safeguards, and 660 attack-safeguard relationships (arxiv:2611.10843); 487 agent incidents 2022-2026 are coded by causal role, disclosure class, and realized outcome (arxiv:2609.11030); 25,014 agentic workflows are linked to 4,112,526 run records (arxiv:2611.06866).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Apply the three-tier mapping to mini-ork's registered tool servers — each MCP/tool entry gets a tier assignment and an accountable mitigation owner in the tool registry — and feed the reflect node's lessons into a coded incident registry that keeps causal role and realized outcome separate. Measurement: no registered tool lacks a tier and owner, and recurring failures become queryable registry entries.

glm.rationale: Census and registry governance is org-scale bookkeeping; the incident-registry taxonomy could inform the reflect step but nothing gates on it.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - a tier assignment and accountable mitigation owner per registered tool
minimax.rationale: The governance inventory is sound (agent instructions appear in 26.3% of 22,854 repositories; 284 atomic attacks and 452 safeguards from an SoK of 186 sources), but mini-ork has a handful of registered tools and a tool registry, not an agent fleet to census, and a coded incident registry duplicates the reflect node's lessons. It does not touch either named hole, so it is skipped.

ranked.technique: Evidence-constrained indicator and CVE enrichment with dependency-graph prioritization
ranked.mechanism: Turn unstructured vulnerability and threat text into structured, prioritized signals under explicit anti-hallucination constraints: extract only indicators the surrounding context actually supports (context-only constraint), predict missing severity metadata by retrieval and structured reasoning over historical CVEs before authoritative scores arrive, and prioritize by propagating exploitation risk through the dependency and asset graph to what the organization actually ships. The caution is kept: LLMs were shown to lack nuanced CTI expertise and cannot reliably distinguish correct from incorrect information, and domain-type indicators are where hallucination concentrates - so enriched output is a ranked hypothesis for a human, never an autonomous verdict.
ranked.reported_results: 0.958 precision and perfect recall (1.0) for actual threats at 0.788 specificity, with domain-type indicators performing poorly and 37.89% of STIX objects redundant (arxiv:2601.09029); macro F1 around 0.80 predicting eventual NVD CVSS vectors from pre-NVD disclosures (arxiv:2611.06477); benchmark finding that LLMs cannot reliably distinguish correct from incorrect CTI information (arxiv:2603.09452).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Rank `make secrets` and dependency findings by reachability: propagate each finding through the repo's import/dependency graph to the artifacts that actually ship, so unreachable findings rank below reachable ones regardless of raw severity. Measure on a historical finding set with known-exploited items - reachability ranking should place the exploited items in the top-k more often than severity-order alone.

glm.rationale: CTI enrichment and CVSS prediction are threat-intel workflows, not pipeline defenses.

minimax.landing_surface: secret scan - reachability-weighted prioritization of findings
minimax.rationale: Ranking findings by dependency-graph reachability overlaps G05-T11, which covers the same property with the stronger measured result (86% mean-rank reduction of the first confirmed-exploitable CVE), and the CTI-enrichment framing here is aimed at external threat intelligence that mini-ork does not consume. It is skipped as redundant.

ranked.technique: Distribution-anomaly detection of extraction queries against agent memory
ranked.mechanism: Defend queryable agent memory and RAG corpora against extraction by modeling the entropy and margin distributions of retrieval behavior over benign traffic and flagging query sequences whose distributional fingerprint targets sensitive records - the narrow, high-margin, coverage-seeking pattern of adaptive extraction campaigns. It detects the attack class that defeats storage-side countermeasures: entropy-guided, multi-turn, evolving-memory querying that accumulates a victim corpus record by record at negligible cost, and blocks flagged sequences at the query boundary. CAUTION: semantic rewriting of stored records is measured to be no defense against these attacks, and even strong defenses must be evaluated against adaptive multi-turn adversaries across every user-visible channel including tool traces, where a residual attack success rate persists.
ranked.reported_results: Entropy-margin malicious-query detection significantly reduced PII leakage (unique leakage chunks, PII count, attack success rate) against four attack strategies and four defense baselines on HealthcareMagic-101 and Enron across four LLMs (arxiv:2609.16095); entropy-guided adaptive extraction reached ASR 1.00 (vs 0.89 for MEXTRA) at as little as $0.0026 per run, and all rewriting strategies still yielded PII exposure (arxiv:2604.09747); all 8 tested science-agent platforms leaked at least one protected skill to evolving-memory extraction, and the strongest defense still admitted 16.7% ASR (arxiv:2610.34365).
ranked.miniork_surface: real sibling: the semantic-memory query path (mini_ork/memory/semantic.py) and run-scoped retrieval
ranked.adoption_sketch: Log every semantic-memory query with its score distribution and flag runs whose pattern matches extraction probing - many narrow high-margin queries over the same record cluster. Measure by replaying an entropy-guided extraction script against a seeded memory and requiring the flag to fire before the corpus is substantially captured, with zero flags across a corpus of normal runs.

glm.rationale: Extraction-anomaly detection defends a queryable memory service; mini-ork's retrieval is run-scoped and not externally reachable.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/memory/semantic.py - log every query with its score distribution and flag extraction-shaped sequences
minimax.rationale: Entropy-margin detection of narrow, high-margin, coverage-seeking query sequences addresses the extraction attack that storage-side countermeasures miss, and adaptive extraction reached ASR 1.00 at as little as $0.0026 per run. It is watch because it presumes a queryable memory exposed to repeated probing, which the local index and per-node scoping currently limit.

ranked.technique: Static cryptographic-asset discovery and CBOM-style governance inventory
ranked.mechanism: Static discovery of cryptographic assets under a three-class taxonomy - crypto material (keys, certs), crypto assets (configured algorithms and protocols), and crypto invocations (calls in code) - driven by an extensible scanner-independent rule repository, with findings normalized into CBOM-oriented output annotated with CWE/CVE weaknesses and post-quantum migration candidates. It detects dormant cryptographic debt that neither secret scanning nor linting sees, because the findings are usages rather than secrets: weak primitives, expiring certs, PQC-vulnerable key exchange. Accept rule: findings are inventoried and diffed over time - a change that adds a weak or unmigrated invocation fails the gate; unsupported language surfaces are reported as unscanned (abstention), never silently passed.
ranked.reported_results: F1 0.75 for asset discovery on a ground-truth benchmark with 91% of expected weaknesses and vulnerabilities correctly annotated; processed 57,610 files in under six minutes on a real ten-service infrastructure, discovering 370 cryptographic assets including 6 CVE-linked vulnerabilities and 52 post-quantum migration candidates (arxiv:2608.04857).
ranked.miniork_surface: secret scan (make secrets and the pinned CI scanning) extended with a CBOM-style crypto-asset inventory as a sibling output
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a rules-based pass over the repo (and run dirty sets) classifying crypto material, assets, and invocations into a committed inventory that CI diffs alongside gitleaks. Measure on mini-ork's own tree: inventory contents (expected: TLS/cert handling in remote providers, hashing in the evidence ledger), zero false blocks, and the diff catching a deliberately planted weak-primitive invocation.

glm.landing_surface: secret scan - CBOM-style crypto-asset inventory sibling output
glm.rationale: Crypto-asset inventory finds dormant cryptographic debt; real value, off the critical path of the verifier-set hole.

minimax.landing_surface: secret scan - a CBOM-style crypto-asset inventory diffed alongside gitleaks
minimax.rationale: It inventories crypto material, assets and invocations rather than secrets, finding 370 assets and 52 post-quantum migration candidates across 57,610 files in under six minutes, which is a category neither secret scanning nor linting sees. It is watch because the value to mini-ork today is speculative - no PQC migration is on the roadmap - and unsupported language surfaces must be reported as unscanned rather than silently passed.

ranked.technique: Dependency-guided rollback and execution-state unlearning of poisoned persistent state
ranked.mechanism: When a poisoned or invalidated persistent record is identified, repair must propagate through derived artifacts: a provenance/dependency graph identifies every summary, plan, decision, and downstream node that consumed the record, deactivates the unsupported state, and selectively replays only the affected computation. Deleting the source record alone is measurably insufficient - instruction-based forgetting leaks at probe rate 1.00 and redaction still acts on the revoked preference in 80% of episodes - and exact unlearning has a formal lower bound of at least T-tau+1 recomputed transitions, which provenance-guided selective replay attains at up to 9x fewer recomputed tokens than full reset. Accept a repair only when downstream re-execution without the record reproduces the outcome; abstain and escalate to full reset when replay is unaffordable.
ranked.reported_results: Dependency-guided rollback repair: 85.3% recovery versus 77.3% for the best competing method; claim-invalidation F1 0.669 versus 0.603 (arxiv:2608.10502). Instruction-based forgetting Leak@probes=1.00; redaction still acts on revoked preference in 80% of episodes; provenance-guided selective replay is indistinguishable from full reset at up to 9x fewer recomputed tokens (arxiv:2609.04875).
ranked.miniork_surface: evidence ledger and traces - provenance edges over run state, lessons, and the worktree claim registry's cross-session records.
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a provenance edge from every ledger row to the artifacts, lessons, and claims that consumed it, plus a revoke operation that marks a source record and all transitive dependents stale and re-queues only those nodes. Measurement: plant a poisoned lesson consumed by k downstream runs, revoke it, and verify all k re-derive while untouched runs are not re-executed.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger - provenance edges over run state and lessons
glm.rationale: Rollback and unlearning machinery pays off only after a demonstrated lesson-poisoning incident, and the provenance-graph substrate it needs does not ship yet.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - provenance edges over run state, lessons, and the worktree claim registry's cross-session records
minimax.rationale: Repair propagation (a revoked lesson must invalidate its dependents, with provenance-guided selective replay reaching indistinguishable-from-reset quality at up to 9x fewer tokens) is a real property the snapshot's ledger does not have. It is remediation after a poisoning event rather than a detector, and it depends on G01-T01's provenance stamps, so it is watch.

ranked.technique: Cross-domain NL+code analysis of agent skills (supply-chain skill scanning)
ranked.mechanism: Agent skills and recipe prompt+code bundles are hybrid artifacts where malicious intent emerges from instruction/code/tool interactions that per-artifact rule matching and single-pass LLM judgment miss. Compile the natural-language instructions into an intermediate representation, merge it with the bundled code on one program-dependence graph, and propagate trust/sensitivity/capability taints to flag capability flows (file writes, network, exec) crossing trust boundaries; static taint evidence is then correlated with dynamic traces of the skill executing under safety constraints before an agentic judgment is rendered. Quarantine on corroborated cross-layer evidence; report isolated static matches as leads, not findings. Anchored on cross-layer dataflow, catching behavior invisible to either artifact type alone.
ranked.reported_results: Compiling skill instructions to an IR analyzed jointly with bundled code reaches 85.6% accuracy, 95.2% recall, and F1 86.9%, and confirms 627 malicious skills among 66,157 real marketplace skills (arxiv:2610.33489); cross-layer evidence correlation reaches F1 0.89 with 5 false positives on 140 held-out skills, where a shipped scanner's default configuration gives 0.91 recall with 33 false positives on 60 benign skills (arxiv:2611.10830).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Run a pilot scanner over mini-ork's own skills and recipe bundles: compile prompts to an IR, taint capability flows (file write, network, exec) from instructions to bundled code to declared tools, and quarantine only on boundary crossings corroborated by a sandboxed dynamic trace. Measure detection on known-malicious fixtures modeled on the papers' skill taxonomy versus grep and single-pass LLM judgment, and false positives on the repo's existing benign skills.

glm.rationale: Joint NL+code skill analysis presumes a marketplace of third-party skills; mini-ork recipes are first-party and reviewed.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - cross-layer NL+code scanning of skills and recipe bundles
minimax.rationale: Compiling skill instructions to an IR analyzed jointly with bundled code reaches 85.6% accuracy and 95.2% recall and confirms 627 malicious skills among 66,157 real marketplace skills, which is a plausible read of the snapshot's unmeasured tool surface. It is watch because the pipeline (IR compilation plus taint propagation plus a sandboxed dynamic trace) is a research-scale component for a small internal tool set.

ranked.technique: Tool-surface attack testing: adversarial-argument fuzzing and leakage taint analysis of MCP tools
ranked.mechanism: Treat LLM-generated tool arguments as untrusted inputs to the tools themselves: replay injection-shaped arguments (for example verbatim repeat-after-me payloads) against tool implementations in a sandbox and fuzz them at scale, and in parallel run protocol-guided taint analysis over tool-server code to find credentials, API keys, and PII crossing trust boundaries through tool inputs and outputs. A finding requires an observed boundary crossing or an executed adversarial call succeeding; 'looks dangerous' is a lead. Anchored on executed tool behavior and cross-language taint evidence - the technique mini-ork's own MCP surface should be tested with, not merely shipped alongside.
ranked.reported_results: A corpus of 1,404 tool-exposing repos with 24,194 extracted tools, of which 417 were built and executed with at least one successful call, underpins fuzzing of MCP tool implementations with adversarial LLM-generated arguments (arxiv:2610.13651); protocol-guided cross-language taint analysis was evaluated on 10,655 real-world MCP servers for credentials, keys, and PII crossing trust boundaries (arxiv:2606.21338).
ranked.adoption_sketch: In a sandbox, point a small harness at mini-ork's registered tool servers: replay adversarial-shaped arguments and run the protocol-guided taint check for credentials and PII crossing tool input/output boundaries. Measure confirmed boundary-crossing findings and the fraction of the registered tool surface the harness covers.

glm.rationale: Tool-argument fuzzing and taint analysis target a tool-server fleet mini-ork does not run.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - adversarial-argument fuzzing and protocol-guided taint analysis of registered tool servers
minimax.rationale: The corpus (1,404 tool-exposing repos, 24,194 extracted tools) and the cross-language taint analysis over 10,655 real MCP servers make this a real hole for the tool surface, and the accept rule (an observed boundary crossing or an executed adversarial call) is deterministic. It is watch because mini-ork's registered tool surface is a fraction of that and the harness cost is not small.

ranked.technique: Workflow-level tail-risk gating for merge and promotion
ranked.mechanism: Gates a multi-step agent workflow on accumulated risk instead of verifying each step independently: risk is modeled as transitions between dependent steps, step-wise tail-risk distributions are estimated by sampling, and the workflow outcome is gated when accumulated tail risk exceeds a set bound. Severity is weighted by execution likelihood — the conditional probability a threat is actually realized given the response — rather than treated as uniform across findings. Release decisions become multi-signal (task success, safety pass rate, evidence coverage, cost, latency) with explicit PROMOTE / HOLD / ROLLBACK outcomes, and longitudinal evidence about the gate's own detection adequacy is bound to each current decision so assurance does not silently go stale as policy or the auditor's behavior changes. Accept = all signals within policy; HOLD or ROLLBACK = any dimension below its floor; a gate that cannot measure holds rather than passes. Anchored on measured per-step outcomes across runs, not on model opinion.
ranked.reported_results: Tail-risk gating improves safety while preserving utility against eleven defense baselines across three benchmarks and six backbones (arxiv:2611.10411).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Extend mini_ork/gates/merge_risk.py so risk-tiers.yaml severities are weighted by per-surface execution likelihood and accumulated across the run's dependent steps into a tail-risk score that can HOLD, with posture bound to the current decision as in continuous assurance. Measurement: seeded multi-step changes whose individual steps are low-tier but joint effect is high get held, while single-file benign merges are unaffected.

glm.rationale: Sampled tail-risk gating is heavy machinery for merge decisions mini-ork already makes on deterministic green gates plus risk tiers.

minimax.landing_surface: merge risk gate and approvals - tail-risk accumulation across dependent steps
minimax.rationale: Gating a workflow on accumulated tail risk across dependent steps, with severity weighted by execution likelihood, is the right shape for the snapshot's risk-tier gate, and the evidence that a gate which cannot measure holds rather than passes matches the doctrine. It is watch because the paper's evidence is a single benchmark result and the accumulation model is a research artifact.

ranked.technique: Constraint-checked, effect-validated response planning
ranked.mechanism: The model generates candidate response actions but never executes them on trust: each candidate is checked against explicit system constraints and lookahead predictions in an iterative loop, and execution goes through a harness (or digital twin of the affected estate) that validates the action's actual effect before it counts as done. Historical experiences carry recovery-effect records that later incidents retrieve, so planning improves from observed outcomes rather than plan text. Accept/reject rule: an action is accepted only when its observed effect matches the predicted effect in the harness; mismatch triggers replanning. The anchor is the measured environment state, not the plan's narrative.
ranked.reported_results: Normalized defense score 0.94 across 100 Docker-based cyber ranges, +9.5% over the strongest baseline (arxiv:2608.09524); recovery times reduced by up to 30% versus frontier LLMs across four public datasets (arxiv:2602.05279); 23% shorter recovery time from a lightweight 14B end-to-end agent (arxiv:2602.13156).
ranked.adoption_sketch: For code-fix runs, validate the remediation's effect in the per-node sandbox before promotion: apply the patch, re-run the originally failing test plus one metamorphic neighbor, and promote only when the observed effect matches the predicted fix, recording the recovery effect in the evidence ledger for later retrieval. Measure on historically reverted fixes - the effect check should block a meaningful share of the fixes that later regressed while passing the ones that held.

glm.rationale: Constraint-checked response planning is incident-response machinery; mini-ork does not execute containment actions.

minimax.landing_surface: sandbox placement and per-node sandbox - validate a remediation's effect in the per-node sandbox before promotion
minimax.rationale: Promoting only when the observed effect matches the predicted effect, with recovery-effect records retrievable later, is the right shape for verifying a remediation rather than reviewing its text. It is watch because the evidence comes from cyber-range deployments rather than from code-fix runs, and the effect check overlaps the paired oracle's fail-to-pass transition.

ranked.technique: Live, adaptive, open-ended evaluation of defenders (static metrics mislead)
ranked.mechanism: Evaluate defensive components in live turn-by-turn interaction against adaptive adversaries and on open-ended telemetry (a raw event database with no guided questions), and score success at the system-impact level - whether unauthorized, harmful, persistent state change occurred - rather than at the model-response level. Kept as a caution technique because the retrieved results are mostly negative: frontier models fail open-ended hunts and miss silent intrusions while reliably finding alert-exposed problems, command-level correctness metrics do not predict real deception success, and single-direction static probes do not generalize across contexts - deceptive/evasive behavior lives in context-dependent multi-dimensional subspaces. The actionable rule: a defense's grade comes from the final iteration of an adaptive attack, never from a static fixture set.
ranked.reported_results: Best frontier model reaches Coverage Score 0.55+/-0.05 across 859 runs and none completes a hunt (arxiv:2604.19533); no model achieves complete detection plus remediation on any of 10 cyber ranges, agents chase alert-exposed problems and miss silent intrusions (arxiv:2607.26791); a 99.02% shell-behavior unit-test pass rate did not improve blind human deception rates (arxiv:2606.27990); subspace probes reach AUROC 0.97 and 94% recall at 5% FPR with 10 examples per dataset where single-direction probes fail to generalize (arxiv:2610.27577); only 7 of 22 reviewed studies report any concrete defense evaluation (arxiv:2609.23894).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Convert one static gaming-scan fixture into an adaptive loop: an attacker node iteratively mutates a diff to evade the current gate, the gate re-runs each iteration, and the gate's published score is the final-iteration evasion rate rather than the first-pass rate. Measure evasion at iteration N versus first-pass, plus the cost per iteration to keep the loop affordable.

glm.rationale: Mostly negative findings about defender evaluation; the transferable rule (system-impact scoring, not model-response scoring) is already how the probe and tripwire are framed.

minimax.landing_surface: gaming scan - an adaptive attacker loop whose published score is the final-iteration evasion rate
minimax.rationale: A defense's grade should come from the final iteration of an adaptive attack rather than a static fixture set, and the retrieved results here are mostly negative (best frontier model reaches Coverage Score 0.55 and none completes a hunt), which is itself the argument. It is watch because it is the same adaptive-evaluation instrument as G02-T02 and G08-T07, and it should be one build, not three.

ranked.technique: Activation-level probes and circuit interventions (caution: weight-access dependent)
ranked.mechanism: Detects adversarial or compromised inputs and strengthens refusal at the model's internal-representation level: k-NN ensembles over residual-stream activations classify jailbreaks and prompt injections during a single forward pass, modal-agnostic and without architectural modification; malicious behavior in multi-agent systems is flagged from internal activations without inter-agent graph modeling; and a characterized detection-to-refusal circuit can be scaled training-free to harden refusal, optionally as a permanent weight edit. Accept = activation score over threshold, flagging or blocking the input; pass-as-benign only with high margin; abstain = no weight access, which is the normal case for API lanes. Caution: vulnerability information is encoded relationally, so linear categorical probes underperform — code models reliably rank relative risk while overlapping distributions defeat classification — and deception features form context-dependent subspaces, so static single-direction probes fail to generalize across datasets; probes must be re-validated per context rather than deployed as fixed directions.
ranked.reported_results: Activation-based detection is state-of-the-art among open-weight detectors and surpasses a closed proprietary judge on combined text and visual F1 (arxiv:2604.06247); vulnerability information is relationally encoded, so linear categorical probes underperform across 8 code LLMs (arxiv:2610.27257); deception features form context-dependent subspaces, so static single-direction probes fail to generalize (arxiv:2610.27577).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Watch-level only: when a lane serves an open-weight model, evaluate an activation guard as one extra detector input to the gate; for API-only lanes record it as not applicable rather than approximating it. Measurement: detection lift on a poisoning probe set, with the published negative results (linear-probe failure, context-dependent feature composition) reproduced before any reliance on it.

glm.rationale: Activation-level probes need weight access mini-ork's hosted lanes (glm/minimax) do not expose, and the relational-encoding caution undercuts probe transfer to code security.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config - an activation guard as one extra detector input for open-weight lanes only
minimax.rationale: Activation-based detection is state-of-the-art among open-weight detectors, but vulnerability information is relationally encoded so linear probes underperform across 8 code LLMs, and deception features form context-dependent subspaces where static single-direction probes fail to generalize. mini-ork's glm and minimax lanes are API lanes with no weight access, so this is not applicable to the two-tier shipping target and is watch at most.

ranked.technique: Provenance gating of observations promoted from untrusted artifacts
ranked.mechanism: When a pipeline promotes observations extracted from untrusted artifacts - tool reports, decompiled output, repository files, retrieved documents - into evidence or instructions, validate each promoted observation against its origin (re-extraction, source binding) before it counts: representation-confusion attacks live at exactly that promotion step, making data read as code or one origin read as many. Observations that fail origin validation are demoted to untrusted context and cannot anchor gate decisions. Anchored on origin-validation checks, trading some recall for refusing to build conclusions on attacker-shaped input - the same fail-closed posture as the evidence ledger.
ranked.reported_results: A Provenance Gate validating promoted observations against their origin reduces false validation relative to a Support Gate on the same drafts in shared-root cases without changing any positive-control decision (arxiv:2607.12507).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add an origin pointer (artifact path plus span hash) to every promoted observation in the evidence ledger, and have the publish gate re-extract a sample before counting it as evidence. Measure promoted observations failing re-verification on adversarial fixture transcripts seeded with representation-confusion content, versus a no-gate baseline.

glm.landing_surface: evidence ledger - origin validation of promoted observations
glm.rationale: Origin validation of promoted observations fits the evidence ledger, but the evidence is one paper on shared-root drafting - too thin to build on now.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - an origin pointer per promoted observation
minimax.rationale: Origin validation at the promotion step, where representation-confusion attacks live, is the right place for a fail-closed demotion, and the evidence is thin (one paper, a shared-root comparison against a Support Gate). It is watch: worth prototyping inside the evidence ledger, but the evidence base does not support ranking it.

ranked.technique: Network-behavior guardrail for tool supply chains
ranked.mechanism: Judge an MCP/tool by what it actually does on the network at runtime, not by its description, README, or a static scan of its code: observe the tool's real outbound interactions from inside the sandbox where it runs and compare them against the behavior its contract declares. The companion benchmark - malicious tools generated from an ATT&CK-derived taxonomy - carries the caution: existing MCP scanners and semantic guardrails perform poorly against supply-chain injections, so static analysis is the weak anchor here. Block rule: undeclared egress or contact with unlisted destinations blocks the tool for the run. The anchor is observed interaction, which a malicious tool cannot fully fake if it wants its payload to work.
ranked.reported_results: SC-Inject-Bench contributes over 10,000 malicious MCP tools grounded in a taxonomy of 25+ attack types derived from MITRE ATT&CK; existing MCP scanners and semantic guardrails perform poorly on it (arxiv:2604.04426).
ranked.adoption_sketch: On first use of each declared MCP tool, record its observed network and process behavior inside the per-node sandbox and diff it against the tool's declared contract in the run manifest; any undeclared contact blocks the tool for the rest of the run. Measure by seeding a test tool that phones home - the behavior diff must block it - while tools operating within their declared contract pass untouched.

glm.rationale: Network-behavior guardrails for MCP tools; the benchmark's own finding is that scanners handle this poorly, and mini-ork has no MCP fleet.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - observe each tool's real network behavior in the sandbox and diff it against its declared contract
minimax.rationale: Judging a tool by observed egress rather than its description is the right anchor, and the companion benchmark (10,000+ malicious MCP tools; existing scanners perform poorly) sets the honest expectation. It is watch because the evidence base is one benchmark paper and the mechanism overlaps the sandbox placement work in G03-T02.

ranked.technique: Semantic information-flow labels across the run DAG
ranked.mechanism: Labels data and subtask outputs with security tags and propagates them from sources through the workflow to sinks; a sink (tool call, publish effect, credential use) accepts input only if its label policy allows it. Full upstream propagation recovers the attack path, so a harmful objective fragmented into locally plausible subtasks — which no single node flags — is still caught at the sink, and taint-hiding attacks mostly fail. Accept: label-compatible flow; reject: labeled-untrusted input reaching a privileged sink; abstain: label violations route to operator review. Single-paper evidence, so treat as a candidate to pilot rather than a settled mechanism.
ranked.reported_results: Average ASR falls 69.3% to 12.7% under a 7-label policy (TCR 90.6%, FPR 5.9%) and to 10.4% at 6.1% FPR under 10 labels; full-upstream propagation raises path recovery 63.5% to 89.2% and drops ASR 25.4% to 12.4%; taint-hiding succeeds 23.0% versus 85.9% undefended (arxiv:2607.25255).
ranked.miniork_surface: artifact contract — declared ports, run-local manifests, transforms, and visibility limits
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a taint label to artifact manifests (untrusted-at-rest versus run-produced) that transforms propagate automatically, and make the publish gate refuse labeled-untrusted content absent an explicit approval. Measure: a cross-node taint test where an untrusted artifact tries to reach the publisher through two transforms is refused.

glm.landing_surface: artifact contract - security labels propagated across the DAG
glm.rationale: Single-paper evidence (69.3% to 12.7% ASR) for label propagation; the artifact contract could carry labels, but the policy set is unvalidated outside that paper.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - taint labels on artifact manifests that transforms propagate automatically
minimax.rationale: A 7-label policy cuts average ASR from 69.3% to 12.7% at 5.9% FPR, and full upstream propagation raises path recovery from 63.5% to 89.2%, so the shape fits the shipped declared-ports model. It is watch because it rests on a single paper and a 7-to-10 label policy is a design project, which is a weaker case than the techniques above it in this group.

ranked.technique: Conformal and anytime-valid risk certification composed across pipeline gates
ranked.mechanism: Per-gate error rates are calibrated on held-out labelled outcomes and composed into a trajectory-level risk certificate using valid spanning-tree combination — the naive pairwise-correlation extension to three or more stages is invalid and yields only a lower bound. Promotion is blocked when the composed risk bound exceeds the declared budget; the certificate abstains when audit samples are insufficient, and correlation artifacts from shared audit samples are controlled so stage dependence is not confused with sample adequacy. Anytime-valid sequential testing then decides gate-versus-gate or agent-versus-agent comparisons without invalid optional stopping.
