ranked.reported_results: Direct trajectory audit is 13.7% tighter than Bonferroni at adequate audit-sample size (and worse when under-sized) while the modular certificate averages +0.6%; removing the correlation artifact drops measured stage correlation from about 1 to 0-0.78 (arxiv:2608.05199); certified anytime-valid stopping makes agent comparison 74x cheaper than fixed-budget protocols (arxiv:2608.06362).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Calibrate each registered gate evaluator's error rate on labelled historical run outcomes and attach a composed (spanning-tree) risk bound to the publish decision, blocking promotion above the declared budget. Measurement: empirical mis-coverage of the certificates on held-out runs.

glm.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - conformal risk composition
glm.rationale: Conformal composition across gates is statistically elegant but needs labelled per-gate outcomes mini-ork does not accumulate yet.

minimax.landing_surface: publish gate / promotion gate - conformal and anytime-valid risk certification composed across pipeline gates
minimax.rationale: A distribution-free risk bound over the pipeline's gates is philosophically the right end-state for a multi-gate system, and it composes with the shipped level vector. It is watch because two papers support it, the certification machinery is L effort, and the snapshot's near-term need is a first security check, not a calibrated risk bound over a suite.

ranked.technique: Spec-to-FSM adversarial protocol analysis under a full-compliance adversary
ranked.mechanism: Extract a verified state machine from a protocol's natural-language specification and enumerate reachable state sequences under a full-compliance adversary - one that violates no rule - exposing design flaws (identity loss across hops, cross-client context injection, credential harvesting) that per-implementation testing cannot see because each implementation is individually conformant. Findings are reachable bad states evidenced by the state sequence, then mapped to implementation points for confirmation. Anchored on the formalized specification itself; for mini-ork the node-agent protocol and the artifact lifecycle (declared, produced, gated, published) are the specs to formalize and check.
ranked.reported_results: An LLM-extracted verified FSM (37 states, 76 transitions from 929 formalized statements) checked under a full-compliance adversary finds 11 new A2A protocol vulnerabilities including cross-client context injection and multi-hop credential harvesting (arxiv:2609.10871); sender identity alone proved unreliable for inter-agent trust, with claim binding mitigating misdirected coordination (arxiv:2608.06830).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Formalize the artifact-contract lifecycle (declared to produced to gated to published) as an FSM extracted from docs/architecture/artifact-graph.md and model-check reachable states under a rule-compliant adversary - an agent that violates no declared port or visibility limit. Measure counterexample state sequences found; each is a design finding to triage by hand.

glm.rationale: Spec-to-FSM analysis of the node-agent protocol is an interesting one-time audit; the 11 A2A findings are about a different, richer protocol.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - formalize the declared/produced/gated/published lifecycle as an FSM
minimax.rationale: An LLM-extracted verified FSM (37 states, 76 transitions) checked under a full-compliance adversary found 11 new protocol vulnerabilities including cross-client context injection and multi-hop credential harvesting, and mini-ork's artifact lifecycle is the natural spec to formalize. It is watch because it is a design-time activity with two papers of support and no bearing on either named hole.

ranked.technique: Watermark and provenance attribution of agent output (caution: provably evadable)
ranked.mechanism: Attributes machine-produced output to its originating run or owner: session-keyed behavioral watermarks embedded in action choices, two-channel trajectory watermarks pairing a structurally rewrite-invariant tally with executed-record binding that an attacker cannot forge without breaking execution, and dual robust-plus-fragile watermarks read out as a three-state provenance / tamper / spoof verdict; detection probes that survive paraphrase measure how a candidate text responds to matched semantic conditions rather than lexical cues. Accept-attribution = watermark verifies on both channels; reject = fragile channel broken, indicating tampering; abstain = no watermark present, which proves nothing either way. Caution (strong): a black-box score-ratio-alignment attack provably evades the major statistical watermark families with query access only, and a non-compliant provider can reshape a model so watermark-based data-use auditing fails while trained capability is retained — so watermark evidence is corroborating, never load-bearing.
ranked.reported_results: A two-channel trajectory watermark attributes reliably at low false-positive rate under full read/write log tampering, where each single-signal scheme has a fatal attack axis (arxiv:2607.08400); a black-box score-ratio-alignment attack provably evades the KGW, GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS, and SynthID1 watermark families (arxiv:2610.27653); a reshaped model defeats watermark-based data-use auditing while retaining trained capability (arxiv:2611.09446).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Bind every published artifact to its run id, a transcript hash, and a rewrite-invariant tally of tool-call counts, checked at promotion when a run's ownership is disputed. Measurement: a disputed-artifact trial attributes correctly even after log rewrites; given the proven evasions, treat this as watch-level corroborating evidence only.

glm.rationale: Watermark attribution is provably evadable by score-ratio alignment, and mini-ork's ledger already attributes deterministically by run id.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - run id, transcript hash and a rewrite-invariant tool-call tally
minimax.rationale: A black-box score-ratio-alignment attack provably evades the KGW, GumbelSoft, DipMark, ITS and SynthID1 families, and a reshaped model defeats watermark-based data-use auditing while retaining capability, so the evidence base explicitly says watermark evidence is corroborating and never load-bearing. That matches the doctrine's rule against a security claim resting on an unmeasured property, but it is a provenance nicety rather than a hole-closer, so it is skipped.

ranked.technique: Inference-time security steering and model editing — out of orchestrator reach; evaluate lanes jointly (caution)
ranked.mechanism: Task-vector arithmetic, activation steering, confidence-gated co-decoding, and weight editing cut insecure generation at the model level, but they require weights or decoding control that an orchestrator calling hosted lanes does not have; the reachable levers are lane selection and prompt-syntax discipline. The cautions matter more than the mechanism here: inference-time methods that win security metrics often do so by over-actuation — degraded functional output — rather than safer code, and model confidence is not a usable security signal at repository level (False Trust). Prompt syntax itself shifts the vulnerability rate of generated code, making prompt templates a security-relevant configuration surface. Any claimed security win for a lane must therefore be measured jointly on functionality and security; a single-axis gain is presumed functionality loss until disproven.
ranked.reported_results: Inference-time methods win secure@passk chiefly through over-actuation rather than safer code, and security tuning does not improve recognition of secure-code problems (arxiv:2606.25195); security-confidence gating improves calibration on controlled benchmarks but deteriorates at repository level, with calibration-guided repair yielding limited gains plus functional regressions (arxiv:2606.31159); task-vector steering adds +2.1 to +36.0 points of trustworthy completions at under 0.6% latency cost (arxiv:2607.07881); per-vulnerability steering vectors cut insecure generation by up to 74% (arxiv:2604.16697); model editing raises security rate +12.8 to +28.4 points while Pass@1 also improves (arxiv:2608.06848); confidence-gated co-decoding adds up to +12.6% Func-Sec@10 (arxiv:2607.28529); double steering cuts vulnerability rate 26.9% while raising functional correctness 7.5% (arxiv:2608.30025).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Add a lane-evaluation rule to provider and lane adoption: a security-tuned lane enters agents.yaml/providers.yaml only if it wins a paired functional-plus-security benchmark jointly, not on the security axis alone. Measurement: joint functional-security score per candidate lane on a fixed evaluation set, with over-actuation (functional drop) reported alongside.

glm.rationale: The technique's own portability caveat is decisive: mini-ork calls hosted lanes and has no decoding or weight control; keep the caution that security-metric wins via over-actuation, which the gate side (G05-T01) already covers.

minimax.landing_surface: lane config - inference-time security steering and model editing
minimax.rationale: The technique's own caution is decisive: the white-box variants require weight or serving-stack access that mini-ork does not have over its glm and minimax API lanes, and the portable slice (paraphrase consensus and judgment-versus-evidence re-verification) is already covered by techniques inside mini-ork's reach. It is a lane-configuration concern rather than a hole-closer, so it is skipped.

ranked.technique: Normalcy-baselined, provenance-grounded investigation
ranked.mechanism: Ground investigation in what this specific deployment normally does: build a normal-behavior baseline (per network, per repo) and queue evidence by relation-role rarity against that baseline, distill large provenance graphs with an information-bottleneck selection that bounds structural distortion while preserving causal reachability, and carry validated attack state across evidence fragments behind a confidence gate so a narrative accumulates instead of restarting per fragment. Segmentation and provenance context are first-class detection signals, not preprocessing. Accept rule: a suspected attack stage is promoted into the tracked narrative only above a confidence gate; below it, it stays a hypothesis. The anchor is the deployment's own baseline, which ablations show is the primary contributor to narrative quality.
ranked.reported_results: F1 of 95.7/90.9/88.9 on DARPA E3 engagement datasets with ~39% less training time, 33% lower latency, and 22% less memory than KAIROS (arxiv:2608.19750); ablations attribute attack-narrative quality primarily to deployment-specific normalcy baselines (arxiv:2609.36494); cross-modal provenance fusion detects all 32 attack events at 1.40% false-positive rate, F1 0.913 (arxiv:2607.05989); segmentation context lifts detection F1 from 0.90 to 0.95 (arxiv:2608.02627).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Accumulate a per-repo baseline of the run artifact graph (which node types write and read which ports across the last N clean runs) and, after each run, queue any edge that never appears in the baseline for confidence-gated review. Measure by seeding cross-artifact contamination into test DAGs - the contaminated edge must appear in the rarity queue - while clean runs keep the queue bounded.

glm.rationale: Normalcy-baselined provenance investigation needs SIEM-scale telemetry mini-ork does not generate.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - a per-repo baseline of the run artifact graph with rarity-queued edges
minimax.rationale: Deployment-specific normalcy baselines are the primary contributor to narrative quality in the ablations, and an edge that never appears in the baseline is a genuine novelty signal for a run DAG. It is watch because the baseline must be built from many clean runs before it means anything, and a small recipe has few.

ranked.technique: Gateway honeypot and shadow routing for hostile requests
ranked.mechanism: Place a fast classifier at the serving/gateway layer that scores every incoming request and transparently redirects flagged-hostile traffic to a honeypot or shadow backend - a decoy model, or a device-faithful mirror twin of the real plant - so production is shielded, the attack continues harmlessly, and the interaction is read for intelligence. Complexity-based routing sends each request to the cheapest tier that can hold the deception (lightweight emulation vs cloud model) with shared session state, and trapped-session fingerprints re-link adversaries who rotate identity. Route rule: the decision is made per request in milliseconds and errs toward the honeypot; the anchor is observed request behavior, not identity claims.
ranked.reported_results: Router P=.903, R=.918, F1=.911, AUROC 0.975, FPR@95TPR=0 at 38 ms median latency - 385x faster than a guard-LLM cascade at 96% of its F1 - with 0% evasion under 13 adversarial transformations and identity re-linking at 56.7% top-1 / 80.7% top-5 across 30 campaigns (arxiv:2609.08306); complexity routing cuts cloud-processed tokens 72.6% at 3.7x lower operational cost under 5% runtime overhead (arxiv:2610.27722); an 84-day backend-free LLM-API honeypot recorded 290,887 interactions from 2,793 unique sources (arxiv:2609.29757).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Wrap external tool servers behind a dispatch-level router: a cheap classifier over tool-call arguments flags hostile or scope-violating calls and transparently routes them to a decoy tool server that logs the interaction, so production tools never see them. Measure by replaying recorded benign traces (zero misroutes required) plus a scripted adversarial probe set (flag rate and evasion under rephrasing).

glm.rationale: Gateway shadow routing defends a serving tier mini-ork operates on the client side of.

minimax.landing_surface: MCP / tool surface - a dispatch-level router that transparently redirects hostile calls to a decoy tool server
minimax.rationale: The router is fast and accurate (F1 0.911 at 38 ms median, 385x faster than a guard-LLM cascade, 0% evasion under 13 adversarial transformations), but it presumes an adversary attacking a serving endpoint, which is not mini-ork's threat model - the threat here is untrusted content reaching mini-ork's own nodes. It is skipped in favor of the boundary controls that fit the actual attack path.

ranked.technique: Integrity-verified and private vector retrieval for memory packs
ranked.mechanism: When vector memory or retrieval results are outsourced or shipped as signed packs, verify that returned vectors correspond to the text they claim: a signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text, and a verifier that recomputes vectors and accepts within a cosine tolerance concedes a predictable share of queries to an attacker controlling the vectors (the margin law). Mechanisms: vector-commitment distance verification with aggregated inner-product arguments and topology-aware authenticated structures for outsourced ANN search, quantisation-code verification binding text to vectors where tolerance checks provably fail, and homomorphic sketching for private search on untrusted infrastructure. Accept rule: a retrieved result is trusted only if its commitment/quantisation proof verifies, otherwise the retrieval abstains. Watch-tier for mini-ork: it matters the day semantic memory is served from a shared or remote store rather than a local index.
ranked.reported_results: Margin-law hijack lowered correct answers from 0.75 to 0.39 on a Raspberry Pi 5 local RAG deployment while an empirically calibrated tolerance left 98-100% of queries exposed; tampered vectors passing a product-quantisation audit put the attacker's document first for 25% of targets; quantisation-code verification accepted every honest vector across three platforms (arxiv:2611.06498); authenticated ANN via vector commitments achieved up to 6.6x end-to-end latency speedup and 99.2% data-transfer reduction vs prior authenticated schemes (arxiv:2611.16516); homomorphic sketching reached Recall@100 0.9715 on BIGANN SIFT1B and 0.9845 at 100M vectors with 3.735 s query latency on a single GPU (arxiv:2611.10622).
ranked.miniork_surface: real sibling: the semantic memory index (mini_ork/memory/semantic.py) and any future shared or remote vector store behind it
ranked.adoption_sketch: If or when semantic memory ships signed memory packs or a shared index, bind quantisation codes at write time and verify at read time, abstaining on mismatch. Measure on a tampered copy of a memory pack: retrieval must reject tampered vectors that a cosine-tolerance check would accept (per the margin law, a tolerant check leaves most queries exposed).

glm.rationale: Integrity-verified vector retrieval matters when memory packs are shared or remote; mini-ork's index is local and run-scoped today.

minimax.landing_surface: mini_ork/memory/semantic.py - bind quantisation codes at write time and verify at read time, abstaining on mismatch
minimax.rationale: The margin law is a real result - a cosine-tolerance check leaves 98-100% of queries exposed and tampered vectors passing a quantisation audit put the attacker's document first for 25% of targets - but the technique says so itself: it matters the day semantic memory is served from a shared or remote store, and mini-ork's index is local. It is watch, not next.

ranked.technique: Design-time misuse-case and attack-tree derivation at intake
ranked.mechanism: Before implementation, misuse cases and attack trees are derived from the requirement and architecture and converted into numbered, mechanically checkable acceptance criteria — catching design-level omissions such as an unguarded sibling route that post-hoc scanning structurally misses. The derivation is anchored on requirement and architecture text, and its output feeds the verifier set as expectations rather than being trusted as findings. Evidence is weak — evaluation is a reference-labeled threat-modeling example and synthetic requirement-architecture pairs with injected weaknesses — so this is watch-tier: derived attack trees inform checks, and the gate abstains rather than blocks on them alone.
ranked.adoption_sketch: For security-relevant task classes, have the kickoff derive misuse cases into numbered Done-When criteria that the verifier set can check mechanically. Measurement: how many derived criteria are later exercised by verifier findings on a pilot batch — the derivation earns adoption only if its criteria catch what generic checks miss.

glm.landing_surface: mini_ork/verify/kickoff_guard.py - misuse cases into Done-When criteria
glm.rationale: Design-time attack-tree derivation is evaluated only on synthetic requirement-architecture pairs; the kickoff guard's numbered Done-When criteria already play the checkable-criteria role.

ranked.technique: Cross-layer attack-path reconstruction
ranked.mechanism: When an incident spans stack layers, reconstruct how a manipulation propagated into harmful action: static analysis extracts a call graph of components across layers, LLM reasoning abstracts each component's semantic flows into one unified representation, and graph analysis recovers the attack path from entry manipulation to harmful action. This moves the question from 'was this input malicious' to 'which components participated in turning it into an effect'. The output is a traceable path naming every participating node; the anchor is the call graph plus observed data flow, and the accept bar is node-level accuracy against known incidents.
ranked.reported_results: 85.3% node-level and 66.7% path-level F1 on 12 real-world incident cases (arxiv:2603.04469).
ranked.adoption_sketch: When a run is flagged, rebuild the propagation path across the run's artifact graph: static extraction of node-to-port edges from the artifact contract plus per-node semantic summaries from the ledger, then graph analysis from the suspect artifact to every node that consumed it. Measure by seeding a poisoned artifact into a test DAG and requiring reconstruction to recover the full consumption path where the raw transcript is too large to read by hand.

glm.rationale: Cross-layer attack-path reconstruction needs multi-layer incidents; mini-ork's layers (dispatch, worktree, gates) are already traced by the ledger.

minimax.landing_surface: evidence ledger and traces - rebuild the propagation path across the run artifact graph
minimax.rationale: Recovering which nodes consumed a suspect artifact, rather than cancelling the source or rolling everything back, is the right containment shape and matches the artifact contract's declared edges. It is watch because the evidence is one paper at 85.3% node-level and 66.7% path-level F1 on 12 incident cases, and it is a diagnostic rather than a detector.

ranked.technique: Poisoning-resilient positive-security policy learning with pre-enforcement validation
ranked.mechanism: Learn what legitimate traffic looks like (a positive-security allowlist) from live traffic without letting malicious requests that contaminate the training stream become policy: candidate signals pass poisoning-resilient validation, a deterministic synthesizer compiles survivors into enforceable rules, each rule carries a confidence score, and every policy is validated against held-out legitimate behavior before it is allowed to block anything. The deterministic synthesizer matches the LLM's blocking power without model inference cost. Accept rule: a policy enforces only after validation, and low-confidence rules wait for human approval - never silently enforce an unvalidated allowlist, and never fail open because the allowlist is incomplete.
ranked.reported_results: Poisoning resilience improved from 53% to 90% versus 62% for the Kruegel-Vigna baseline; the deterministic synthesizer provides attack blocking comparable to the tested language model without model inference cost (arxiv:2609.06840).
ranked.adoption_sketch: Derive each node type's declared port set in the artifact contract from observed legitimate runs rather than hand-authoring alone, validating the synthesized ports against holdout clean runs before enforcement and parking low-confidence ports for operator approval. Measure with a poisoning probe: contaminate the observation set with a run that exfiltrates through an undeclared port and require the validated policy to still reject it.

glm.rationale: Policy learning from traffic is SecOps-shaped; no mini-ork surface learns blocking policies from observed requests.

minimax.landing_surface: artifact contract - derive declared port sets from observed legitimate runs
minimax.rationale: Learning ports from observed traffic rather than hand-authoring them, with poisoning-resilient validation, is elegant but assumes a large corpus of observed runs to learn from, and mini-ork's recipes number in the low tens with declared ports already hand-specified. It is skipped as an insufficient return for the machinery.
